items.title: GPN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Genius Growth, Margins Rise
items.summary: Global Payments reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.58, beating estimates by 0.3%, with adjusted net revenues rising 31% year-over-year to $3.18 billion. The company expanded operating margins by 220 basis points to 42.5% and raised its synergy target to $650 million. GPN reaffirmed full-year guidance and expects over $2 billion in shareholder returns for 2026. Peers Visa, Mastercard, and Marsh & McLennan also reported strong quarterly results.

items.title: Sempra's Q3 Earnings Outpace Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Sempra Energy reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.40, beating estimates by 16.7% with a 26.1% year-over-year increase. The company raised its full-year 2026 GAAP EPS guidance to $7.41-$8.41 and maintained long-term EPS growth targets of 7-9%. Strong performance was driven by higher Oncor equity earnings and improved infrastructure results, though revenues slightly missed expectations.

items.title: 4 Healthcare ETFs to Tap Into Eli Lilly's Post-Q3 Earnings Rally
items.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) jumped 10.1% following better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and raised 2026 sales guidance. The company's blockbuster drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound generated over $16 billion in combined revenues with $6 billion year-over-year growth. However, LLY trades at a premium P/E ratio of 30.91, prompting investors to consider healthcare ETFs with significant LLY weightings as a balanced alternative for exposure.

items.title: ZTS Q3 Earnings Top Estimates, 2026 Profit Outlook Improves, Stock Up
items.summary: Zoetis reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.75, beating consensus of $1.51, with total revenues of $2.4 billion slightly exceeding expectations. However, U.S. companion animal sales declined 8% due to price sensitivity and competition. The company narrowed 2026 revenue guidance while raising adjusted earnings outlook. Stock rose 7.5% on results but remains down 27.5% year-to-date.

items.title: Host Hotels' Q3 FFO Beat Estimates on Strong RevPAR Growth
items.summary: Host Hotels & Resorts (HST) beat Q3 FFO estimates with 11.4% year-over-year growth to 39 cents per share, driven by strong transient demand and higher room rates. The company raised its 2026 adjusted FFO guidance to $2.21 per share and RevPAR growth outlook to 6.75%, citing resilient leisure demand and improving business travel. HST also expanded its portfolio with acquisitions of luxury properties in New York and Dallas.

items.title: TRMB Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates as AECO Growth Lifts Revenues
items.summary: Trimble (TRMB) reported Q3 2026 non-GAAP earnings of 86 cents per share, matching consensus estimates, with revenues of $966.8 million up 7.3% year-over-year. The company's AECO segment showed strong momentum with 9% organic revenue growth and record ARR of $1.636 billion, prompting management to raise full-year AECO operating margin guidance to 36%. However, Field Systems faced recurring revenue pressure with slower ARR growth, and Transportation & Logistics growth moderated amid freight weakness. Trimble lowered full-year organic ARR growth guidance to 10% from 12-14% but slightly raised earnings outlook.

items.title: Is GNRC Worth Buying as Data Center Growth Tests Margins and Risk?
items.summary: Generac Holdings (GNRC) benefits from a $4.5B data center backlog and recovering residential demand, with potential C&I revenue doubling in 2027. However, the company faces margin compression as data center sales (lower profitability) grow faster than residential, with Q4 gross margins expected to fall to 37-38%. Valuation is attractive on forward earnings (14.6X) but less compelling on EV/EBITDA and price-to-cash-flow metrics. Production ramp execution and supply constraints remain key risks.

items.title: Eversource Energy Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates, Revenues Decline Y/Y
items.summary: Eversource Energy missed Q3 earnings expectations with non-GAAP EPS of 92 cents versus consensus of 97 cents, driven by weaker electric and gas distribution results, higher interest expenses, and regulatory challenges. Despite the miss, the company raised 2026 EPS guidance to $4.62-$4.70 and maintained its $26.5B capital investment plan through 2030.

items.summary: Fair Isaac (FICO) reported Q4 FY2026 non-GAAP earnings of $11.10 per share, up 43.4% YoY and beating consensus estimates. Revenues grew 27.4% to $657.05 million, driven by higher mortgage origination score pricing and strong software platform growth. Software ARR reached $851 million with platform ARR up 72%. However, management withheld FY2027 guidance citing uncertainty around mortgage pricing transitions and continued weakness in mortgage market activity due to elevated interest rates.

The company raised its fiscal 2027 product revenue outlook to $6.07 billion (36% YoY growth) driven by strong AI adoption, expanding customer base of 14,554 customers (up 32% YoY), and innovative AI products like CoCo and CoWork. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/S ratio of 13.44X versus the industry average of 3.8X. Zacks rates SNOW as a Buy (Rank #2).

items.title: GNRC Drops 15.3% in the Past Month. Is the Selloff a Buying Chance?
items.summary: Generac Holdings (GNRC) shares declined 15.3% over the past month despite Q3 sales rising 16% and adjusted earnings jumping 38.8%. While the company's data center backlog reached $4.5 billion with 2027 revenues expected to exceed $2 billion, investors remain cautious due to Q3 revenue missing expectations, margin pressure from lower-margin data center sales, and manufacturing execution risks. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with strong momentum but faces headwinds from gross margin compression expected in Q4.

items.title: GNRC's Amazon Deal Adds $2.4 Billion in Data Center Revenue Visibility
items.summary: Generac Holdings secured a major long-term Amazon supply agreement for backup power generators targeting $2.4 billion in deliveries during 2027-2028. The deal significantly strengthens revenue visibility with the company's data center backlog reaching $4.5 billion. However, execution risks remain as Generac must ramp production capacity, secure engines, and manage margin pressures amid rapid scaling.

items.title: McDonald's Q3 Earnings Beat, but U.S. Traffic Still Pressures Growth
items.summary: McDonald's reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.57, beating consensus by 6.3%, driven by strong franchised margins and other operating income. However, revenue missed expectations at $7.16B, revealing weak U.S. comparable sales (-0.2%) offset by international strength, particularly in Japan, Germany, and Australia. The company plans 2,500 gross restaurant openings in 2026, but softer U.S. traffic and inflation pressures temper near-term growth prospects.

items.title: PepsiCo Lowers 2026 EPS Outlook as North America Pressures Margins
items.summary: PepsiCo reduced its 2026 core EPS growth guidance to 2.5-3.5% from 5-7%, citing persistent North American margin pressures. Foods North America's operating margin fell 280 basis points while Beverages North America declined 15 basis points. International operations provided offset with 8% organic revenue growth and 105 basis points of margin expansion. The company is pursuing productivity initiatives and structural cost reductions to support earnings recovery.

items.title: PepsiCo Jumps 15.1% in a Month as Investors Weigh What Comes Next
items.summary: PepsiCo shares surged 15.1% in one month, but weaker earnings expectations and North American margin pressures raise concerns about sustainability. While international operations show strong momentum with 8% organic revenue growth, North America faces headwinds with declining volumes and margin compression. The company lowered its 2026 core earnings growth outlook to 1-2%, and despite trading at a valuation discount, execution risk remains high.

items.title: Verisk Analytics Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Jump 5% Y/Y
items.summary: Verisk Analytics (VRSK) beat Q3 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of $1.96 (vs. $1.92 estimate) and revenues of $809M, driven by 8.2% subscription revenue growth and strong performance in underwriting and claims segments. However, free cash flow declined 40.5% to $200M, and net income fell 2.8% year-over-year. The company reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $3.19-$3.24B but lowered adjusted EPS guidance midpoint to $7.60 from consensus of $7.71.

items.title: Amcor September 2026-End Earnings Miss on Higher Costs, View Cut
items.summary: Amcor (AMCR) reported adjusted EPS of 95 cents, missing consensus estimates by 1.04% and declining 2.1% year-over-year due to higher energy, distribution, and interest costs. While revenues rose 6.7% to $6.13B driven by raw-material cost pass-through and volume growth, gross margins contracted to 18.9% from 19.6%. The company lowered transition-period EPS guidance to $1.70-$1.80 but reaffirmed double-digit EPS growth for 2027.

items.title: How Kraft Heinz Is Reshaping Its Portfolio for Long-Term Growth
items.summary: Kraft Heinz has agreed to sell its North America coffee business, including brands like Maxwell House and Gevalia, to One Rock Capital Partners for $650 million while retaining a 30% equity stake. The company expects approximately $500 million in after-tax proceeds to be used for debt repayment. The transaction is expected to close in mid-2027 and is anticipated to be growth and margin accretive while strengthening Kraft Heinz's financial flexibility.

items.title: EMCOR Raises 2026 Outlook as Record RPOs Strengthen Growth Visibility
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $9.60, up 46.1% YoY and beating consensus by 15.3%, with revenues climbing 28.8% to $5.54 billion. The company raised its 2026 guidance to $34.50-$35.50 EPS and $20.6-$21 billion revenue, driven by record remaining performance obligations of $18.57 billion, with data-center work more than doubling YoY and now representing 47% of the backlog.

items.title: Is EMCOR Stock a Buy Now as Growth Strength Offsets Valuation Risk?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported 22.9% revenue growth to $15.32 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with management raising full-year guidance. The company generated strong operating cash flow of $1.09 billion and maintains a Zacks Rank #1 rating. The company achieved a record $18.57 billion backlog, up 47.2%, with data-center obligations more than doubling. However, execution risks including labor availability, fixed-price contract exposure, and heavy data-center concentration (47% of backlog) pose challenges to margin sustainability.

items.title: Roper Technologies Rewards Shareholders With 10% Dividend Hike
items.summary: Roper Technologies (ROP) announced a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.00 per share, bringing the annual payout to $4.00. The company will pay the dividend on January 19, 2027, to shareholders of record as of January 4. ROP has raised its dividend for 34 consecutive years with a five-year dividend CAGR of 10.1%, supported by strong operating cash flow of $1.88 billion in the first nine months of 2026.

items.title: GE HealthCare Unveils Allia Celeo to Advance Interventional Imaging
items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies introduced Allia Celeo, a ceiling-mounted image-guided system for cardiology and interventional radiology procedures. The system features AI-powered imaging, flexible controls, and predictive maintenance capabilities. GEHC stock gained 12.1% following the announcement. The system is CE-marked but awaits FDA 510(k) clearance. The global angiography equipment market is projected to grow at 4.1% CAGR through 2033.

items.title: Aflac Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong U.S. Profit Growth
items.summary: Aflac reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.43, beating estimates by 35% despite a 2.4% YoY decline. U.S. pretax earnings surged 31.5% driven by higher premiums and reserve gains, while Japan's pretax earnings fell 21%. The company returned $1.1B to shareholders and raised its Japan segment profit margin guidance to 35-38%.

items.title: Datadog Q3 Earnings & Revenues Surpass Estimates, Both Rise Y/Y
items.summary: Datadog (DDOG) delivered robust Q3 2026 results with non-GAAP EPS surging 47.3% to 81 cents and revenues rising 35.2% to $1.2 billion, both beating consensus estimates. The company expanded its AI customer base to over 850 and achieved accelerating non-AI revenue growth for the fifth consecutive quarter. However, Q4 guidance of $1.19-$1.20 billion represents a slowdown to 25-26% growth, with the largest customer reducing usage creating near-term headwinds.

items.title: RL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Asia Sales, Margins Rise
items.summary: Ralph Lauren reported Q2 fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $4.64, up 22.4% YoY and beating estimates by 8.7%, with revenues growing 9.1% to $2.19B. Asia revenues surged 28.2% led by China's 35%+ growth, while global comparable store sales increased 10%. The company raised its FY27 revenue growth outlook to 6-7% and projects 80-100 basis points of margin expansion.

Operating margins reached post-pandemic highs at 66% flow-through, supported by rental rate growth and disciplined expense management.

items.title: Greg Abel's 2 Big Acquisitions This Year Cost Berkshire Hathaway About $16 Billion, Less Than 5% of Its Cash Pile
items.summary: Since taking over as CEO, Greg Abel has completed two major acquisitions for Berkshire Hathaway: OxyChem for $9.7 billion and Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion, totaling $16.5 billion or just 4.5% of the company's $365.5 billion cash pile. These deals suggest Abel is maintaining acquisition discipline while potentially pursuing more synergistic deals than Warren Buffett, signaling a slow pivot in strategy that may help prevent Berkshire from stagnating.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark Q3 Earnings Beat on Lower Interest Costs, Sales Miss
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.70, beating consensus estimates, but net sales declined 0.4% to $4.13 billion, missing expectations. Adjusted operating profit fell 0.9%, while gross margins contracted 130 basis points. KMB completed its Kenvue acquisition and reaffirmed its 2026 standalone earnings outlook, though the stock has underperformed the industry significantly.

However, the company lowered its 2026 revenue guidance to $1.35 billion from $1.4 billion due to deteriorating consumer credit conditions and higher funding costs. The company's secured lending business turned profitable with a 17% contribution margin, and management plans to launch Upstart Bank in early 2027 with $404.1 million in capital.

items.title: SMCI Q1 Earnings Beat on Large AI Deployments, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) reported exceptional Q1 fiscal 2027 results with EPS surging 417.1% to $1.81 and revenues jumping 297.5% year-over-year to $19.95 billion, driven by large AI data center projects accounting for 71% of sales. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $72-$82 billion. However, customer concentration remains elevated with one customer representing 44% of quarterly revenues, and the company faces constraints from component shortages and power availability.

items.title: MPC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Refining Strength and Asset Sales
items.summary: Marathon Petroleum Corporation (MPC) delivered strong third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted earnings of $26.93 per share exceeding estimates by 4.60% and revenues of $56.487 billion surpassing consensus by 68.30%. The company achieved 100% refinery utilization with 3.2 million barrels per day throughput, supported by elevated refining margins. MPC announced a $4.2 billion divestiture of St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries to CVR Energy, with proceeds to be reinvested in Gulf Coast operations. The company returned $3.284 billion to shareholders and increased its quarterly dividend by 10%, while maintaining a constructive refining outlook through mid-2027.

items.title: AIZ Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Lifestyle and Housing Strength
items.summary: Assurant (AIZ) reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $6.15 per share, significantly beating consensus estimates of $4.57. Revenue grew 9.2% to $3.55 billion, driven by strong performance in Global Lifestyle and Global Housing segments. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately 10% growth and expects low-double-digit adjusted earnings per share growth. Other multi-line insurers showed mixed results, with Everest Group missing estimates while Prudential Financial beat expectations.

items.title: SHOP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Commerce and Margin Discipline
items.summary: Shopify reported Q3 2026 earnings beating consensus estimates with $3.74B in revenue and $0.49 EPS. The company highlighted AI-driven commerce growth with AI-referred traffic up 2.6X and orders up 3.3X. Q4 revenue is expected to grow in the low 30s percentage range. Free cash flow reached $816M at a 22% margin, with payments penetration exceeding 68%. Sidekick AI assistant usage surged while costs declined 18%, and the company expanded into offline retail, B2B, and international markets.

items.title: ZBRA Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Strong Demand and Raised Outlook
items.summary: Zebra Technologies (ZBRA) raised its 2026 sales growth outlook to 17% following strong third-quarter earnings, with Q3 EPS of $4.95 beating estimates and sales of $1.61B exceeding expectations. The company reported broad-based demand across retail, transportation, logistics, manufacturing, and healthcare sectors, with Connected Frontline posting 15% organic growth. However, rising memory costs pressured gross margins, declining 220 basis points to 46%. Management expects 2027 growth to approach the upper end of its long-term 5-7% range, supported by a multiyear transportation and logistics device refresh pipeline.

items.title: XYZ Q3 Earnings Call Highlights 2027 Outlook and AI Expansion
items.summary: Block, Inc. (XYZ) exceeded Q3 2026 earnings and revenue estimates with adjusted EPS up 109% and gross profit rising 22%. The company raised its 2026 outlook and provided 2027 targets, projecting 15% gross profit growth and 30% adjusted operating income growth with a 32% margin. Square's GPV grew 14%, Cash App lending surged 40%, and Block expects initial AI revenues in Q4 2026.

items.title: WMB Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Power Backlog and Funding
items.summary: The Williams Companies reported Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $2.039B (up 6%), maintaining 2026 guidance of $8.3B-$8.5B. Management expects one or two more power deals by year-end with longer contracts and phased expansions. Year-end leverage projected near 3.75X with ~$2B financial capacity remaining under its 4X ceiling. The company emphasized execution on pipelines, storage, and power projects while managing expansion and balance sheet growth.

items.title: ServiceNow Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Outlook Risks
items.summary: ServiceNow lifted its 2026 AI ACV target to $1.7B as AI contract value surged 65% year-over-year, with AI deals exceeding $1M growing 4.5x. The company raised 2026 subscription revenue guidance to $15.785B and increased free cash flow margin targets. However, slower-than-expected Q4 cRPO growth of 18.5% and bundled deployment services impacting subscription revenue recognition raised investor concerns about future acceleration.

items.title: GOOGL Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Spending Pressures
items.summary: Alphabet reported Q3 earnings of $2.12 per share, missing consensus estimates of $2.94, with revenues of $111.21 billion below the $111.8 billion estimate. Google Cloud revenues surged 103% to $30.7 billion driven by enterprise AI demand, while the company reaffirmed $195-205 billion in 2026 capex guidance. Q3 capital expenditures of $51.4 billion resulted in negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion, reflecting heavy infrastructure investments and TPU inventory accumulation.

items.title: GEHC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Margin Risks
items.summary: GE HealthCare Technologies (GEHC) raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $4.95-$5.05 and expects ~4% organic revenue growth, driven by strong Q3 performance and productivity improvements. The company's diagnostics segment grew 13.8% while Patient Care Solutions grew 8.8%. However, tariff exposure and fourth-quarter comparisons pose risks to near-term growth.

items.title: FTNT Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Services Outlook and AI Demand
items.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.125-$8.215 billion and billings guidance to $9.568-$9.718 billion, driven by strong enterprise demand, AI security initiatives, and large deployments. However, the company faces headwinds from delayed service revenue recognition, component cost pressures, and questions about sustainability of hardware demand in 2027.

items.title: FORM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Capacity Expansion and AI Demand
items.summary: FormFactor (FORM) announced plans to expand manufacturing capacity at its Farmers Branch facility to $400M in annual probe card revenue by end-2027. The company raised its 2026 TRITON photonics system revenue outlook to over $30M, reported strong Q3 results with 10% sequential growth in Foundry and Logic revenues, and expects sustained margin improvements around 53% baseline. Systems revenues hit a record $59.5M with 23% sequential growth.

items.title: FANG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Capital Discipline and Permian Growth
items.summary: Diamondback Energy (FANG) reported strong Q3 2026 earnings, beating consensus estimates with adjusted EPS of $5.86 and revenues of $5.43 billion. The company raised its 2026 oil production guidance to 524,000 barrels per day while maintaining capital discipline with a ~30% reinvestment rate. Management highlighted Barnett formation development with target well costs of $850-$900 per lateral foot, explored enhanced oil recovery technology, and secured pipeline access for natural gas opportunities. The company generated $2.15 billion in adjusted free cash flow during the quarter.

items.title: CAT Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Record Backlog and Capacity Push
items.summary: Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) reported a record $78 billion backlog, up 96% year-over-year, driven by strong demand in power generation (data centers, AI infrastructure), construction, and mining. The company maintains mid-to-high-teens 2026 revenue growth outlook and plans to triple large engine capacity by 2030. However, management acknowledged $2.2 billion in projected tariff costs and manufacturing capacity constraints. Q3 adjusted earnings of $7.2 per share and revenues of $20.68 billion both exceeded consensus estimates.

items.title: BKNG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Travel Slowdown and AI Push
items.summary: Booking Holdings (BKNG) reported Q3 earnings with AI-powered services showing strong conversion improvements, but management issued a cautious Q4 outlook citing moderating international travel demand and Middle East disruptions. The company expects Q4 room night growth of 1-3% and adjusted revenue growth of 0-2%, while maintaining 2026 full-year guidance for high-single-digit growth. BKNG is investing heavily in AI initiatives, loyalty programs through Connected Trips, and targeting $650M in annual savings by 2027.

items.title: Arista Networks Q3 Earnings Call Maps Out 2027 AI Expansion
items.summary: Arista Networks raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13.3B (48% growth) with Q3 revenues reaching $3.66B, beating estimates. The company projects 2027 revenues of $18.5B with AI fabrics doubling to $7B and cognitive campus reaching $2B. Management addressed supply constraints through $11.4B in purchase commitments and emphasized enterprise adoption across healthcare, hospitality, and web services sectors.

items.title: AMGN Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Pipeline and Raised Outlook
items.summary: Amgen reported strong Q3 earnings with adjusted EPS of $6.45 beating estimates and raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $38.9B-$39.7B and EPS outlook to $22.90-$23.70. The company highlighted growth from key medicines like IMDELLTRA, MariTide, and TEZSPIRE, though biosimilar competition pressured mature products like Prolia and XGEVA. Management emphasized late-stage clinical progress and manufacturing readiness as foundations for future growth.

items.title: SMCI Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and Margin Pressures
items.summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $72B-$82B, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure demand and stronger customer commitments. The company reported record Q1 revenues of $19.95B and adjusted EPS of $1.81, exceeding consensus estimates. However, SMCI faces margin pressures from large AI deployments, component shortages, and significant customer concentration, with one customer representing 44% of revenues.

items.title: NVTS Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Infrastructure Growth
items.summary: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) reported Q3 2026 earnings and revenue beats with 38% year-over-year sales growth to $14 million. The company expects AI infrastructure to contribute over 40% of Q4 revenues and potentially triple in 2027, with double-digit sequential revenue growth possible throughout the year. Management highlighted a book-to-bill ratio of 2, backlog extending into mid-2027, and multiple 800-volt power conversion opportunities. The Claros acquisition expands the company's integrated voltage regulation capabilities for AI processors.

items.title: FLEX Q2 Earnings Call Highlights Axiom Spin-Off and AI Growth
items.summary: Flex Ltd. reported strong Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings, beating consensus estimates with adjusted EPS of $1.18 and revenues of $8.49 billion. The company raised full-year guidance to $34.9-$35.9 billion in revenue and $4.84-$5.16 in adjusted EPS, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure demand and the planned spin-off of its Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) business as Axiom. CPI revenues surged 54% year-over-year to $2.5 billion with expanding margins, while management projects 75-85% CPI growth in fiscal 2027.

items.title: AMD Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and 2027 Growth Outlook
items.summary: AMD raised its 2027 growth expectations to over 80%, with data centers expected to contribute more than 80% of revenues. Q3 data center revenues surged 97% to $8.5B, driven by record EPYC processor and Instinct accelerator sales. However, the company faces supply constraints amid rising AI orders and expects double-digit PC market declines in 2027.

items.title: ADM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Biofuels Strength and 2027 Outlook
items.summary: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (ADM) raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.50-$5.80 for the third time this year, driven by strong North American biofuels margins and improved operational execution. The company's Ag Services and Oilseeds segment saw profit surge 105% to $778M on stronger soybean crushing and biodiesel margins. ADM also increased its 45Z incentive benefit forecast to $350M and reduced planned 2026 capital spending to $1.2-$1.3B, while maintaining a constructive but measured outlook for 2027.

items.title: BSX Q3 Results Reset Growth Expectations as 2027 Outlook Stays Weak
items.summary: Boston Scientific reported Q3 organic sales growth of 1.5%, missing its 3%-5% guidance due to an August cybersecurity disruption that impacted manufacturing and shipments. The company cut its full-year 2026 organic sales growth forecast to 3.75% from 5%-6% and reduced adjusted EPS guidance to $3.16-$3.18. Management expects 2027 to be the cycle's trough, with recovery anticipated in 2028 driven by new product launches. The company faces ongoing competitive pressure in electrophysiology and WATCHMAN sales weakness.

items.title: Pfizer: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Pfizer raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $62-64 billion, driven by strong performance from launched and acquired products with 32% operational revenue growth in Q3. The company is implementing $7.2 billion in cost-saving initiatives to offset upcoming patent expirations on key drugs. Management projects high single-digit revenue growth from 2028-2033, contingent on successfully converting late-stage oncology and obesity treatment trials into commercial revenue.

items.title: Diamondback Q3 Earnings Beat on Higher Oil Prices and Production
items.summary: Diamondback Energy (FANG) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.86, beating estimates by 19.1%, with revenues surging 38.4% year-over-year to $5.43 billion. The company generated $2.15 billion in free cash flow, raised its 2026 production guidance, increased its dividend by 7.3%, and repurchased $251 million in shares. Higher oil prices and 9.7% production growth drove strong results.

items.title: Cerebras Systems vs. Innodata: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: The article compares two AI infrastructure companies: Cerebras Systems, a hardware manufacturer with 91% revenue growth but $512M net losses and negative cash flow, versus Innodata, a data engineering specialist with 39% revenue growth, $47M net income, and $184M free cash flow. The author recommends Innodata for 2027 due to profitability, cheaper valuation metrics, and expected 22% annualized earnings growth, while suggesting waiting on Cerebras until it demonstrates sustainable cash flow.

items.summary: Seagate Technology (STX) delivered robust Q1 fiscal 2027 results with revenues surging 61% to $4.2B and non-GAAP EPS jumping 194% to $7.68, driven by strong data center demand and record capacity shipments. The company projects Q2 revenues of $4.8B with continued growth expected from HAMR technology adoption and favorable pricing. Competitors Western Digital and NetApp also reported strong performance in AI-driven storage demand.

items.title: MOS Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Higher Costs, Lower Volumes
items.summary: The Mosaic Company (MOS) reported a Q3 2026 net loss of 23 cents per share, wider than consensus estimates, as net sales declined 10.2% year-over-year to $3.1 billion. Lower sales volumes across all segments and higher raw material costs pressured results, though the company beat revenue expectations. MOS expects continued cost pressures in Q4 2026 and revised full-year potash production guidance downward to 8.6 million tons due to lower ore grades.

items.title: Andy Jassy Just Delivered Magnificent News for Amazon Investors
items.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) reported record $45.9 billion in Q3 revenue with 39% year-over-year growth, marking six consecutive quarters of accelerating growth. CEO Andy Jassy forecasted AWS could grow revenue by over 40% in 2027-2028 and become a trillion-dollar revenue business within 5-10 years, driven by expanding AI services and custom chip adoption. Despite a 15% stock correction, Amazon trades at a P/E of 19.4, significantly below the Nasdaq-100's 29.9, presenting a potential buying opportunity.

items.title: Bloom Energy's New Guidance Implies Up to $1.55 Billion in Q4 Revenue. Can It Deliver?
items.summary: Bloom Energy raised its Q4 revenue guidance to $1.35-$1.55 billion, driven by surging demand from AI data centers needing rapid power solutions. The company is expanding manufacturing capacity toward a 5+ GW annual goal and management believes it won't be a bottleneck for hardware assembly, positioning it to capitalize on the power grid interconnection bottleneck.

items.title: Broadcom vs. Taiwan Semiconductor: Two AI Powerhouses, but One Offers a Better Value for 2027
items.summary: Both Broadcom and Taiwan Semiconductor are major beneficiaries of the AI boom, but Taiwan Semiconductor offers better value for 2027 investors. While Broadcom generated $63.9B in revenue with strong AI chip growth, Taiwan Semiconductor delivered superior financial performance with $122.4B in revenue, 45.1% profit margins, and lower valuation multiples (24.2x forward P/E vs. 27.9x for Broadcom). Taiwan Semiconductor's stronger growth, higher margins, and more attractive valuation make it the more compelling investment despite geopolitical risks.

items.title: Amazon vs. Target: One Is Riding the AI Boom, While the Other Faces a Consumer Spending Squeeze
items.summary: Amazon and Target show diverging growth trajectories. Amazon maintains double-digit revenue growth fueled by e-commerce, AWS cloud computing (up 39%), advertising, and AI infrastructure demand, reaching $201.9B in Q3 2026 revenue. Target struggles with weaker discretionary consumer spending, showing modest 5.3% sales growth and flat revenue trends, though recent stabilization and digital growth offer some encouragement. Amazon's diversified business model positions it as a more attractive investment than Target's uncertain retail turnaround.

items.title: Coca-Cola vs. PepsiCo: Pepsi's Revenue Dwarfs Coke's, but This Is the Number to Watch
items.summary: While PepsiCo's revenue nearly doubles Coca-Cola's, Coca-Cola's steadier quarterly growth and superior operating margins (33.4% vs 16.9%) signal stronger pricing power and a more efficient business model. Recent account losses to Coca-Cola, including KFC's $500M switch and Marriott's beverage provider change, have pressured PepsiCo's outlook, while Coca-Cola stock has surged 40% in 2026.

items.title: Nokia vs. AT&T: Comparing Cyclical Sales Patterns vs. Steady Revenue
items.summary: AT&T generates roughly five times more revenue than Nokia with consistent quarter-over-quarter performance, while Nokia exhibits cyclical patterns with sharp Q4 spikes reflecting IT budget spending cycles. items.title: Why Intel Stock Collapsed 23.4% Last Month
items.summary: Intel stock fell 23.4% in October due to weak PC market demand and concerns about its foundry business. While the company's AI and data center segment grew 78%, the traditional PC business declined 5%. The foundry business, despite 58% revenue growth, is losing over $1 billion per quarter and underperforming expectations compared to competitors. With a P/S ratio of 5.3 and facing headwinds, the stock appears overvalued for current growth prospects.

items.title: Seagate's $1.2 Billion Debt Paydown: What Comes Next for Investors?
items.summary: Seagate Technology (STX) has significantly improved its financial position by retiring $1.95B in debt across fiscal Q1 2027 and post-quarter, reducing net leverage to 0.2x and principal debt to $1.6B. The company generated $1.5B in free cash flow, returned $568M to shareholders with a 3% dividend increase, and plans to accelerate buybacks in 2027 with $4.4B authorization remaining. Management expects fiscal Q2 revenues of $4.8B (+/-$100M), representing 70% year-over-year growth, supported by strong cloud storage demand and HAMR technology adoption.

The company faces significant profitability pressure with adjusted operating margins contracting 580 basis points to 31.2%, driven by weakness in Merchant Solutions revenues (down 3%) and higher transformation costs. Despite challenges, Fiserv reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $7.20-$7.40 and doubled its Project Elevate cost-savings target to $1 billion.

items.summary: Clorox (CLX) delivered impressive Q1 fiscal 2027 results with adjusted EPS surging 82% year-over-year to $1.55 and net sales jumping 33% to $1.91B, both beating consensus estimates. The company maintained full-year earnings guidance of $5.70-$6.00 per share but lowered gross margin expectations to 41.5%, with management expecting results near the lower end of guidance.

items.summary: Alphabet's stock fell 17.5% despite strong Q3 earnings (25% revenue growth, $127.6B total revenue) due to investor concerns about Google Search losing market share to AI competitors like ChatGPT and Claude. The company maintained full-year guidance but faces pressure as costs rise while sales stall, requiring a strong fourth quarter to meet targets.

The company falsely represented its China operations as limited to R&D and technical support, when in reality its core platform, software development, and 62% of its global workforce were China-based. A split may occur if the stock price sustains above $1,000 per share.

Management believes these investments will generate sustained free cash flow and strong returns on invested capital.

items.title: Edison International: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Edison International reaffirmed its 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.90-$6.20 on its Q3 earnings call. The company faces challenges from delayed California wildfire liability reform, which threatens to increase financing costs and force SCE to curb clean energy investments during its 2029 rate case. However, SCE has hardened 90% of its distribution network in high fire areas and plans $38-41 billion in capital spending through 2030 without issuing common stock, targeting 5-7% annual earnings growth.

items.summary: Johnson & Johnson took a $7 billion charge in Q3 2026 due to talc litigation settlement ($5.5 billion) and strategic investments in acquisitions and partnerships. Despite a 96% decline in GAAP earnings per share, the company raised its full-year guidance and reported nearly 6% revenue growth, demonstrating the resilience of its core business and reinforcing its status as a Dividend King with 64 consecutive years of dividend increases.

items.summary: Robbins LLP announced class action lawsuits against Everest Group, Ltd. for allegedly misleading investors about its U.S. casualty insurance business risks and reserve adequacy. The lawsuit covers purchases between February 2024 and October 2025, with Everest's stock declining significantly after disclosures of $478 million in unfavorable reserve development and a $1.2 billion protection agreement. Additional class actions were filed against O-I Glass, Inc. for misrepresenting financial outlook and Tenax Therapeutics, Inc. for misleading claims about its drug candidate levosimendan.

items.title: J.B. Hunt Investor News: If You Have Suffered Losses in J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc., You Are Encouraged to Contact The Rosen Law Firm About Your Rights
items.summary: The Rosen Law Firm is investigating potential securities claims against J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc. following allegations of materially misleading business information. The investigation was prompted by J.B. Hunt's September 16, 2026 announcement that third-quarter earnings would fall due to increased costs for recruiting, advertising, onboarding, training, and sign-on bonuses (approximately $25 million more than Q2), causing the stock to plunge 10% intraday. The firm is preparing a class action lawsuit to recover investor losses.

items.title: BULL Shareholders Have Rights – If You Lost Money Investing in Webull Corporation Contact Robbins LLP Information About Leading the Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Webull Corporation (NASDAQ: BULL) for allegedly misrepresenting itself as a U.S.-based company while concealing its structural dependence on Chinese operations and personnel. A U.S. House Select Committee found a 'profound gap' between Webull's claims of American independence and its actual China-tied ownership, workforce, and infrastructure. The stock fell 19% on October 7, 2026, following the committee's findings. Investors who purchased shares between April 26, 2025 and October 6, 2026 may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit.

items.title: DUOL Shareholders Have Rights – If You Lost Money in Duolingo, Inc. Contact Robbins LLP for Information About Leading the Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. for allegedly misleading investors about product quality and sustainability. The company concealed negative impacts from aggressive monetization strategies involving excessive ads and lower-quality AI-generated content. Stock prices fell significantly following three disclosure events between November 2025 and February 2026, with DAU growth decelerating from 49% to 20% and the CFO resigning. Investors who purchased DUOL stock during the class period (May 2, 2025 - February 26, 2026) may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 7, 2026.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 30: Amazon Misses Revenue and Earnings Expectations
items.summary: Amazon stock fell 1.41% after missing Q3 revenue and earnings expectations, with concerns over heavy AI capital expenditures ($220B planned for 2026) and negative free cash flow of $42.4B over the trailing 12 months. However, AWS grew 39% year-over-year, and the company's $114B in liquidity provides a cushion. The broader market declined with S&P 500 down 2.07% and Nasdaq down 2.86%, while retail competitors Walmart and Costco gained.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 30: Intel Plunges Nearly 29% as Weak Outlook Rattles Wall Street
items.summary: Intel shares plummeted 28.58% on Friday despite beating Q3 earnings expectations, driven by disappointing Q4 guidance citing weakening PC demand and manufacturing constraints. The sell-off rippled through the semiconductor sector, with AMD and Nvidia also declining. However, Intel's Data Center and AI division showed strength with 78% year-over-year revenue growth, suggesting challenges are concentrated in PC markets rather than data center demand.

items.title: Lululemon (LULU) Dips More Than Broader Market: What You Should Know
items.summary: Lululemon (LULU) closed down 2.35% and received a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating. The company faces significant headwinds with expected EPS down 62.55% and revenue down 10.02% in the upcoming quarter, along with full-year earnings projected to decline 27.98%. Despite trading at a discount to its industry's Forward P/E ratio, the stock's weak growth prospects and negative estimate revisions have prompted the bearish outlook.

items.title: Compared to Estimates, LyondellBasell (LYB) Q3 Earnings: A Look at Key Metrics
items.summary: LyondellBasell reported Q3 2026 revenue of $8.5 billion, up 10% year-over-year, slightly beating the consensus estimate of $8.47 billion. However, EPS of $2.54 missed expectations of $2.73, representing a -6.96% surprise. The company showed mixed segment performance, with strong results in Intermediates & Derivatives and Olefins & Polyolefins Americas, but weakness in European and Asian operations. The stock has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Amazon (AMZN) Stock After Q3 Earnings: Buy the Dip, Sell, or Hold?
items.summary: Amazon missed Q3 earnings and revenue expectations, with EPS of $1.89 vs. consensus of $2.01 and revenue of $201.94B vs. expected $202.11B. However, the company achieved record 13.9% operating margins. AWS revenue surged 39% YoY to $46B, driven by AI infrastructure demand, but heavy $220B capital expenditure for 2026 pushed free cash flow negative by $33.5B in Q3. Amazon projects Q4 revenue growth of 12-16% for the holiday season and maintains a Hold rating at historically attractive 24X forward earnings valuation.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Alerts Duolingo, Inc. (NASDAQ: DUOL) Investors to a Securities Class Action Lawsuit – Contact the Firm Before Deadline on December 7, 2026 for Leadership Role
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a class action lawsuit against Duolingo on behalf of investors who purchased stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The complaint alleges that Duolingo made false and misleading statements about the negative impact of increased ad volume, subscription upsells, and AI-generated content on daily active user growth. The stock experienced significant drops following disappointing financial results and the CFO's departure.

items.title: OKTA vs. S: Which Enterprise Cybersecurity Stock Has an Edge Now?
items.summary: Okta and SentinelOne are both cybersecurity companies benefiting from enterprise security modernization and AI adoption. Okta specializes in identity and access management with a 28% operating margin, 107% net retention rate, and new products contributing 30% of bookings. SentinelOne focuses on autonomous threat detection with 21% revenue growth and AI security ARR tripling, but lower profitability. Okta appears better positioned due to its stronger financial profile, larger customer base of 20,000+, and superior cash generation, despite SentinelOne's faster revenue growth.

items.title: SYK Stock Skids as Q3 Earnings and Sales Miss & 2026 Outlook Cut
items.summary: Stryker Corporation reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.52 and sales of $6.52B, both missing consensus estimates. The company cited weak hip and knee procedures, cybersecurity disruptions, and SAP implementation challenges as headwinds. Stryker cut its 2026 organic sales growth outlook to 6.5-7.0% from 8.3-9.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $14.80-$14.90, causing shares to fall 11.8% after hours.

items.title: REGN Q3 Earnings Beat on Dupixent Profits & Eylea HD Growth, Stock Up
items.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $20.07, surging 70% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates. Revenues jumped 36% to $5.12 billion, driven by strong Dupixent profits, robust Eylea HD sales growth, and momentum in Libtayo. The company raised R&D guidance and secured a $1 billion upfront payment from an expanded Sanofi collaboration, though legacy Eylea sales declined due to competitive pressure.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Encourages Investors of Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) Who Suffered Losses to Contact the Firm Before December 15, 2026
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a class action lawsuit against Bank of America on behalf of investors who purchased stock between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026. The lawsuit follows the U.S. Department of Treasury's announcement of over $1.2 billion in penalties and settlements against Bank of America's subsidiary for violations of Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering laws, including failure to detect and report over $5 billion in suspicious activity. The regulatory charges reduced Bank of America's Q3 2026 diluted earnings per share by $0.17, and the stock fell 4.8% on October 14, 2026.

items.title: ADBE vs. PEGA: Which Enterprise Software Stock Has an Edge?
items.summary: Adobe (ADBE) outperforms Pegasystems (PEGA) with stronger revenue growth, higher AI monetization ($650M+ AI-first ARR), and a more diversified product portfolio. While PEGA offers exposure to enterprise workflow automation with growing cloud adoption, it faces slower ACV growth (7%), prolonged sales cycles, and operational challenges. ADBE trades at a lower valuation (P/E 9.05X vs. 14.73X) and carries a Hold rating, while PEGA is rated Strong Sell.

items.title: MPWR Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and Capacity Expansion
items.summary: Monolithic Power Systems (MPWR) raised its 2026 enterprise data revenue growth floor to 150% from 130%, driven by strong AI and server power management demand. Q3 earnings of $8.19 per share beat consensus estimates, with revenues of $1.20 billion exceeding expectations. The company plans to expand capacity to $8 billion by H2 2027 and $10 billion beyond, while communications revenues surged 134.7% and automotive grew 19.2%. Management projects Q4 revenues between $1.315-$1.385 billion.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, the company made false or misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: Adobe vs. Axon Enterprise: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Adobe and Axon Enterprise present a classic value-versus-growth investment choice. Adobe offers stable 10.5% revenue growth, strong 30% net margins, and $9.9B free cash flow at a reasonable 10.1x forward P/E valuation, but faces leadership transitions and AI disruption risks. Axon Enterprise demonstrates aggressive 33.5% revenue growth in public safety technology but suffers compressed profitability (4.5% net margin) and trades at a steep 49.8x forward P/E. The article recommends Adobe as the better buy based on valuation and cash generation despite Axon's superior growth prospects.

items.title: Onsemi to Report Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: ON Semiconductor is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on November 2, with revenues projected at $1.71B and EPS at 88 cents, representing 10% revenue growth and 40% EPS growth year-over-year. The company is expected to benefit from strong AI data center demand, SiC adoption, and automotive recovery, though rising manufacturing costs and supply constraints pose headwinds. ON has a positive Earnings ESP of +5.68% and Zacks Rank #3, suggesting a likely earnings beat.

items.title: KLA (KLAC) Q1 Earnings: How Key Metrics Compare to Wall Street Estimates
items.summary: KLA reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $4.14 billion, up 28.9% year-over-year, beating consensus estimates by 2.2%. EPS of $1.22 exceeded expectations by 3.39%. Key metrics showed strong performance in wafer inspection (+37.4% YoY) and patterning (+29.1% YoY), though Taiwan revenues missed estimates. The stock has declined 16.4% over the past month but maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: Federal Realty's Q3 FFO Beat Estimates on Rental Growth & Strong Leasing
items.summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust (FRT) reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $1.87 per share, beating estimates by 1.1%, with revenues up 5.2% to $339 million. Rental income grew 5.3% year-over-year, and the company achieved strong leasing spreads with 14% cash rent growth. FRT raised its 2026 FFO guidance to $7.54-$7.58 per share, implying over 7% growth. The company also acquired The Summit retail center in Birmingham, AL for $508 million.

items.title: EXC Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Utility Rates, Sales Up Y/Y
items.summary: Exelon Corporation (EXC) reported Q3 2026 adjusted operating earnings of 87 cents per share, beating consensus estimates by 8.75%, with revenues rising 9.2% to $7.32 billion. The company narrowed its 2026 EPS guidance to $2.85-$2.91 and reaffirmed 5-7% annualized earnings growth through 2029, supported by a $41.7 billion capital investment plan and 7.9% rate-base growth. However, operating income declined 8.1% due to higher operating expenses, and results were mixed across its utility subsidiaries.

items.title: Is TMUS Worth Buying as Growth Strength Clashes With High Debt Risks?
items.summary: T-Mobile reported strong Q3 2026 results with service revenues up 6.2% and core adjusted EBITDA growing 10.8%, supported by broadband expansion and improved cash generation. However, rising debt ($77.32B), increasing customer churn (1.09%), and intensifying competition from AT&T and Verizon temper the growth outlook. The company maintains a Hold rating despite favorable valuation metrics.

items.title: Coinbase: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Coinbase reported that prediction markets reached $200 million in annualized run rate revenue within eight months of launch, diversifying revenue away from volatile spot crypto trading which declined 10% quarter-over-quarter. The company is positioning itself for the 'agentic economy' through AI infrastructure and tokenized equities, leveraging deep market liquidity and regulatory compliance as competitive advantages.

items.title: CBOE Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Options Volumes
items.summary: Cboe Global Markets reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.63 per share, beating estimates by 5.8%, with net revenues rising 18% to $712.2 million. Options revenues jumped 23% driven by record SPX 0DTE trading activity. The company raised its 2026 organic revenue growth outlook to the high teens and lowered expense forecasts. Peer exchanges CME Group, Nasdaq, and Intercontinental Exchange also reported strong Q3 results with double-digit revenue growth.

items.title: Intel: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Intel reported Q3 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion driven by strong Data Center and AI division growth. Management projects server CPU market could expand fivefold to $200 billion over five years due to AI infrastructure demand. However, near-term headwinds persist as PC unit volumes are expected to decline 12% in 2026 due to memory shortages and limited IT budgets. Manufacturing yield improvements have reduced production costs, with Intel 18A costs declining 40% since Q1.

items.title: GDDY Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Revenue Growth and Airo Gains
items.summary: GoDaddy (GDDY) delivered robust Q3 2026 results with earnings per share jumping 37.7% to $2.08 and revenues rising 6% to $1.34 billion, both beating consensus estimates. The company's AI product Airo showed exceptional momentum with annualized bookings surpassing $100 million, more than doubling from the prior quarter. GoDaddy raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to the higher end of its range and reaffirmed profitability targets, supported by strong operational leverage and continued AI-driven growth.

items.title: Weyerhaeuser Q3 Earnings & Sales Top, Adjusted EBITDA Rises Y/Y
items.summary: Weyerhaeuser (WY) exceeded Q3 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of 8 cents (up 33.3% YoY) and sales of $1.86 billion (up 8.4% YoY), driven by strong Timberlands performance. However, Wood Products segment margins contracted significantly, and the company issued cautious Q4 guidance citing weaker results expected in Wood Products and Strategic Land Solutions. Related construction stocks Masco, Comfort Systems USA, and United Rentals also reported strong Q3 results with raised guidance.

items.title: Lost Money on The Cooper Companies, Inc. Stock? Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Continues Investigating Possible Securities Fraud After 14.67% Share Price Drop
items.summary: Law firm Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is investigating potential securities fraud at The Cooper Companies following a 14.67% stock price drop on September 10, 2026. The decline occurred after the company reported flat year-over-year revenue of $717 million and reduced full-year guidance by approximately 1.4% due to U.S. channel inventory reductions. Investors who suffered losses may be eligible to pursue claims for recovery.

items.title: FDXF Four-Month Transition Period Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Yields
items.summary: FedEx Freight (FDXF) reported four-month transition period 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.49, beating consensus estimates of $1.38 by 8%, with revenues up 8.1% to $2.44 billion. The company raised its full transition-period EPS guidance to $2.80-$2.90 from $2.40-$2.60, driven by higher freight yields and fuel surcharges, though shipment volumes declined 0.7% year-over-year. Operating expenses increased significantly, but the company maintained strong liquidity with $1.6 billion available.

items.title: Alliant Energy Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates, Revenues Rise Y/Y
items.summary: Alliant Energy (LNT) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.52 per share, beating estimates by 23.58%, with revenues up 6.2% to $1.29 billion. The company narrowed its 2026 guidance and initiated 2027 guidance, while increasing its four-year capital expenditure plan by 19% to $15.9 billion. LNT secured 3.4 gigawatts of contracted data-center demand, expecting 60% peak demand growth by 2031.

items.title: ADM vs. INGR: Which Food Ingredients Stock Looks More Attractive?
items.summary: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is positioned as the stronger investment choice compared to Ingredion (INGR) in the agricultural processing and food ingredients sector. ADM demonstrated superior Q2 2026 performance with 7.2% revenue growth and 75% operating profit increase, while INGR saw only 1% sales growth with margin pressures. ADM's diversified operations, oilseed capacity expansion, and growing Nutrition business support sustained earnings growth, whereas INGR faces operational disruptions and cost inflation challenges. ADM trades at a forward P/E of 13.71X versus INGR's 8.35X, with upward earnings estimate revisions for ADM contrasting downward revisions for INGR.

items.title: Republic Services Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise 8.2%
items.summary: Republic Services (RSG) reported better-than-expected Q3 2026 results with adjusted earnings of $1.94 per share and revenues of $4.56 billion, driven by pricing strength and improved Environmental Solutions performance. The company raised its 2026 guidance for revenues, adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow, though adjusted EBITDA margins contracted 100 basis points. RSG maintained pricing discipline amid volume pressures and generated strong cash flow while returning capital to shareholders.

items.title: Are Smaller Home Projects Sustaining Home Depot's Sales Growth?
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q2'26 comparable sales growth of 1.7% driven by resilient demand for repair and maintenance projects, with digital sales climbing 11%. However, underlying demand remains uneven as transactions declined 1% while average ticket grew 2.8%, indicating consumers are spending more per visit but visiting less frequently. Management reaffirmed flat to 2% FY26 comps guidance. Lowe's and Williams-Sonoma are also benefiting from similar small-project spending trends, though with varying momentum.

items.title: VNT or P: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two Technology Services sector stocks reveals that Vontier Corporation (VNT) presents a superior value opportunity compared to Everpure (P). VNT holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook and a Value grade of A, supported by a forward P/E of 10.27 and P/B ratio of 4.21. Everpure carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Value grade of D, featuring a higher forward P/E of 49.19 and P/B ratio of 29.42.

items.title: MKSI or ROK: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a value investing comparison, MKS (MKSI) emerges as the superior choice over Rockwell Automation (ROK). MKSI holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook and a Value grade of B, featuring a forward P/E of 16.44 and PEG ratio of 0.45. ROK has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Value grade of D, a forward P/E of 30.26, and PEG ratio of 2.14, making it significantly more expensive on traditional valuation metrics.

items.title: Colgate Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Organic Sales & Pricing Gains
items.summary: Colgate-Palmolive (CL) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 97 cents per share, up 7% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates. Net sales grew 4.6% to $5.37 billion with 3.6% organic sales growth driven by balanced volume (1.7%) and pricing (2%) gains. The company raised its 2026 Base Business earnings growth guidance to 5-7% and expects gross margin expansion. Regional performance was mixed, with Latin America and Asia Pacific showing strong growth while North America declined.

items.title: VICR vs. SNPS: Which Stock Offers Better Growth Potential?
items.summary: Synopsys and Vicor are both benefiting from AI infrastructure expansion but serve different parts of the semiconductor ecosystem. Synopsys provides EDA software and semiconductor IP with 82% recurring revenue and a $10.9 billion backlog, while Vicor develops high-density power-conversion components with strong Advanced Products growth. Synopsys is rated as the more compelling investment due to diversified growth avenues and greater visibility, earning a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) versus Vicor's Rank #2 (Buy).

items.title: Mastercard Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Guidance & AI Commerce
items.summary: Mastercard exceeded Q3 2026 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of $5.31 versus consensus of $5.14, and revenues of $9.81 billion surpassing estimates. The company maintained its full-year revenue growth outlook at the high end of low-double-digit range. Value-added services grew 19% year-over-year, while cross-border volume increased 11%, though European activity softened. Mastercard is advancing AI commerce through Agent Pay technology and expanding stablecoin capabilities via its BVNK acquisition.

items.title: Amazon Q3 Revenues Miss Estimates, AWS Growth Hits Near 5-Year High
items.summary: Amazon reported Q3 2026 net sales of $201.9 billion (12% YoY growth) slightly missing estimates, but operating income surged 61% to $28.1 billion with record 13.9% margins. AWS revenues jumped 39.3% to $46 billion, marking fastest growth in nearly five years with a $578 billion backlog. The company expects Q4 sales of $240-$247 billion and projects AWS growth exceeding 40% in 2027-2028, though capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion in Q3 as Amazon invests heavily in AI infrastructure.

items.title: LHX Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Record Backlog and Revised Outlook
items.summary: L3Harris Technologies (LHX) exceeded Q3 earnings expectations with $3.28 EPS and $6.06B in revenues, driven by record $53.2B backlog and $19.3B in quarterly orders. The company raised 2026 guidance but reduced 2028 free cash flow target to $3B from $3.5B due to lower anticipated margins and accelerated $3B missile capacity investments. Management prioritizes backlog conversion and operational execution across defense markets.

items.title: First Solar's Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Decrease Y/Y
items.summary: First Solar reported Q3 2026 earnings of $5.30 per share, beating estimates by 14.2%, with gross profit up 16.8%. However, revenues fell 23% year-over-year to $1.23B, missing consensus. The company cut its 2026 sales guidance to $4.60-$4.90B and lowered module shipment forecasts to 16-17 GW, signaling weakening demand in the solar sector.

items.title: Starbucks Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Sales Leverage, Revenues Miss
items.summary: Starbucks reported mixed Q4 fiscal 2026 results with adjusted EPS of 80 cents beating estimates by 9.6%, but revenues of $9.14B missed consensus. North America comparable sales grew 7.9% driven by higher spending and transactions, while international revenues fell 36.9% due to the China business transition to a licensed model. For fiscal 2027, the company projects non-GAAP EPS of $3.15-$3.25 with approximately 1% revenue decline and plans to add 1,200 net new stores globally.

items.title: Ingersoll Rand Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates, Raises Revenue Guidance
items.summary: Ingersoll Rand (IR) delivered strong third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted earnings of $1.07 per share, beating estimates by 20.2%, and orders surging 20.7% to $2.35 billion. The company raised its 2026 revenue growth guidance to 5.5-7% and earnings guidance to $3.58-$3.70 per share, citing improved demand and healthy order momentum across its business segments.

items.title: TT Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Strong Demand & Margin Pressures
items.summary: Trane Technologies raised its 2026 organic revenue growth outlook to 11% and reported strong Q3 earnings, beating consensus estimates. However, the company cut operating leverage guidance to low-20% range due to supply-chain disruptions, inflation, and weaker pricing. A substantial $12.5B backlog with over $8B for 2027+ provides visibility, while the company pursues data center opportunities and strategic acquisitions.

items.title: GILD Beats Q3 Earnings on HIV Strength & Trodelvy Sales Growth
items.summary: Gilead Sciences beat Q3 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of $2.55 and revenues of $8.3 billion, driven by strong HIV drug sales (up 18% to $6.25 billion) led by Biktarvy, Descovy, and Yeztugo. Trodelvy oncology sales jumped 42% and Livdelzi grew 93%, prompting the company to raise 2026 product sales guidance to $31-$31.3 billion. However, Cell Therapy revenues declined 18% amid competitive pressures, and the company faces a $1.5 billion revenue headwind for Biktarvy in 2028 from Medicare pricing changes.

items.title: DexCom Stock Up on Q3 Earnings & Revenue Beat, Margins Rise
items.summary: DexCom (DXCM) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of 73 cents, beating estimates by 10.6%, with revenues growing 11.2% to $1.34B. U.S. revenues rose 13.8% while adjusted gross margin expanded 380 basis points to 65.1%. The company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $5.20-$5.25B and authorized an additional $1B share buyback. International growth moderated to 4.8% due to prior-year reimbursement comparisons, but management expects recovery in early 2027.

items.title: Clorox's Q1 Earnings Coming Up: Key Insights for Investors
items.summary: The Clorox Company (CLX) is set to report Q1 FY2027 results on Nov. 2, with consensus revenue expectations of $1.9 billion (31% YoY growth) and EPS of 97 cents (14.1% YoY growth). While product innovation, brand investments, and the GOJO/Purell acquisition are expected to support performance, the company faces headwinds from higher commodity and logistics costs, cautious consumer spending, and margin pressure. The Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat given CLX's +4.31% Earnings ESP combined with a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

items.title: DaVita Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on IKC Strength, Revenues Rise Y/Y
items.summary: DaVita (DVA) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.82, up 52.2% YoY, and revenues of $3.58 billion, up 4.6%, beating consensus estimates. Strong performance in Integrated Kidney Care and international operations drove results, though higher patient care costs and sequential RPT decline pressured margins. The company narrowed 2026 EPS guidance to $14.30-$15.20 amid cost pressures.

items.title: MPWR Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates on Enterprise Data Strength
items.summary: Monolithic Power Systems (MPWR) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $8.19 per share, up 73.2% YoY, with revenues surging 63.1% to $1.20 billion, beating consensus estimates. Enterprise Data revenues jumped 164.6% driven by strong AI and server demand. The company raised its 2026 Enterprise Data revenue growth floor to 150% and projects Q4 revenues of $1.315-$1.385 billion, targeting $8 billion in annual capacity by H2 2027.

items.title: Bloom Energy Joined the S&P 500 at Nearly 400 Times Earnings. History Says This Is What Happens Next.
items.summary: Bloom Energy joined the S&P 500 on Sept. 21 with an extremely high valuation of nearly 400 times trailing earnings, which has since dropped to 120 times earnings as the stock declined 29%. Historical data shows that S&P 500 additions and high P/E ratio stocks typically underperform the market, though Bloom Energy's strong revenue growth (138% YoY) and positive earnings present a contrasting factor.

items.title: Pre-Markets Spooked on Questions Regarding AI, Oil Prices
items.summary: Markets opened lower on October 30, 2026, with the Nasdaq down 2.5% (-750 points) amid concerns about AI trade outlook in Q3 earnings. However, major oil companies and pharmaceutical firms posted strong earnings results, buoyed by elevated oil prices due to U.S.-Iran tensions and solid pharma performance. Employment costs came in line with expectations at +0.8%.

items.title: CHD Q3 Earnings Top Estimates, Organic Growth Fuels Margin Gains
items.summary: Church & Dwight (CHD) delivered strong Q3 2026 results with adjusted EPS rising 13.6% to 92 cents and sales growing 1% to $1.6 billion, both beating estimates. The company raised its full-year sales outlook and expects 5% organic sales growth and 7% adjusted earnings growth in 2026, driven by brand momentum across key products like ARM & HAMMER and THERABREATH. Gross margins expanded 170 basis points year-over-year, supported by higher volumes and productivity gains.

items.title: Dominion Energy's Q3 Earnings Top Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Dominion Energy (D) reported Q3 2026 operating earnings of $1.28 per share, up 20.8% year-over-year, beating consensus estimates. Revenues surged 24.1% to $5.62 billion. The company reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $3.45-$3.69 and maintained its 5-7% annual earnings growth target through 2030. Strong performance was driven by Virginia utility earnings of $862 million, favorable rates, and data center demand in Virginia reaching 54.9 GW.

items.title: AJG Q3 Earnings and Revenues Miss on Lower Interest Income
items.summary: Arthur J. Gallagher (AJG) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.00 per share, narrowly missing the consensus estimate of $3.01, though earnings grew 29.9% year-over-year. Revenues of $3.91 billion also fell short of expectations. The company achieved its 26th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted EBITDAC growth with 5% organic revenue growth and 200 basis points of margin expansion in the brokerage segment. Peer companies Willis Towers Watson and Aon beat estimates, while Brown & Brown missed.

items.title: DLR Q3 FFO & Revenues Beat Estimates on Rental Growth, '26 View Raised
items.summary: Digital Realty Trust reported strong Q3 2026 results with core FFO per share up 11.1% to $2.10, beating estimates by 6.6%, and revenues up 20.6% to $1.90 billion. The company set record bookings of $626.6 million at its share and raised 2026 guidance for both core FFO ($8.30-$8.35) and revenues ($7.05-$7.125 billion), driven by robust hyperscale demand and improving occupancy rates.

items.title: Edison International Q3 Earnings Outpace Estimates, Revenues Miss
items.summary: Edison International (EIX) reported Q3 2026 core EPS of $1.92, beating estimates by 4.9%, but revenues of $4.89 billion missed by 11.7%. Southern California Edison's earnings declined 17.9% year-over-year due to absence of prior-year GRC benefits. EIX reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $5.90-$6.20 EPS and maintained 5-7% annual earnings growth target through 2030.

items.title: RDDT Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Search Traffic Pressures
items.summary: Reddit reported Q3 earnings of $1.40 per share and revenues of $895 million, beating estimates. However, the company faces significant headwinds from declining Google search referrals, with CEO warning of potential low-double-digit sequential DAU declines in Q4. To counter this, Reddit plans to transition toward a logged-in platform experience and is investing in personalization and user retention. Despite traffic concerns, advertising revenues surged 54% year-over-year to $847 million, with Q4 guidance projecting 38-42% annual growth.

items.title: TEM vs. DOCS: Which Medical Info Systems Stock Is the Better Pick Now?
items.summary: Tempus AI (TEM) appears more favorable than Doximity (DOCS) in the medical information systems sector. TEM is expected to deliver 23.1% Q3 revenue growth driven by oncology testing and data licensing, while trading at a lower valuation (7.32X P/S vs 8.53X P/S). DOCS faces headwinds from cautious pharma spending and margin pressure, with only 1.3% expected revenue growth and a 24.4% EPS decline, despite strong physician engagement and AI adoption.

items.title: ASE Technology Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI-Driven LEAP Growth
items.summary: ASE Technology (ASX) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 37 cents per ADS, beating estimates by 8.8% with revenues surging 44.8% year-over-year to $7.64 billion. Strong AI-driven demand for Leading-edge Advanced Packaging (LEAP) services drove ATM revenues up 51% YoY. The company raised its 2026 LEAP revenue outlook above $4 billion and expects revenues to double in 2027, with gross margins expanding 500 basis points to 22.1%.

items.title: SYK Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Softer Demand and Revised Outlook
items.summary: Stryker Corporation (SYK) lowered its 2026 organic sales growth guidance to 6.5%-7% and adjusted EPS outlook to $14.80-$14.90 following weaker-than-expected Q3 results. The company faces headwinds from slower hip and knee procedures due to affordability pressures and insurance deductibles, peripheral vascular supply constraints, and commercial execution challenges. However, MedSurg and Neurotechnology segments showed strength with 9.1% organic growth, and the company announced a strategic investment in CMR Surgical for robotic platform expansion.

items.title: MO Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Guidance and Nicotine Strategy
items.summary: Altria Group (MO) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.52, beating consensus estimates, with revenues net of excise taxes growing 3.6% to $5.44B. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.66-$5.74, supported by strong cigarette pricing discipline and growth in its on! nicotine pouch portfolio. Altria returned over $6B to shareholders in the first nine months and increased its quarterly dividend by 4.7%.

items.title: LLY Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Obesity Drug Growth
items.summary: Eli Lilly reported strong Q3 2026 earnings, beating estimates with $7.48 EPS vs. $5.38 consensus and $24.40B revenue (+39% YoY). The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $91-92B from $85-87B, driven by robust demand for obesity and diabetes treatments Mounjaro and Zepbound, which combined for over $16B in sales. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Program has attracted 500,000+ prescriptions since July, with new oral treatment Foundayo generating $184M in Q3 sales. Despite pricing pressures and upcoming manufacturing investments, management remains confident in long-term growth opportunities across its cardiometabolic and broader pipeline.

items.title: LIN Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Restructuring and Growth Outlook
items.summary: Linde (LIN) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.59 (up 9% YoY) and revenues of $9.4B (up 9% YoY), beating consensus estimates. The company initiated a $425M restructuring charge targeting cost efficiency with full run-rate savings expected in H2 2027. Despite strong electronics growth (15%) and a $7.9B project backlog, management maintained a cautious near-term outlook citing uneven industrial demand, particularly weakness in Europe and China's domestic consumption. Lincare homecare operations remain a profitability headwind.

items.title: HSY Q3 Earnings Call Highlights 2027 Growth and Margin Risks
items.summary: The Hershey Company maintained its 2027 sales growth outlook of 2-4% despite facing headwinds from cautious consumers and cost pressures. Q3 organic sales rose 0.8% with pricing gains offsetting a 10-point volume decline. Management plans a 50% larger innovation pipeline for 2027 and targets margin recovery, though freight and input cost inflation remain obstacles.

items.title: GILD Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Pricing Risks
items.summary: Gilead Sciences raised its 2026 sales guidance to $31B-$31.3B with expected HIV revenue growth of ~12%, driven by strong performance in Biktarvy, Yeztugo, and Trodelvy. However, the company disclosed a $1.5B Biktarvy revenue headwind in 2028 due to Medicare price negotiations. Despite this, management expects overall HIV revenues and earnings to continue growing, while advancing its oncology and inflammation pipelines.

items.title: FSLR Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Pricing Shift and Outlook Cut
items.summary: First Solar reduced its 2026 sales guidance to $4.6B-$4.9B and module volume outlook to 16-17 GW due to weak demand and slower customer procurement decisions. Despite Section 232 tariffs strengthening the case for domestic manufacturing and enabling higher pricing on new contracts, the company is taking a selective approach to bookings. Management approved $500M in buybacks while maintaining a $1.5B-$2B net cash target, with CuRe technology rollout beginning in India in Q1 2027.

items.title: EME Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Data Center Demand and Higher Outlook
items.summary: EMCOR Group raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $20.6-$21B and adjusted EPS to $34.50-$35.50, driven by strong Q3 results and record remaining performance obligations. Data center RPOs more than doubled to $8.74B fueled by cloud and AI infrastructure demand. The company also reported improved operating margins and diversified growth across healthcare, water, and institutional projects.

items.title: EIX Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Urgency of Wildfire Reform
items.summary: Edison International (EIX) reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $5.90-$6.20 and 5%-7% annual core earnings growth through 2030, while emphasizing the urgent need for California wildfire liability reform. The company faces rising infrastructure financing costs potentially reaching $300 million due to elevated credit spreads, and is managing Eaton Fire liabilities with over $1.1 billion in settlement offers extended. EIX plans $38B-$41B in capital spending through 2030 while advancing grid hardening efforts.

items.title: AMZN Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AWS Growth and AI Spending
items.summary: Amazon outlined ambitious cloud growth expectations during its Q3 2026 earnings call, with AWS revenue growing 39.3% YoY to $46B and management projecting growth exceeding 40% in both 2027 and 2028. The company plans $220B in capital expenditures for 2026, primarily for AWS infrastructure, with higher spending expected in 2027. AWS backlog reached $578B and Bedrock token volume surged nearly 17-fold, reflecting accelerating AI adoption. However, the company missed earnings estimates and faces margin pressures from lower-margin AI services and rising infrastructure costs.

items.title: SIMO Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI and Enterprise Growth Outlook
items.summary: Silicon Motion Technology Corporation (SIMO) outlined ambitious growth plans during its Q3 2026 earnings call, projecting at least 40% revenue growth in 2027. The company expects Q4 revenues between $588-616 million with gross margins of 54-55%. Key growth drivers include enterprise storage (MonTitan controllers with seven customers ramping in 2026), automotive solutions (which grew 75% sequentially and represent 40% of Q3 sales), and AI infrastructure. Management acknowledged ongoing weakness in consumer markets but expects PCIe Gen 5 adoption to reach 20-25% PC market penetration by end of 2027.

items.title: ORLY Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Sales & Tariff Refunds
items.summary: O'Reilly Automotive (ORLY) beat Q3 earnings expectations with 97 cents per share and $5.12B in revenues, driven by 12.7% professional sales growth and $39M in tariff refunds. The company raised its 2026 EPS outlook to $3.25-$3.35 and plans to accelerate store openings to 265-275 in 2027. DIY sales grew 6.2% despite consumer pressure, while gross margins expanded to 52.4%.

items.title: Why ServiceNow Stock Plunged This Week
items.summary: ServiceNow stock fell 31% after the company guided for slower fourth-quarter current backlog growth, despite reporting 20.5% revenue growth and raising AI revenue targets. The stock's high P/E ratio of 79 leaves little room for error, and investors are advised to wait for the next earnings report for clarity on whether backlog growth stabilizes.

items.title: Intel Surpasses Q3 Earnings Estimates on Robust Data Center Demand
items.summary: Intel reported strong Q3 2026 results with earnings surging 126.1% to 52 cents per share and revenues rising 20.9% to $16.51 billion, driven by robust Data Center and AI demand.
