items.title: Buy These 5 Top-Ranked Stocks With Superior Financial Efficiency
items.summary: A stock screening based on four efficiency ratios (receivables turnover, asset utilization, inventory turnover, and operating margin) combined with a Zacks Rank #1 rating narrowed 7,906 stocks down to 16 candidates. Five stocks emerged as top performers: Healthcare Services Group, CarMax, Hasbro, FormFactor, and MaxLinear, all demonstrating efficiency levels exceeding industry averages and posting significant four-quarter earnings surprises ranging from 11.1% to 70.8%.

items.title: Quantum vs. NetApp: Which Data Storage Stock is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Quantum Corporation and NetApp are both benefiting from rising AI and cloud storage demand, but they present different investment profiles. Quantum posted 25.7% revenue growth with improving profitability and a strengthened balance sheet, but faces persistent supply-chain constraints. NetApp delivered stronger 30% revenue growth with expanding margins and raised guidance, though it grapples with rising component costs. NetApp holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) versus Quantum's Rank #3 (Hold), making NetApp the more compelling pick despite trading at a higher valuation.

items.title: Leidos Holdings to Release Q3 Earnings: Here's What to Expect
items.summary: Leidos Holdings (LDOS) is expected to report Q3 2026 results on November 3 with revenue estimated at $4.71 billion (5.3% growth) but earnings projected to decline 0.3%. The company's Homeland and Intelligence segments are expected to benefit from AI cloud services and new contracts, while the Health segment may face revenue pressure. The Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat due to a negative Earnings ESP of -0.12% despite a Rank #3 rating.

items.title: CVNA Q3 Earnings Miss on Higher Costs Despite Record Sales
items.summary: Carvana (CVNA) missed Q3 EPS estimates at 39 cents vs. 47 cents consensus but beat revenue expectations at $8.04B (+42.4% YoY). The company achieved record retail units of 217,385 and raised 2026 EBITDA guidance to the higher end of $2.7-$3B range. However, higher logistics costs and rising interest rates pressured unit economics, with gross profit per unit declining. The company strengthened its cash position to $3.05B and improved its debt-to-EBITDA ratio to 0.8x.

items.title: Just 15 Stocks Make Up 71% of the Dow. Here's My Top Pick to Buy Now.
items.summary: American Express is highlighted as a top buy among the 15 largest Dow components, which represent 71% of the index's weight. Despite a 15.3% year-to-date decline and recent Q3 earnings-driven sell-off, AXP offers compelling value at 17.6x adjusted 2026 earnings guidance. The company demonstrates strong fundamentals with double-digit revenue growth, excellent credit quality metrics, aggressive buybacks, and a diversified revenue model superior to competitors Visa and Mastercard.

items.title: SNDK Q1 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and Supply Discipline
items.summary: Sandisk (SNDK) reported Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings that beat estimates with revenues of $11.03 billion (up 378% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $49.51. Datacenter revenues surged 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion driven by AI infrastructure demand. The company secured long-term customer commitments covering 50% of fiscal 2027 bits and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 bits. Q2 guidance projects revenues of $12.2-$12.6 billion with continued growth expected from AI-driven storage demand.

items.title: RMD Stock Up on Q1 Earnings and Revenue Beat, Gross Margin Climbs
items.summary: ResMed (RMD) delivered solid first-quarter fiscal 2027 results with adjusted EPS of $2.91, up 14% year-over-year and beating consensus by 9%. Revenues grew 6% to $1.41 billion, driven by sustained demand for sleep devices and masks. Gross margins expanded 50 basis points to 62.5% from productivity gains. However, the company faced headwinds from discontinued Astral life-support device sales and the MatrixCare divestiture. RMD maintained its fiscal 2027 guidance for 5-7% core constant-currency revenue growth and $12.00-$12.25 adjusted EPS.

items.title: Top ETF Stories of October
items.summary: October saw mixed market performance with tech stocks declining due to concerns about AI spending returns and rising bond yields. Alphabet plunged 13% after missing search revenue estimates and reporting negative free cash flow from AI investments. Meta also slumped 10% despite beating earnings, as free cash flow turned negative and capex guidance increased. Cybersecurity stocks rallied as AI-driven threats increased. Strong U.S. GDP growth of 3.4% may benefit small-cap stocks going forward.

items.title: AMD vs. SpaceX: Here's The Stock I'd Buy Now
items.summary: The article compares AMD and SpaceX as AI investments, highlighting that while AMD is an AI infrastructure play, SpaceX has shifted to become primarily an AI application company through its Super Intelligence division. SpaceX's AI revenue grew 830% to $7.6B in Q2, surpassing AMD's data center division growth of 107% to $6.7B. The author recommends SpaceX as the better buy due to superior growth rates and the shift toward AI applications over infrastructure.

items.title: Joby Is Buying a Defense Company. Archer Plans to Buy 3 From Boeing. Here's Which Pivot Makes More Sense.
items.summary: Joby Aviation is acquiring defense specialist Resonant Sciences for $500 million while Archer Aviation is acquiring three Boeing subsidiaries (Wisk Aero, SkyGrid, and Insitu) for a 16.5% stake. Both companies are pivoting toward defense as their commercial eVTOL aircraft businesses remain unproven. Archer appears further behind in FAA certification and commercial viability, making its defense diversification more critical, though neither company has demonstrated strong organic revenue growth in their core eVTOL businesses.

items.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Cisco Systems, Digi International and Lantronix
items.summary: The Computer-Networking industry is positioned for growth driven by AI infrastructure investments, 5G deployment, and Wi-Fi 7 adoption. Cisco Systems, Digi International, and Lantronix are highlighted as key players benefiting from increased demand for networking solutions supporting AI workloads and edge computing. However, macroeconomic uncertainty, tariff concerns, and supply chain volatility pose near-term headwinds.

items.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Marriott International, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts and Choice Hotels International
items.summary: The Hotels and Motels industry faces headwinds from rising operating costs, economic uncertainty, and intense competition, but benefits from steady travel demand and recovery in business/group travel. Marriott International (Rank #2 Buy) shows strong growth prospects with 17.2% EPS growth expected. Wyndham Hotels & Resorts (Rank #2) benefits from its asset-light model with 6.6% EPS growth projected. Choice Hotels International (Rank #3 Hold) shows modest 0.6% bottom-line improvement. The industry ranks #166 out of 247 Zacks industries with dull near-term prospects despite outperforming the S&P 500 over the past year.

items.title: Lockheed Martin's Backlog Is Soaring: Time to Buy the Stock
items.summary: Lockheed Martin's order backlog surged to $292 billion in Q3 from $194 billion at year start, with improvements in both quantity and quality. The company is securing higher-margin contracts like the $58.6 billion PAC-3 missile defense system and establishing more favorable long-term agreements with the Department of Defense that include fixed-price escalators, upfront payments, and cancellation protections. These developments reduce execution risk and suggest improving profit margins, making the stock attractive at 22x earnings.

items.summary: While Anthropic's S-1 filing signals an exciting AI company entering the market, Nvidia emerges as the smarter investment choice. Anthropic's filing reveals massive long-term AI spending plans (5-10 years), confirming that Nvidia's GPUs will be essential infrastructure for the AI build-out. items.summary: TSMC maintains significantly higher revenue than Applied Materials, with Q3 2026 reaching $46.7 billion compared to AMAT's $9.1 billion in Q2 2026. items.title: Palantir Technologies vs. Figma: Comparing Revenue Growth Trends
items.summary: Palantir Technologies and Figma both demonstrated consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth over eight quarters, with Palantir's quarterly revenue nearly tripling Figma's. Palantir generated $1.9 billion in Q2 2026 revenue driven by government contracts and AI platform demand, while Figma achieved $370.1 million with a 48% year-over-year increase, bolstered by new AI credit monetization. Both companies show strong growth trajectories in their respective markets.

items.title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy Just Made a Wild Prediction. It Could Make the Tech Giant a Big Winner.
items.summary: Amazon stock fell 7% after earnings despite strong 12% revenue growth and 61% operating income growth, as investors worry about massive AI capital expenditures. CEO Andy Jassy predicted Amazon could become the first company to have two trillion-dollar revenue businesses within 5-10 years, with e-commerce and AWS each potentially reaching $1 trillion in annual revenue.

items.title: GOOGL Shareholders Have Rights – If You Lost Money Investing in Alphabet Inc. Contact Robbins LLP for Information About Recovering Your Losses
items.summary: Shareholder law firm Robbins LLP announced a class action lawsuit against Alphabet Inc. for allegedly failing to disclose that its Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model was experiencing disappointing training results and would face significant launch delays. The stock dropped 4.4% on July 16, 2026, when Bloomberg reported Google was months behind schedule on the flagship AI model. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19 and July 16, 2026, may be eligible to participate in the class action.

items.title: Mastercard: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Mastercard reported Q3 2026 earnings with 14% year-over-year net revenue growth and 18% net income increase. The company is expanding beyond traditional payment processing into high-margin services including cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and analytics (up 19% YoY). Mastercard is positioning itself for AI-enabled transactions through verified tokenization tools and acquired BVNK to bridge fiat currencies with digital assets, strengthening its network infrastructure for long-term growth.

items.title: Is AI Killing Google's Golden Goose?
items.summary: Alphabet stock plummeted 12% after earnings missed expectations, with Google Search revenue growth slowing to 12%—its slowest rate since 2023—as users shift to AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. While Google Cloud posted impressive 103% growth and the company maintained strong operating margins, investors were spooked by a $9 billion free cash flow loss and concerns about search monetization in the AI era. Management argues the slowdown is transitional as it ramps up ads in AI mode.

items.title: ASML vs. Nvidia: Who Really Captures the AI Chip Boom?
items.summary: While Nvidia generates nearly 10 times ASML's revenue and maintains higher profit margins (74% vs 49%), ASML holds a critical monopoly as the sole supplier of EUV lithography machines essential for advanced chip manufacturing. The article suggests ASML may be the safer AI investment due to its irreplaceable position in the supply chain, though Nvidia's faster growth offers greater long-term upside potential.

items.title: Lockheed Martin: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Lockheed Martin raised full-year sales guidance after Q3 2026 sales grew 11% YoY to $20.7 billion. The company expanded its record backlog to $292 billion with a 4x book-to-bill ratio, secured a landmark F-35 agreement for 850 jets over 10 years, and committed $8 billion through 2030 to expand munitions manufacturing. items.title: Why Norwegian Cruise Line Stock Jumped Today
items.summary: Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH) stock surged 13.45% after reporting Q3 earnings that beat Wall Street expectations with adjusted net income of $514 million ($1.12 per share vs. $0.93 expected). The company improved operating efficiency despite rising fuel costs, benefited from increased last-minute bookings and higher onboard spending, and raised full-year guidance to $1.70 per share from $1.50. Management is using profits and asset sales to strengthen the balance sheet by paying down debt.

items.title: Lost Money on The Cooper Companies, Inc. Shares? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Continues Investigating Potential Securities Fraud After 14.67% Stock Decline
items.summary: The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz is investigating The Cooper Companies, Inc. for potential securities fraud following a 14.67% stock decline on September 10, 2026. The decline occurred after Cooper Companies reported flat year-over-year revenue of $717 million and reduced full-year guidance by approximately 1.4% due to U.S. channel inventory reductions. Investors who suffered losses may have claims to recover them.

items.title: Alphabet Sheds $500 Billion in a Single Day Despite Cloud Growth of 103%
items.summary: Alphabet experienced its worst day ever, dropping over 13% after Q3 2026 earnings. While revenue surged 25% to $127.6 billion and Google Cloud revenue doubled to $30.7 billion, record capital expenditures of $51.4 billion for AI infrastructure caused net income to fall 25% and resulted in negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion. The market is concerned that massive AI spending is currently outweighing gains, and slowing Google Search growth raises questions about AI's long-term impact on the company's core business.

items.title: Semiconductor Sell-Off: The 1 AI Chip Stock I'd Buy and 1 I'd Avoid
items.summary: During the semiconductor sell-off, Broadcom emerges as the better AI chip investment with its 221% year-over-year AI revenue growth, custom chip capabilities, and attractive 18x forward P/E ratio. Intel, while offering turnaround potential, presents higher risks due to execution challenges in its foundry business and a premium 51x forward P/E valuation that leaves little room for disappointment.

items.title: ROSEN, A RANKED AND LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages Everest Group, Ltd. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - EG
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed class action lawsuits against Everest Group, Ltd., FuelCell Energy, Inc., and DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased securities during specified periods. The firm is seeking lead plaintiffs and encouraging investors to join the litigation. The Everest Group lawsuit alleges materially false statements regarding casualty risk exposure, inadequate pricing, and insufficient reserves.

items.title: Is Alphabet Stock a Buy After Its Post-Earnings Drop?
items.summary: Alphabet's stock fell ~10% after Q3 earnings despite 25% revenue growth to $127.6B and Google Cloud revenue doubling. While underlying profits grew 22% year-over-year (excluding investment losses), the company faces margin pressure from massive AI spending. Free cash flow turned negative for the second consecutive quarter as capital expenditures more than doubled to $51.4B. The author suggests the stock is reasonably valued at 19x 2027 earnings and considers it a buying opportunity, though acknowledges cash flow challenges may persist.

items.title: CELH IMPORTANT DEADLINE: ROSEN, HIGHLY RECOGNIZED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Celsius Holdings, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important November 3 Deadline in Securities Class Action - CELH
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is encouraging investors in Celsius Holdings (CELH) who purchased securities between February 21, 2025 and June 3, 2026 to join a class action lawsuit before the November 3, 2026 deadline. The lawsuit alleges that Celsius made materially false and misleading statements regarding cardiac risks associated with its Alani Nu products and inappropriately marketed these products to consumers under 18. Similar class action notices are being issued for Everest Group, Ltd. (EG) and FuelCell Energy, Inc. (FCEL).

items.title: ASTS DEADLINE: ROSEN, RECOGNIZED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - ASTS
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. for allegedly making false and misleading statements regarding its capital requirements, liquidity position, competitive standing in the satellite D2C market, and user adoption rates. Investors who purchased securities between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is November 13, 2026.

items.title: Fortinet (FTNT) Stock Plunges After Q3 Earnings: Time to Buy the Dip?
items.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) stock fell 20% after Q3 earnings despite beating expectations and raising full-year guidance, following a 100%+ year-to-date rally. While earnings and billings growth were strong, slowing service revenue growth disappointed investors. However, the stock now trades at a more attractive 37X forward P/E, well below the industry average of 56X, presenting a potential buying opportunity for long-term investors.

items.title: BAIDU DEADLINE: ROSEN, RECOGNIZED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Baidu, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BIDU
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying Baidu investors of an important November 13, 2026 deadline to serve as lead plaintiff in a securities class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that Baidu made false statements about its AI business's ability to offset declines in its legacy online marketing business, resulting in misleading revenue projections. Investors who purchased Baidu securities between November 18, 2025 and August 17, 2026 may be eligible for compensation.

items.title: The Hidden Cost of AI: How Intapp is Saving Law Firms From Skyrocketing IT Bills
items.summary: Intapp's Celeste platform helps law firms control AI costs by routing simple queries to databases instead of expensive AI models, reducing token burn. The company's cloud migration strategy is driving 28% year-over-year ARR growth with 70%+ gross margins and strong free cash flow, positioning it as an efficient alternative to standard AI implementations that waste compute resources.

items.title: The Cooper Companies, Inc. Investor News: If You Have Suffered Losses in The Cooper Companies, Inc., You Are Encouraged to Contact The Rosen Law Firm About Your Rights
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is investigating potential securities claims against The Cooper Companies, Inc. (NASDAQ: COO) for allegedly issuing materially misleading business information. The investigation was prompted by Cooper Companies' September 10, 2026 earnings report that disappointed Wall Street with weak guidance and a decision not to sell Cooper Surgical, causing the stock to fall 14.6% that day. Investors who purchased Cooper Companies securities may be eligible for compensation through a class action lawsuit.

items.title: Intel Server Sales Jump 78%, Q4 Outlook Dims: Rapid Earnings Reaction
items.summary: Intel reported its strongest data center revenue growth in 15 years with a 78% jump and tripled operating income, but shares fell 18% after-hours due to a weak Q4 forecast showing lower revenue, gross margin, and earnings. While server chip demand outpaces supply, a PC market slowdown expected through mid-2025 is offsetting data center strength.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 29: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Beats Q3 Estimates, Raises Full-Year Guidance
items.summary: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings (NCLH) surged 13.45% after beating Q3 earnings estimates and raising full-year EPS guidance to $1.70. The cruise operator reported $2.95 billion in revenue and is managing high fuel prices and slow bookings effectively. Peer cruise operators Royal Caribbean and Carnival also gained on stronger cruise demand. The broader market declined with S&P 500 down 0.31% and Nasdaq down 1.38%.

items.title: Arista Networks (ANET) Declines More Than Market: Some Information for Investors
items.summary: Arista Networks (ANET) declined 1.34% on October 29, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.31% loss. The cloud networking company has lost 8.29% prior to this session. Despite the recent weakness, the company maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with strong earnings expectations for Q3 2026 (EPS of $1.08, +44% YoY) and full-year guidance (EPS of $4.12, +38.26% YoY). However, ANET trades at a premium valuation with a Forward P/E of 45.37 versus the industry average of 20.67.

items.title: Starbucks (SBUX) Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates
items.summary: Starbucks reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.80 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.73, representing a 9.59% surprise. However, revenues of $9.14 billion missed expectations by 1.41%. The company has outperformed the S&P 500 by 22.6% year-to-date and holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, though the Retail-Restaurants industry ranks in the bottom 40% of sectors.

items.title: UPS vs. FedEx: Which Stock Is the Better Buy After Strong Q3 Results?
items.summary: UPS and FedEx both rallied following strong Q3 earnings and raised financial guidance. UPS offers cheaper valuation (13X forward earnings) and higher dividend yield (6.2%), making it attractive for value and income investors. FedEx shows stronger earnings growth (28% EPS increase) and stock performance (24% YoY gain), appealing to growth investors. Both stocks received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating following their sharp rallies.

items.title: SpaceX vs. Nvidia: The Best AI Stock to Buy Now
items.summary: While SpaceX's AI division showed explosive 830% revenue growth in Q3, Nvidia remains the superior AI investment choice. SpaceX trades at a 41x forward price-to-sales ratio compared to Nvidia's 12x, and Nvidia maintains a 66% operating margin versus SpaceX's 5.7%. Though SpaceX is in a growth phase prioritizing market share, Nvidia's combination of strong growth (106%), profitability, and valuation makes it the safer, more reliable AI stock investment.

items.title: Bristol Myers’ Growth Drugs Hit $7.7 Billion: Rapid Earnings Reaction
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb's Growth Portfolio of newer drugs surged 12% to $7.7 billion in Q3 2026, driving the company's 7% overall revenue growth to $13.1 billion. While adjusted EPS fell 17% to $1.35, this decline reflects upfront acquisition costs for pipeline drugs rather than core business weakness. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $49.75-$50.25 billion, signaling confidence in its drug portfolio diversification strategy.

items.title: INCY Q3 Loss Narrower Than Expected, Sales Beat, FY'26 View Raised
items.summary: Incyte Corporation reported Q3 2026 revenues of $1.56 billion, up 14% year-over-year and beating estimates, despite posting an adjusted loss of $3.60 per share due to acquisition-related R&D expenses. Key products Opzelura, Niktimvo, and Zynyz showed strong growth. The company raised its 2026 net sales guidance to $5.21-$5.30 billion, reflecting continued commercial momentum.

items.title: FedEx Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on Higher Yields, 2026 Outlook Raised
items.summary: FedEx exceeded Q3 earnings and revenue expectations with $3.74 EPS and $22.86B in revenues, driven by higher package yields, international growth, and Network 2.0 cost savings. The company raised its 2026 EPS guidance to $18.00-$18.60 and expects ~12% revenue growth. Other transportation peers showed mixed results, with Delta and United missing estimates while J.B. Hunt beat expectations.

items.title: Western Digital vs. Seagate: Best AI Stock to Buy After Earnings
items.summary: Both Western Digital and Seagate reported strong Q1 2027 earnings driven by AI infrastructure demand, with revenue growth of 55% and 61% respectively. However, Seagate appears more attractive with a higher ROE of 386.9% versus Western Digital's 57.9%, and a lower forward P/E ratio of 19.01 compared to 19.37, making it the better buy.

items.title: C.H. Robinson Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on Pricing and Lean AI Gains
items.summary: C.H. Robinson (CHRW) delivered impressive Q3 2026 results with earnings up 28.6% to $1.80 per share and revenues surging 29.5% to $5.36 billion, beating consensus estimates. The company maintained its 2026 profit guidance and expects $300 million in annual synergies from its proposed $5.8 billion RXO acquisition. Strong performance was driven by higher freight pricing, AI productivity gains, and market share growth, though operating cash flow declined due to unfavorable working capital changes.

items.title: Okta Surges 158% YTD: Should Investors Hold the Stock Now?
items.summary: Okta shares have surged 157.5% YTD, driven by strong enterprise demand for identity security and AI solutions. The company benefits from newer products delivering 40% ACV uplift and large enterprise customer growth exceeding 20%. However, intense competition from Microsoft and CrowdStrike, slowing revenue growth projections (10-11% for fiscal 2027), and premium valuation warrant a Hold rating.

items.title: HONA Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Supply Chain Recovery and 2027 Growth
items.summary: Honeywell Aerospace (HONA) beat Q3 earnings expectations with $2.21 EPS and $4.64B revenue, raising 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.85-$8.00. The company announced a $500M capacity expansion and inaugural dividend but faces continued supply chain constraints from 70 suppliers, particularly in bearings, machining, and castings. Management expects margin pressures to persist through 2027 despite strong aerospace demand.

items.title: KLAC Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on AI Demand
items.summary: KLA Corporation reported Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings of $1.22 per share, up 38.6% year-over-year, with revenues reaching $4.14 billion, up 28.9%. The growth was driven by AI infrastructure investments and strong demand for wafer inspection equipment, which surged 37%. The company projects Q2 revenues of $4.7 billion and raised its calendar 2026 wafer equipment market outlook to the mid-$150 billion range.

items.title: NOW Q3 Earnings Lag Estimates, Revenues Rise on Subscription Growth
items.summary: ServiceNow reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.00 per share (missing estimates by 1.96%) with revenues of $4.11 billion, up 20.5% YoY. Subscription revenues grew 21% to $3.99 billion, while AI net new ACV surged 65% YoY. The company raised 2026 subscription revenue guidance to $15.78-$15.79 billion and AI ACV target to $1.7 billion. However, gross margins contracted to 77.5% from 81%, reflecting cost pressures from increased R&D and sales investments.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alphabet Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding Gemini 3.5 Pro's performance. The complaint claims the AI model delivered disappointing training results, leading to significant launch delays, while the company made positive statements about its business prospects that lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026.

items.title: BKR Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong IET Growth & Chart Gains
items.summary: Baker Hughes (BKR) beat Q3 2026 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of 70 cents and revenues of $8.03 billion, driven by strong Industrial and Energy Technology (IET) orders that surged 42% to $5.89 billion. The company raised its full-year IET orders outlook to $21.5-$23.5 billion and targets over $50 billion in cumulative orders through 2028, though GAAP profitability declined due to acquisition-related costs and higher debt from the Chart acquisition.

items.title: GOOGL Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates, Cloud & Search Aid Top-Line Growth
items.summary: Alphabet reported Q3 2026 revenues of $127.58B (+25% YoY) but missed EPS expectations at $2.12 (-26% YoY) due to unrealized losses on equity investments. Google Cloud surged 103% with a $561B backlog, but AI capital expenditures more than doubled to $51.36B, resulting in negative free cash flow of $9.07B. The company maintained 2026 capex guidance of $195-205B with expectations for significant increases in 2027.

items.title: Vertiv Q3 Earnings Beat on Robust Sales Growth and Strong AI Demand
items.summary: Vertiv (VRT) delivered exceptional Q3 2026 results with adjusted earnings jumping 78% to $2.21 per share and revenues surging 61.2% to $4.31 billion, driven by robust AI infrastructure demand. The company reported organic orders more than doubling and raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting net sales between $14.45-$14.85 billion and adjusted earnings of $7.10-$7.20 per share.

items.title: GE Vernova Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Pricing and Grid Expansion
items.summary: GE Vernova (GEV) exceeded Q3 earnings expectations with $4.81 EPS vs. $4.03 consensus and $12.64B revenue vs. $12.10B estimate. The company raised 2026 guidance, expects 50% higher gas equipment pricing in 2026, announced a $9B Trench Group acquisition for grid expansion, and doubled its share buyback to $20B. Electrification segment backlog reached $42B with improving margins, though Wind segment continues to face headwinds.

items.title: PWR Q3 Earnings Beat on Electric Strength, 2026 View Raised, Stock Up
items.summary: Quanta Services (PWR) delivered impressive Q3 2026 results with adjusted EPS surging 82% to $6.06 and revenues jumping 57.4% to $12.01 billion, both beating consensus estimates. The Electric segment led growth with 58.8% revenue increase, while total backlog hit a record $63.7 billion. PWR raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $41.30-$41.60 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $17.90-$18.30, with management anticipating strong double-digit earnings growth in 2027.

items.title: Innodata vs. Accenture: Which AI Stock Has More Growth Potential?
items.summary: Innodata (INOD) and Accenture (ACN) are both capitalizing on AI adoption, but with different strategies. INOD specializes in AI training datasets and frontier AI services with projected 2026 revenue growth of 43.1% and earnings growth of 28.3%, but trades at a premium valuation (26.55X P/E) with customer concentration risks. ACN offers greater financial stability, lower valuation (16.36X P/E), and improving earnings estimates, but with slower growth prospects (4-5% expected). INOD is favored for growth-oriented investors willing to tolerate volatility, while ACN appeals to those seeking stability.

items.title: Kenvue's Q3 Earnings on the Horizon: Key Insights for Investors
items.summary: Kenvue Inc. is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 30, with consensus estimates at $3.9 billion in revenue (3.3% growth) and 28 cents EPS (flat YoY). While the company likely benefited from brand investments, e-commerce expansion, and strong demand for products like Zyrtec and Tylenol, inflationary pressures and margin headwinds pose challenges. The Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat, with KVUE showing 0% Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

items.title: Teradyne Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and 2027 Growth Plans
items.summary: Teradyne (TER) exceeded Q3 earnings expectations with $2.29 EPS and $1.31B in revenues, driven by sustained AI demand with AI-related revenues exceeding 60% of total sales. The company reported record memory test revenues of $301M and expects continued growth in 2027 from hyperscaler compute programs and memory testing. Q4 guidance of $1.25B-$1.35B implies ~20% YoY growth, though margin pressures from supply costs and capacity expansion are acknowledged.

items.title: WM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Healthcare Gains and Volume Pressure
items.summary: Waste Management reported Q3 2026 revenues of $6.85B beating estimates, but adjusted EPS of $2.15 missed consensus of $2.18. The company maintained full-year guidance despite headwinds from sluggish waste volumes (down 0.5%), elevated fuel costs, and insurance expenses. Healthcare EBITDA surged 33% on pricing and integration savings, while free cash flow rose 42% year-to-date. CEO Jim Fish will retire in early January, with President John Morris taking over.

items.title: Teqnion Acquires Odlings Group - www.marketscreener.com
items.summary: Teqnion Acquires Odlings Group    www.marketscreener.com

items.title: WEC Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Demand, Revenues Rise Y/Y
items.summary: WEC Energy Group reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.18 per share, beating estimates by 20.41% with a 42.2% year-over-year increase. Revenues grew 8.9% to $2.29 billion, driven by favorable weather, capital investments, and operating efficiency. The company raised its 2026 earnings guidance to $5.60-$5.64 per share and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

items.title: EQT and Range Resources Are Merging: Is It Time to Buy the New U.S. Natural Gas Titan?
items.summary: EQT will acquire Range Resources in an all-stock deal valued at $13 billion, creating the largest U.S. natural gas producer with combined enterprise value exceeding $50 billion. The merger is expected to close in Q1 2027 and will generate $325 million in annual corporate/operational cost savings plus $300 million from post-production optimization. With strong natural gas demand from AI infrastructure and data centers, EQT stock trading at an 11% free-cash-flow yield presents an attractive investment opportunity.

items.title: LIN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Americas Pricing & Volumes
items.summary: Linde plc (LIN) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.59, up 9% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates by 1.55%. Revenue grew 9% to $9.40 billion, driven by higher pricing and volume growth across all regions. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.82-$17.92 (8-9% growth), supported by a strong $10.8 billion project backlog. However, LIN carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating.

items.title: Altria Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Pricing & Higher Profits
items.summary: Altria Group reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.52, beating consensus estimates, with net revenues up 1% to $6.13 billion. Higher pricing in smokeable products drove a 3.9% increase in adjusted OCI despite lower volumes. The company raised its 2026 EPS guidance to $5.66-$5.74 and expanded its share buyback program by $1 billion. However, oral tobacco products faced headwinds with declining volumes in traditional brands like Copenhagen and Skoal, though the on! nicotine pouch brand showed growth.

items.title: Corning Q3 Sales Jump 19% as AI Optical Demand and Margins Accelerate
items.summary: Corning (GLW) reported Q3 core sales growth of 19% to $5.08 billion and core earnings up 36% to 91 cents per share, driven by a 44% surge in Optical Communications sales fueled by AI infrastructure demand. The company secured multibillion-dollar long-term customer agreements with Verizon and AT&T, expanded operating margins to 22.7%, and provided Q4 guidance suggesting continued double-digit earnings growth. However, the Solar segment remains unprofitable despite 37% revenue growth.

items.title: Vulcan Materials Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Miss, Stock Down
items.summary: Vulcan Materials reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.83 per share, beating estimates, but revenues of $2.18 billion missed expectations and declined 4.7% year-over-year. While aggregates pricing rose 5%, shipments fell 3% and higher diesel costs pressured profitability. The company lowered its 2026 EBITDA outlook to $2.4 billion but expects earnings growth in 2027. VMC stock declined 1.9% following the earnings release.

items.title: Everest Group Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Higher Catastrophe Losses
items.summary: Everest Group reported Q3 2026 operating EPS of $7.62, missing estimates by 18.8%, with revenues declining 14% to $3.71 billion. The company faced an underwriting loss of $223 million due to elevated catastrophe losses and adverse reserve development, pushing the combined ratio to 107.1%. However, investment income surged 17.4% to a record $634 million. Comparatively, peers Chubb, Travelers, and Arch Capital beat earnings expectations in the same quarter.

items.title: Is CLS a Buy Now as AI Growth Collides With Premium Valuation Risks?
items.summary: Celestica (CLS) is experiencing rapid AI-driven growth with Connectivity & Cloud Solutions revenues surging 102% YoY, but the stock now trades at a premium to its sub-industry at 16.79X forward earnings. While the company benefits from strong AI and data-center demand, it has reduced its 2026 free cash flow guidance to $460M from $600M due to rising inventory and capital investments. The investment case hinges on converting exceptional growth into durable cash generation while managing high customer concentration risk.

items.title: AEP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Growth Outlook and $100B Capital Plan
items.summary: American Electric Power (AEP) beat Q3 2026 earnings and revenue estimates, reporting operating earnings of $2.23 per share versus consensus of $2.04. The company unveiled a $100 billion five-year capital plan through 2031 and raised its long-term earnings growth outlook to 9-11% annually (from 7-9%), driven by accelerating electricity demand from data centers and manufacturing. AEP reported 84 GW of contracted load through 2031, with rate base expected to grow from $87 billion to $162 billion.

items.title: CLS Falls 14.4% in a Week as AI Growth Meets Rising Execution Risks
items.summary: Celestica Inc. (CLS) shares dropped 14.4% in a week despite posting strong Q3 2026 results with 82.5% revenue growth and 108.9% adjusted EPS growth, driven by AI infrastructure demand. However, the company lowered its 2026 free cash flow outlook to $460M due to higher inventory and working capital needs, raising concerns about execution risks and customer concentration as the company scales.

items.title: CLS Raises 2026 Outlook as AI Demand Powers an Aggressive 2027 Ramp
items.summary: Celestica (CLS) beat Q3 earnings estimates by 9.3% with 82.5% revenue growth driven by strong AI infrastructure demand. The company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $21B and set a $40B target for 2027, implying ~90% growth. However, the expansion plan requires $1.5B-$2B in capital spending and significant working capital investments, with free cash flow guidance reduced to $460M for 2026, leaving limited room for execution errors.

items.title: L3Harris Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates, Raises 2026 Revenue View
items.summary: L3Harris Technologies reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.28 per share, beating estimates by 9.7% with a 33.3% year-over-year increase. Revenues reached $6.06 billion, up 7.1%, driven by double-digit growth in Space & Mission Systems (up 10.3%) and strong demand in Missile Solutions. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $23.5-$23.7 billion while maintaining its $3 billion free cash flow outlook.

items.title: Alibaba Cloud Revenue Growth Accelerates: Can AI Sustain Momentum?
items.summary: Alibaba Cloud achieved its fastest growth in 22 quarters with 45% revenue surge driven by strong AI infrastructure demand, reaching RMB12.4 billion in AI product revenues. However, a 75% capex surge and intense competition from Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud pose sustainability challenges to its growth momentum.

items.title: HII Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $5.48 per share, up 48.9% YoY and beating consensus by 24.3%. Revenues climbed 10.8% to $3.54B, driven by higher submarine, aircraft carrier, and amphibious assault ship volumes. The company raised its 2026 shipbuilding revenue outlook to $10.5-$10.7B and reaffirmed free cash flow guidance of $500-$600M.

items.title: BigBear.ai vs. Booz Allen: Which Government AI Stock is Better Now?
items.summary: BigBear.ai (BBAI) demonstrates strong revenue growth of 31% YoY and expanding backlog, but faces persistent operating losses and negative adjusted EBITDA. Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) offers stronger fundamentals with a $40.9 billion backlog, improved earnings guidance, and superior ROE of 75%, though elevated debt levels warrant attention. Overall, BAH appears the more compelling investment for risk-averse investors seeking profitability visibility, while BBAI represents a higher-risk, higher-growth opportunity.

items.title: HSY Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on Cost Relief and Pricing Gains
items.summary: The Hershey Company reported strong Q3 2026 earnings of $2.64 per share, up 103.1% year-over-year, driven by strategic pricing actions, tariff refunds, and lower commodity costs. However, the company faced volume declines due to pricing elasticity and cautious consumer spending. Net sales rose 3% to $3.28 billion, with adjusted gross margins expanding significantly. Management raised its 2026 earnings outlook to 36-38.5% growth but acknowledged ongoing challenges in convenience stores and salty snacks supply constraints.

items.title: MRK Q3 Earnings & Sales Beat Estimates, '26 EPS View Raised, Stock Up
items.summary: Merck (MRK) beat Q3 2026 earnings and revenue estimates with adjusted EPS of $2.49 and revenues of $18.09 billion. Keytruda sales grew 6% to $8.60 billion, while newer products like Winrevair, Welireg, and Enflonsia showed strong momentum. The company raised its 2026 guidance for adjusted EPS to $2.77-$2.82 and sales to $66.8-$67.3 billion. However, established drugs like Januvia/Janumet and Bridion faced headwinds from generic competition.

items.title: Norwegian Cruise Q3 Earnings & Revenues Beat Estimates, Stock Up
items.summary: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings (NCLH) exceeded Q3 earnings expectations with $1.12 per share and revenues of $2.95 billion, driven by strong onboard revenue growth of 12.7%. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $1.7 and EBITDA to $2.55 billion, though passenger ticket revenues declined 5.1% year-over-year. Shares gained approximately 8% in pre-market trading following the results.

items.title: ETFs to Buy as Microsoft Shares Gain 4% Post Q1 Earnings Beat
items.summary: Microsoft shares gained 4% following better-than-expected fiscal Q1 2027 earnings and revenues. Cloud revenues grew 30% with Azure up 48%, but capital expenditure surged 29.5% to $45.2 billion, pressuring free cash flow by 27%. The company added 24 new data centers globally. Investors seeking Microsoft exposure with diversification can consider tech ETFs with significant MSFT holdings.

items.title: BG Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Soybean and Softseed Results
items.summary: Bunge Global (BG) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.56, up 12.8% YoY and beating consensus estimates of $2.45. Strong performance in Soybean and Softseed Processing segments drove results, with softseed processing EBIT jumping 19.6%. The company maintained full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $9.25-$9.75, though it expects slightly lower Soybean Processing results and weaker Tropical Oils performance, offset by improved Grain Merchandising outlook.

items.title: West Pharma Q3 Earnings Rise on HVP Strength, 2026 Outlook Raised
items.summary: West Pharmaceutical Services (WST) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.66, up 35.7% year-over-year and beating consensus by 22%. Revenues reached $874.5 million with 11.9% organic growth, driven by strong HVP Components sales. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for revenue and adjusted EPS, reflecting confidence in continued momentum.

items.title: EMCOR Q3 Earnings Beat on Construction Strength, '26 Outlook Raised
items.summary: EMCOR Group reported Q3 2026 earnings of $9.60 per share, up 46.1% YoY and beating estimates by 15.3%, with revenues rising 28.8% to $5.54 billion. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenues ($20.6-$21B) and EPS ($34.50-$35.50), driven by strong demand in electrical and mechanical construction. Record remaining performance obligations of $18.57 billion indicate sustained demand for mission-critical infrastructure.

items.title: Textron Q3 Earnings Outpace Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Textron Inc. reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.76, beating estimates by 23.1% with a 13.5% year-over-year increase. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.55-$6.65, above consensus estimates. Textron Aviation revenues jumped 14% to $1.7B driven by higher Citation jet volume, while Bell segment revenues declined 9% due to lower military volumes. The company maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Mastercard Beats Q3 Earnings on Higher Cross-Border Volumes & Pricing
items.summary: Mastercard delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS of $5.31, up 21.2% year-over-year and beating consensus estimates. Net revenues grew 14% to $9.8 billion, driven by cross-border volumes, pricing initiatives, and strong value-added services growth of 19%. The company maintained an adjusted operating margin of 60.5% despite higher operating expenses and payment network rebates.

items.title: Honeywell Aerospace Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Sales Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Honeywell Aerospace (HONA) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.21, beating estimates by 16.3%, with revenues up 2.4% to $4.64 billion. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.85-$8.00 and maintained 4-5% organic sales growth outlook. Backlog grew 12% to $19.32 billion, though tariff refunds were needed to offset higher costs and unfavorable sales mix.

items.title: BMY Q3 Earnings Tops Estimates, Higher Charges Weigh on Outlook
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb reported Q3 2026 revenues of $13.07 billion, beating estimates, with strong Growth Portfolio performance and 25% Eliquis sales growth. However, adjusted EPS fell 17% to $1.35 due to higher acquired in-process research and development charges and margin compression. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance but cut EPS outlook, citing a negative 60-cent IPRD impact.

items.title: Carrier Q3 Earnings & Sales Beat on HVAC Demand, Tariff Refunds
items.summary: Carrier Global (CARR) delivered exceptional Q3 2026 results with adjusted EPS up 30% to 87 cents and sales growth of 12% to $6.26 billion, driven by surging commercial HVAC orders (60% increase) and explosive data-center demand (300% jump). The company raised 2026 sales guidance to $23.8-$24 billion with record backlog of $8.5 billion. However, a $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge resulted in a GAAP loss, causing the stock to plunge 7.2% in pre-market trading.

items.title: Trane Technologies' Q3 Earnings Beat on Strong Commercial HVAC Demand
items.summary: Trane Technologies (TT) delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results with EPS of $4.86 (up 25.3% YoY) and revenues of $6.76 billion (up 17.7% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. Strong commercial HVAC demand drove 20% organic bookings growth and a 73% surge in backlog to $12.5 billion. The company raised its 2026 revenue growth outlook to 13.5% from 11.5%, though operating margins contracted 40 basis points due to inflation and supply chain pressures.

items.title: Microsoft vs. MongoDB: Which Technology Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: MongoDB and Microsoft are competing as AI data platforms, but MongoDB emerges as the better investment opportunity. MongoDB raised its fiscal 2027 guidance targeting 20%+ revenue growth with expanding margins and minimal capital spending, while Microsoft faces rising AI infrastructure costs exceeding $50 billion quarterly, cloud margin pressure, and Windows business weakness. MongoDB's lower valuation multiple and recent product launches position it as the more attractive entry point.

items.title: INVH Q3 FFO Meets Estimates, Revenues Miss, '26 Views Raised
items.summary: Invitation Homes (INVH) reported Q3 2026 core FFO of 48 cents per share, matching consensus estimates, with revenues rising 6.3% to $731.28 million. The company raised its 2026 core FFO guidance midpoint to $1.96 per share and improved same-store NOI outlook. Blended rental rate growth improved to 3%, though occupancy dipped slightly to 96.4%. INVH completed $318 million in home dispositions and repurchased 8.87 million shares for $250 million.

items.title: AOS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Boiler Growth, Pricing
items.summary: A.O. Smith beat EPS estimates with 93 cents per share but saw earnings decline 1.1% year-over-year. North America sales grew 3% while China sales plummeted 17% due to weak demand. The company announced plans to divest an 81% stake in its China business for approximately $400 million, with the deal expected to close in H1 2027.

items.title: Baxter Q3 Earnings Beat on Broad-Based Growth, '26 Outlook Raised
items.summary: Baxter International (BAX) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of 58 cents, beating estimates by 13.7%, with revenues up 5% to $2.98 billion. The company raised its 2026 sales growth outlook to 4-5% and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.05-$2.15, driven by strong performance in Medical Products & Therapies and Healthcare Systems & Technologies segments. However, adjusted operating margins contracted 40 basis points due to cost pressures.

items.title: CAT Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher Volume and Pricing
items.summary: Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) delivered robust Q3 2026 results with adjusted EPS of $7.20, up 45.5% year-over-year, beating consensus estimates. Sales climbed 17.3% to $20.68 billion driven by higher volume and favorable pricing across all three segments. The company's order backlog surged 95.7% to a record $78.1 billion, while operating margins expanded significantly. CAT maintained its mid-to-high-teens revenue growth outlook for 2026.

items.title: Fortinet Q3 Earnings & Revenues Beat Estimates, Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Fortinet delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results with non-GAAP EPS of 91 cents (up 23% YoY) and revenues of $2.08 billion (up 20.5% YoY), beating consensus estimates. Billings grew 29.2% to $2.34 billion, driven by strong demand for SASE Firewall, OT security, and AI-driven solutions. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for revenues, billings, and EPS, now projecting non-GAAP EPS of $3.54-$3.58.

items.title: Xcel Energy Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
items.summary: Xcel Energy reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.52 per share, beating consensus by 9.4% with a 22.6% year-over-year increase. Revenues climbed 6.6% to $4.17 billion, driven by infrastructure investment recovery, favorable weather, and higher electric sales. The company narrowed 2026 EPS guidance to $4.10-$4.16 and introduced 2027 outlook of $4.48-$4.62 per share.

items.title: American Water Q3 Earnings Miss on Higher Costs Despite Revenue Growth
items.summary: American Water Works (AWK) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.00, missing consensus estimates of $2.11 by 5.21%, despite 4.1% revenue growth to $1.51 billion. Higher operating costs and increased financing expenses pressured earnings, though rate increases and acquisitions provided growth drivers. The company narrowed 2026 guidance to $6.07-$6.12 and initiated 2027 guidance of $6.53-$6.63, representing ~8% growth.

items.title: GE Vernova's $197 Billion Backlog, $9 Billion Acquisition, and One Clear Strategy
items.summary: GE Vernova reported staggering Q3 results with orders jumping 96% and backlog reaching $197 billion, driven by AI data center demand. The company announced a $9 billion acquisition of Trench Group to secure critical grid components and lock up supply chain bottlenecks for competitors. Management raised full-year guidance and doubled its stock buyback plan to $20 billion.

items.title: PepsiCo vs. Coca-Cola: Which Beverage Titan Is the Better Bet?
items.summary: Coca-Cola emerges as the superior investment choice over PepsiCo, driven by stronger Q3 revenue growth (7%), margin expansion, and consistent market-share gains across 22 consecutive quarters. While PepsiCo trades at a lower valuation (15.43X forward P/E vs KO's 26.32X), it faces profitability pressures and declining North American demand. Coca-Cola's upward earnings estimate revisions and robust operational momentum justify its premium valuation, whereas PepsiCo's downward revisions and subdued earnings outlook warrant caution.

items.title: KIM Q3 FFO Beats on Strong Leasing, Revenues Miss, 2026 Outlook Raised
items.summary: Kimco Realty reported Q3 2026 FFO of 47 cents per share, beating consensus estimates by 1 cent, driven by strong leasing activity with 12% blended cash rent spreads and record small-shop occupancy of 92.9%. While total revenues missed expectations at $546.15 million, the company raised its 2026 FFO guidance to $1.84-$1.86 per share and same-property NOI growth outlook to 3.5%-3.8%, reflecting healthy leasing demand and improved tenant credit performance.

items.title: Micron Is Down 17% Over the Past Month. Is This AI Stock Still a Buy?
items.summary: Micron Technology's stock has declined 17% over the past month amid investor concerns about excessive AI spending by tech companies. However, the article argues Micron remains a strong buy, citing the company's exceptional Q4 results (380% revenue jump to $54.2B) and evidence that major tech companies' AI infrastructure investments are generating substantial returns. With memory demand outpacing supply and S&P Global projecting $1.3 trillion in AI infrastructure spending next year, Micron is well-positioned for continued growth despite near-term market volatility.

items.title: Mid-America's Q3 FFO Meets Estimates, Revenues Beat as Occupancy Gains
items.summary: Mid-America Apartment Communities (MAA) reported Q3 2026 core FFO of $2.10 per share matching estimates, with revenues beating consensus at $560.13 million driven by occupancy gains and 5.3% renewal lease rate growth. However, same-store NOI declined 1.8% due to rising operating expenses, and the company lowered its full-year 2026 core FFO guidance midpoint to $8.49 from $8.53, below consensus expectations.

items.summary: Textron reported quarterly earnings of $1.76 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.43 by 23.08%, though revenues slightly missed expectations. The aerospace and defense company has underperformed the S&P 500 by 23.3% year-to-date. With mixed estimate revisions, Textron received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

items.title: Merck (MRK) Surpasses Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
items.summary: Merck reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.49 per share, beating consensus estimates of $2.12, with revenues of $18.09 billion exceeding expectations. However, the company received a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revision trends, suggesting near-term underperformance. The pharmaceutical industry ranks in the bottom 11% of sectors, which may negatively impact the stock's outlook.

items.title: Warren Buffett's $48 Billion American Express Stake Has Been a Huge Winner. The Latest Results Say the Streak Is Far From Over.
items.summary: American Express, Berkshire Hathaway's second-largest holding worth $48 billion, continues to deliver strong performance with 440% total returns over the past decade. Q3 results show 9% revenue growth, 3.1 million new card members, and a stellar 38% return on equity. Management raised full-year profit guidance and is investing in AI partnerships with OpenAI to drive future growth.

items.title: Willis Towers Watson (WTW) Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates
items.summary: Willis Towers Watson reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.63 per share, beating consensus estimates of $3.60, but revenues of $2.46 billion missed expectations by 0.7%. Despite the earnings beat, the company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revision trends. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 15.2% year-to-date. The Insurance-Brokerage industry ranks in the bottom 6% of Zacks industries.

items.summary: Microsoft reported Q1 FY2027 earnings with Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassing $63 billion at 30% year-over-year growth. Data center efficiency gains are unlocking additional AI capacity, with Foundry revenue more than tripling. Microsoft is developing first-party AI models to reduce enterprise training costs and added 24 new data centers globally while reducing deployment times by 20%.
