items.title: Cadence Design Systems: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to 21% growth and reported record backlog of $8.2 billion in Q3 2026. The company launched Maestro, an AI-specialized suite for semiconductor design, and saw accelerating demand for hardware verification tools as chip complexity increases. Management highlighted strong customer R&D investments and structural competitive advantages positioning the company well in the AI-driven semiconductor market.

items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb’s Cancer Drug Just Doubled Survival Time Without Progression — Here’s Why It Matters
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb announced positive Phase 3 trial results for izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren), an experimental cancer drug that doubled progression-free survival time (11.1 months vs. 5.7 months) compared to chemotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer patients. However, the stock reaction was muted because the trial was conducted only in China, and FDA approval typically requires multi-region confirmatory data meeting Western standards. The drug represents part of BMY's strategy to transition from legacy medications to a growth portfolio.

items.title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth
items.summary: NVIDIA and Meta announced an expanded partnership to optimize infrastructure for AI agents, particularly Meta's Muse models. Meta will deploy NVIDIA's Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X networking, and BlueField-4 technology. NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering. The collaboration aims to improve inference and training performance while enhancing security and monitoring capabilities for AI agent deployment.

items.title: Elon Musk Predicts a Wave of Failures Among AI Cloud Companies. Is SpaceX Stock a Sell?
items.summary: Elon Musk warned that debt markets have cut off lending to AI cloud companies without significant revenue outside data centers, predicting most of 200+ neoclouds will fail or be acquired. SpaceX's AI segment now represents 52% of revenue ($7.56B in Q3), but the company differs from struggling neoclouds due to profitable Starlink and launch businesses providing $7B in quarterly revenue. While SpaceX faces high capital spending ($35-40B forecasted for Q4), its investment-grade credit rating and profitable AI unit suggest it's not a sell, though the stock at 34x sales isn't a bargain.

items.title: Alphabet Must Show This on Oct. 28 or the Stock Could Stall
items.summary: Alphabet's Oct. 28 earnings report will be critical for investors to assess whether Google Cloud's growing profits are translating into actual cash flow. The company posted negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion in Q2 despite strong cloud growth, and is now spending more on capex ($195-205B annually) than it generates in operating cash flow ($185.7B over trailing 12 months). Investors should focus on whether operating cash flow returns to the $45-50 billion range to confirm the AI investment is self-funding, or if the company continues relying on shareholder capital.

items.title: Tesla Is Investing Aggressively in its Next Generation Technology
items.summary: Tesla is making significant capital expenditure investments in next-generation technologies including driverless/autonomous driving capabilities and robotics. However, these heavy investments are currently causing the company's profits to decline as it prioritizes long-term technology development over near-term profitability.

items.title: ROSEN, TRUSTED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Duolingo, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - DUOL
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. alleging that the company made materially false statements regarding Daily Active User growth rates. The lawsuit claims Duolingo deliberately added user friction through increased ads and subscription upsells while knowing this would negatively impact DAU growth, and that AI-generated content degraded product quality. Investors who purchased DUOL stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026 may be eligible for compensation, with a December 7, 2026 deadline to serve as lead plaintiff.

items.title: Anthropic's Billions in Microsoft Commitments Add to Its Mounting Compute Bill
items.summary: Anthropic faces over $400 billion in cloud infrastructure commitments across multiple providers, with Microsoft alone accounting for at least $44.9 billion through 2033. The AI startup spent nearly $9 billion on compute in the first half of 2026, representing its largest cost. While these massive commitments pose risks if demand falters, they reflect the scarcity of computing power needed to support Anthropic's growth in generative AI.

items.title: ROSEN, A TOP-RANKED AND GLOBAL LAW FIRM, Encourages Baidu, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BIDU
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is soliciting investors who purchased securities in Baidu, Tigo Energy, and XTI Aerospace during specified class periods to join securities class action lawsuits. The firm alleges that Baidu overstated its AI business capabilities and misled investors about revenue prospects, while similar claims are being pursued against the other companies.

items.title: XTIA DEADLINE NOTICE: ROSEN, NATIONAL TRIAL LAWYERS, Encourages XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 27 Deadline in Securities Class Action - XTIA
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against XTI Aerospace, Inc. for investors who purchased securities between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities requiring Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to file timely earnings reports. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 27, 2026.

items.title: Why Range Resources Stock Surged Today
items.summary: Range Resources stock jumped nearly 18% after announcing an all-stock acquisition deal by EQT, creating a natural gas giant valued at over $50 billion. The merged company expects $325 million in annual cost savings and $20 billion in free cash flow over five years, positioning it to capitalize on rising LNG demand in Asia and Europe, plus growing natural gas demand from AI data centers.

items.title: Roper Technologies: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Roper Technologies reported 8% total revenue growth in Q3 2026 and raised full-year earnings expectations. The company is expanding AI agents into specialized enterprise workflows, has over $6 billion in acquisition capacity, and maintains enterprise software retention in the mid-90s, positioning it well for disciplined M&A and shareholder returns.

items.title: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) Laps the Stock Market: Here's Why
items.summary: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) closed at $12.79, up 2.65%, outperforming the S&P 500's 0.7% gain. The stock has gained 17% over the past month despite the sector declining 7.7%. Upcoming earnings are projected at -$0.22 per share with quarterly revenue expected at $53.09 million, down 29.36% year-over-year. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Principal Financial (PFG) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Miss Estimates
items.summary: Principal Financial (PFG) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.22 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $2.46 and representing a -9.76% earnings surprise. Revenue also fell short at $4.28 billion versus the $4.31 billion estimate. The company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revisions, with shares expected to underperform the market. Despite outperforming the S&P 500 by 23.1% year-to-date, the Insurance - Multi line industry ranks in the bottom 22% of Zacks industries.

items.title: Tesla Isn’t a Hyperscaler. Why the AI Bears Are Misreading Its $5 Billion Capex Cut.
items.summary: Tesla reduced its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $5 billion to approximately $20 billion, but this doesn't signal a pullback from AI development. Unlike hyperscalers like Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft that build data centers for external customers, Tesla's AI investments are focused on developing autonomous driving, robotaxi services, and humanoid robots for internal use. Management indicated spending will increase in coming years, suggesting the cut reflects timing rather than reduced ambition.

items.title: AI Headlines Pile Up as Wall Street Navigates a Volatile Week
items.summary: Anthropic filed for IPO with impressive financials showing $4.6B revenue in 2024 and $16.3B in H1 2026, while Meta announced a $95B equity offering to fund AI expansion. SpaceX secured $40B in debt financing for AI chips, but concerns mount over neocloud operators' sustainability as debt markets tighten. The AI investment cycle is shifting from infrastructure buildout to financing sustainability, with major central bank decisions and hyperscaler earnings reports this week adding to market volatility.

items.title: Deadline Alert: XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors Have Until October 27, 2026 to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role in Securities Fraud Class Action, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Reminds Investors
items.summary: XTI Aerospace investors have until October 27, 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status in a securities fraud class action lawsuit. The company failed to disclose material adverse facts about senior executives' undisclosed activities and governance issues, leading to a 15.9% stock price drop on August 18, 2026 when the company announced it could not timely file its quarterly report.

items.title: Elon Musk Warns of “Death and Consolidation” Across the AI Cloud Industry. Is SpaceX Really Different?
items.summary: Elon Musk warns that tightening debt markets are forcing widespread failures and consolidation among AI cloud providers ('neoclouds'). While SpaceX has diversified revenue streams that provide protection from this financing crunch, its AI infrastructure investments remain unproven and must eventually generate sufficient returns to justify their enormous costs.

items.title: Top Stock Picks for Week of October 26, 2026
items.summary: Zacks has identified Shopify (SHOP) and Penguin Solutions (PENG) as Zacks Rank #1 stocks with strong growth prospects. Shopify, a leading commerce platform, is expected to grow earnings 61.5% this fiscal year with improving free cash flow margins. Penguin Solutions, an AI infrastructure provider, reported Q4 EPS more than doubled year-over-year with revenue up 68%, and raised its fiscal 2027 guidance to 40% growth with 55% EPS growth at the midpoint.

items.title: FIX Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Backlog Growth and 2027 Outlook
items.summary: Comfort Systems USA (FIX) reported third-quarter revenues of $3.77B, exceeding consensus estimates, with a record $17.81B backlog representing 90% year-over-year growth. The company projects mid-40% organic growth in 2026 and mid-20% growth in 2027, driven by strong demand from technology customers who now represent 59% of revenues. Management is expanding modular capacity to 6M square feet by 2027 while maintaining disciplined capital allocation and selective customer commitments.

items.title: Vertiv to Report Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Vertiv is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 28, with expected revenues of $3.76 billion (40.63% YoY growth) and EPS of $1.82 (46.77% YoY growth). The company is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure and data center demand, margin expansion to 24-25%, and geographic strength across Americas, APAC, and EMEA. However, supply chain challenges and higher tariffs pose headwinds. Despite a stretched valuation at 15.72X price-to-book, Zacks rates VRT as a Buy (Rank #2) based on robust growth prospects and AI innovation.

items.title: Is REAL a Buy Now as Growth Accelerates but Valuation Stays Rich?
items.summary: The RealReal (REAL) reported Q2 2026 GMV growth of 22% to $617M and doubled adjusted EBITDA, raising its 2026 outlook. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (10.96X forward PEG) with concerns around take-rate compression, high debt levels, and competition from eBay and ThredUp in the resale market.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alphabet Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding Gemini 3.5 Pro's performance. The complaint claims the AI model delivered disappointing training results, leading to significant launch delays, while the company made positive statements about its business prospects that lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026.

items.title: Masco to Report Q3 Earnings: Here's What to Expect This Season
items.summary: Masco Corporation is set to report Q3 2026 results on October 28, with EPS estimated at $1.01 (up 4.1% YoY) and sales projected to grow 0.8%. The Decorative Architectural Products segment is expected to drive growth with 9.8% sales increase, while Plumbing Products may decline 2.3%. The company's restructuring initiatives and cost controls should support margins, though the stock carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with no earnings beat predicted.

items.title: Here's What Investors Must Know Ahead of BigBear.ai's Q3 Earnings
items.summary: BigBear.ai is expected to report Q3 2026 revenues of $38.9 million, up 17.5% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AI solutions in defense and border operations. However, the company is forecast to report a loss of six cents per share, narrower than the prior year but wider than consensus estimates from 30 days ago. While higher-margin GenAI products like Ask Sage may help reduce losses, rising R&D and operational expenses are expected to pressure profitability.

items.title: Equinix to Post Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: Equinix (EQIX) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 28, with consensus estimates projecting 11% revenue growth to $2.57 billion and 6.9% AFFO per share growth to $10.51. Strong demand for interconnected data center infrastructure driven by AI adoption and cloud expansion is expected to support growth, though high interest expenses may be a headwind. The company's quantitative model does not predict a surprise beat this quarter.

items.title: BXP to Post Q3 Earnings: Is the Stock a Portfolio Must-Have?
items.summary: BXP, Inc. is scheduled to report Q3 2026 results on October 27, with revenues projected to rise 3.7% and FFO per share expected to grow 3.5% year-over-year. The office REIT is positioned to benefit from strong demand for premier office spaces and positive U.S. office market recovery, though competitive leasing conditions and higher operating costs may limit margin expansion.

items.title: Salesforce vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Salesforce and IBM present contrasting investment profiles in 2026. Salesforce leads in growth (13.5% vs 4.5% average revenue growth) and profitability (21.5% operating margin), while IBM offers better valuation metrics (3.4x P/S ratio vs 4.7x) and higher dividend yield (2.66% vs 0.70%). The choice depends on investor preference: growth-oriented investors favor Salesforce, while value investors may prefer IBM.

items.title: Intuit vs. BILL: Which Financial Software Stock Is a Better Buy Today?
items.summary: Intuit and BILL Holdings both compete in the financial software space, with different strategies. Intuit leverages its QuickBooks platform and broader diversification, but faces slowing customer growth and declining EPS estimates. BILL focuses on payment workflows with stronger profitability prospects (23-24% operating margin expected in FY27) and positive EPS revisions. BILL trades at a lower forward P/E multiple and is rated a Strong Buy, while Intuit is rated Buy, with BILL offering stronger growth and profitability improvement potential.

items.title: Fortinet Stock Before Q3 Earnings: Buy Now or Wait for Results?
items.summary: Fortinet is set to report Q3 2026 results with projected revenues of $2.01-$2.1B (19.55% YOY growth) and billings of $2.25-$2.35B. Strong demand for SASE Firewall, AI-security expansion through the Virtue AI acquisition, and strategic partnerships with Intel support growth. However, premium valuation (P/E of 47.69), margin pressures, and intense competition from established cybersecurity players present headwinds.

items.title: Not AMD. Not Marvell. Here's Which Company Nvidia Needs to Be Worried About.
items.summary: Broadcom, not AMD or Marvell, poses the biggest threat to Nvidia's AI computing dominance through custom AI chips. With AI segment revenue expected to reach $115 billion in 2027 and $230 billion in 2028, Broadcom is positioned to capture significant market share. Trading at 17x 2027 earnings estimates, the stock could potentially double if valued at 35x earnings, offering strong growth potential alongside multiple years of revenue expansion.

items.title: Can Synopsys' AI Push Drive Chip Design Efficiency and Growth?
items.summary: Synopsys (SNPS) is capitalizing on rising demand for advanced chip design tools by integrating AI agents across its EDA portfolio to automate engineering workflows. The company reported 82% recurring revenues, a $10.9 billion backlog, and raised fiscal 2026 guidance to $9.69-$9.74 billion. However, SNPS faces competitive pressures from Cadence and Keysight, elevated debt from the Ansys acquisition, and trades at a premium valuation of 7.53X forward P/S versus the industry average of 6.27X.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Innventure, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) and its officers for alleged securities fraud. The complaint alleges that the company made false and misleading statements regarding its subsidiary Accelsius's deal with DarkNX, claiming the transformative deal was unlikely to materialize and that revenue targets for 2026 were not reasonably plausible. Investors who purchased Innventure securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 are encouraged to join the case.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has 69% of Berkshire Hathaway's Portfolio Invested in Just 5 Stocks. Here's My Top Pick for October.
items.summary: Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO, has concentrated the portfolio into 5 stocks representing 69% of holdings, down from 42 to 29 total positions. Abel has aggressively increased Alphabet holdings from 2% to 9.4% in just one year, similar to how Warren Buffett built Apple into the largest position. Despite high capital expenditures, Alphabet's attractive 16x P/E ratio and $514 billion cloud backlog make it an appealing investment during the AI boom.

items.title: Generac to Report Q3 Earnings: Should Investors Hold or Fold?
items.summary: Generac (GNRC) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on Oct. 28 with expected revenue growth of 17.9% to $1.31 billion. The company's data center business is accelerating with a $1.6 billion backlog and a major $2.4 billion Amazon supply deal, but residential segment weakness, margin pressures from product mix, and capacity expansion execution risks warrant caution. The stock has underperformed its industry over the past six months.

items.title: EQT Is Building a $50 Billion Natural Gas Giant as AI Power Demand Surges
items.summary: EQT is acquiring Range Resources in an all-stock deal to create a $50 billion natural gas giant, positioning itself as the largest U.S. gas producer with over 9 Bcfe/d production capacity. The merger is driven by surging AI data center power demand, with EQT strategically locking in long-term supply agreements at premium prices. However, the company faces risks from potential AI infrastructure slowdown.

items.title: Intel and TSMC Are Vying for Chip Fabrication Supremacy. 1 Offers Superior Value.
items.summary: While Intel's foundry business is showing growth momentum with recent government and Nvidia investments, TSMC remains the superior value investment. Intel's foundry division operates at a 36% loss with a forward P/E of 44x, compared to TSMC's 59% operating margin and 18x P/E ratio. Despite Intel's turnaround narrative gaining market attention, TSMC's profitability and valuation make it the more attractive choice for investors.

items.title: HPE vs. AGYS: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is positioned as the superior value investment compared to Agilysys (AGYS) based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook. HPE has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 14.88 and PEG ratio of 0.44, while AGYS carries a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 50.08 and PEG ratio of 2.50. HPE received a Value grade of B versus AGYS's F grade.

items.title: Adobe vs. Datadog: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Adobe and Datadog represent two different investment approaches in cloud software: Adobe offers established profitability with a 30% net margin and $9.9B free cash flow at an 11.1x forward P/E, while Datadog delivers rapid 27.7% revenue growth but trades at a premium 101.7x forward P/E with minimal profitability. Adobe suits value-focused investors prioritizing profits and affordability, while Datadog appeals to growth-oriented investors willing to pay for expansion potential.

items.title: Xylem Gears Up to Post Q3 Earnings: What's in the Cards?
items.summary: Xylem Inc. (XYL) is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 27, with revenue expected to grow only 0.4% to $2.28 billion and earnings per share projected at $1.47 (up 7.3% YoY). While infrastructure demand, data-center growth, and the TriOS acquisition support revenues, project delays, rising costs, and inflationary pressures cloud the outlook. The company carries a negative Earnings ESP of -1.27% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), suggesting limited likelihood of beating consensus estimates.

items.title: Citigroup Lifts 2026 RoTCE Outlook: What's Fueling the Optimism?
items.summary: Citigroup raised its 2026 return on tangible common equity (RoTCE) outlook to above 11% from 10-11%, driven by strong Q3 results with 11.5% RoTCE. Services and Wealth revenues grew 15% each, while the efficiency ratio improved to 58.5%. The company targets 11-13% RoTCE for 2027-2028 and 14-15% medium-term, supported by ongoing restructuring and operational improvements.

items.title: WCN Stock Gains 11% After Reporting Q3 Earnings & Revenue Beat
items.summary: Waste Connections (WCN) exceeded Q3 earnings and revenue expectations, driven by 5.5% core pricing growth, 3% landfill volume increase, and stronger recycling revenues. The company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $10.09B and increased its quarterly dividend by 10%, causing shares to gain 10.9% post-earnings.

items.title: Investors Are Avoiding This Industry Like the Plague. Berkshire Is Going All In. Should You Invest?
items.summary: The U.S. housing industry is struggling with pending home sales down 7.3% month-over-month and 11.3% year-over-year, causing investors to flee homebuilder stocks. However, Berkshire Hathaway is making significant investments in the sector, including acquiring Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion and increasing its stake in Lennar to 11%. Berkshire CEO Greg Abel views the 10-million-home housing shortage as a long-term opportunity, though he cautions recovery won't be quick. The article suggests ordinary investors should consider buying Berkshire shares rather than directly investing in homebuilders given the volatility and patience required.

items.title: Netflix Co-CEO Greg Peters Just Said "We Know That We Can Do Better" When It Comes to U.S. Engagement. Should Investors Be Worried?
items.summary: Netflix reported Q3 earnings ahead of consensus but disappointed investors with lower full-year revenue guidance. Co-CEO Greg Peters acknowledged the company can improve U.S. engagement, citing it as an opportunity rather than a crisis. While engagement is strong in Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and EMEA regions, the U.S. market shows softer trends. The stock has declined 47% over the past year amid investor concerns about competition from short-form content and potential AI disruption to content creation costs.

items.title: Gen Digital to Report Q2 Earnings: What's in the Cards for the Stock?
items.summary: Gen Digital (GEN) is scheduled to report Q2 FY2027 results on Oct. 28, expecting revenues of $1.325-$1.350 billion and EPS of 71-73 cents. The company has blocked over 500 million scam attacks in Q1 and its Engine Marketplace reached a $500 million revenue run rate. Growth is expected to be driven by sustained demand for cybersecurity solutions amid rising AI-enabled threats, expansion of AI-driven products like Norton Neo, and the Engine Marketplace's partner additions.

items.title: AXP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Guidance Hike and AI Strategy
items.summary: American Express raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.60-$17.90, driven by resilient premium customer spending, 8% billed business growth, and 17% net card fee acceleration. The company is expanding AI capabilities across its membership model and plans to cut 5% of global positions to improve efficiency and investment capacity.

items.title: Verizon Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Strong Margins, Revenues Miss
items.summary: Verizon reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.31 per share, beating estimates by 3.15%, with revenues missing expectations. The company added 406,000 postpaid phone subscribers and raised its 2026 EPS outlook to $5.04-$5.06. Strong service revenue growth, improved margins, and robust cash flow supported the results, though broadband additions slowed slightly.

items.title: Are Utilities Stocks Lagging  Consolidated Edison (ED) This Year?
items.summary: Consolidated Edison (ED) has returned 16.5% year-to-date, significantly outperforming the Utilities sector average of 1.3%. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook. Enel Chile (ENIC) is also highlighted as an outperformer in the same industry with an 8% year-to-date return.

items.title: CVS Health Q3 Earnings Preview: How to Approach the Stock?
items.summary: CVS Health is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings on Nov. 4 with modest EPS growth of 1.3% to $1.62 and revenue growth of 2.1% to $105.04 billion. While Aetna margin recovery and Government business strength are positive, the company faces headwinds from elevated medical costs, 340B pharmacy pressures, and membership declines. CVS's $20 billion technology investment and strong earnings beat history provide some optimism, though near-term challenges persist.

items.title: Verizon Communications (VZ) Q3 Earnings Surpass Estimates
items.summary: Verizon Communications reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.31 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.27, but revenues of $34.31 billion missed expectations by 1.43%. The company has underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date (9.7% vs 11.4%). With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, the stock is expected to perform in line with the market. items.title: 2 Growth Stocks to Hold for the Next Decade (Hint: These Aren’t AI Stocks)

Both companies are positioned to deliver solid long-term returns through patent protection and diversified product pipelines.

items.title: Comfort Systems: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Comfort Systems reported Q3 2026 earnings with 54% revenue growth and record $17.8 billion project backlog, providing visibility through 2028. items.title: Top Stock Reports for Apple, Berkshire Hathaway & Goldman Sachs
items.summary: Zacks Research Daily presents analysis of 16 major stocks on October 23, 2026. Apple receives a Neutral rating despite strong AI capabilities and device ecosystem, citing supply constraints and margin pressures. Berkshire Hathaway maintains Neutral stance with balanced risk-reward profile. Goldman Sachs outperforms its industry with strong earnings, though rising spending concerns remain. Additional coverage includes Texas Instruments benefiting from AI data center demand, RTX facing supply chain challenges, and various other companies with mixed outlooks.

items.title: Why Comfort Systems Plunged Today
items.summary: Comfort Systems stock fell 9.36% despite beating revenue and earnings estimates with 53.7% revenue growth and 68.6% EPS growth to $13.91. The decline was driven by CFO Bill George's retirement announcement and broader 'sell the news' sentiment among AI-related stocks, as investors worry about the sustainability of the AI data center build-out beyond 2027. The stock now trades at a reasonable 19.4x forward 2027 earnings, down 38% from its June high.

items.title: Intel Stock Has Moved an Average of 16% the Day After Its Last 3 Reports. Should You Buy Before the Next One?
items.summary: Intel stock has experienced volatile swings averaging 16% the day after its last three earnings reports, despite beating forecasts each time. The key driver of stock movement appears to be forward guidance rather than quarterly results. While Intel topped revenue expectations in April (stock surged 24%) and July (stock fell 8% despite strong results), the pattern suggests investors focus on sequential growth rates and capital spending outlooks. With the next earnings report due October 29, the fourth-quarter guidance—particularly regarding supply growth and revenue trajectory—will likely be the critical factor determining stock direction.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Alerts Investors of Duolingo, Inc. (NASDAQ: DUOL) to a Pending Securities Class Action – Deadline is December 7, 2026
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a securities class action lawsuit against Duolingo on behalf of investors who purchased stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The complaint alleges that Duolingo made false and misleading statements about the negative impact of increased ad volume, subscription upsells, and AI-generated content on daily active user growth. The stock experienced significant drops following disappointing financial results and the CFO's departure, with declines of 25%, 8.5%, and 14% on respective dates in late 2025 and early 2026.

items.title: Nokia: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Nokia reported Q3 2026 results with 9% year-over-year net sales growth, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand. AI and cloud revenue surged 123% year-over-year, representing 12% of total sales. The company raised 2027 growth guidance for Optical and IP Networks to 25%-30%, while operating margins expanded 220 basis points. Infinera acquisition synergies are materializing a year ahead of schedule, and AI radio access networks demonstrated 20% spectral efficiency gains in live tests.

items.title: Bloom Energy Stock Sinks Despite Record Revenue and a Stellar Outlook. Is It Time to Buy?
items.summary: Bloom Energy delivered record Q3 results with 138% revenue growth and raised full-year 2026 guidance to $4.5 billion (122% growth), yet its stock plunged 30% in one month. The decline appears driven by negative free cash flow of $181 million in Q3, though the author argues this reflects necessary capacity expansion to meet exploding AI data center demand. With backlog growing faster than revenue and a $25 billion financing deal from Brookfield, the article suggests the selloff may present a buying opportunity.

items.title: American Express: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: American Express reported record Q3 2026 quarterly revenues of $20 billion with 10% full-year revenue growth target. The company is restructuring to eliminate 5% of global positions ($336M charge), integrating membership rewards into AI tools, and focusing on premium creditworthy customers. A new partnership with Airbnb adds over 1 million listings to Amex Travel, positioning the company for sustained mid-teen EPS growth.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AppLovin Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims that between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026, the company made false statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

items.title: CoStar Group to Report Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: CoStar Group is set to report Q3 2026 results on Oct. 27, with expected revenues between $935-945 million (13% YoY growth) and adjusted EPS of 31-34 cents. The company's Commercial and Residential segments are expected to benefit from strong platform adoption and marketplace growth, though results may be pressured by declining Ten-X transaction revenues, Homes.com sales-force restructuring, and pricing pressures at Apartments.com. The Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat with a 0.00% Earnings ESP and Rank #2.

items.title: SOAR AI Details Expansion Roadmap and Phased Financing Plans
items.summary: SOAR AI announced a major AI infrastructure expansion strategy following its merger and rebranding, securing $1.2 billion in contracted orders from a major customer. The company plans to deploy over 16,000 GPUs across its Ohio campus by 2027, with expected revenues of $175-200 million in 2027 and up to $294 million annually once fully operational. Expansion will be financed through customer prepayments, equipment financing, and debt.

items.title: The AI Rout: Sorting CAPEX Fact From Fiction
items.summary: AI stocks have experienced significant pullbacks amid concerns over CoreWeave's debt sustainability, with bonds yielding distressed 15% rates. However, betting markets suggest bankruptcy fears are overblown, and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence in neocloud financing solutions. Despite corrections, hyperscaler CAPEX spending continues accelerating, with Goldman Sachs projecting growth from $768B in 2026 to $1.182T in 2027, supporting the bullish fundamental case for AI.

items.title: Hubbell Incorporated Declares a 7% Dividend Increase
items.summary: Hubbell Incorporated's Board of Directors announced a 7% increase in its common stock dividend rate, raising the annual payment from $5.68 to $6.08 per share ($1.52 quarterly). The dividend will be paid on December 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of November 30, 2026.

items.title: Verisk Comments on Delaware Supreme Court Order Regarding AccuLynx
items.summary: Verisk announced it will comply with the Delaware Supreme Court's affirmation of the Delaware Chancery Court's judgment regarding the AccuLynx transaction. The company stated the deal remains subject to customary closing conditions and FTC review with no guarantee of completion. Verisk reaffirmed its commitment to serving the global insurance industry.

items.title: Comfort Systems Q3 Earnings & Revenues Beat Estimates, Backlog Surges
items.summary: Comfort Systems USA (FIX) delivered impressive Q3 2026 results with earnings surging 68.6% to $13.91 per share and revenues jumping 53.7% to $3.77 billion, driven by strong technology sector demand. The company's backlog soared 90% to $17.81 billion, and operating income climbed 64.8%. However, shares fell over 6% after-hours due to absent forward guidance and CFO transition concerns. Other construction sector peers showed mixed results, with United Rentals beating expectations while KB Home and Lennar underperformed.

items.title: SOLV Wins FDA Clearance to Combine Restrata Matrix With V.A.C.Therapy
items.summary: Solventum Corporation (SOLV) received FDA 510(k) clearance for combining its Restrata Synthetic Electrospun Fiber Matrix with V.A.C. Therapy for advanced wound care. The clearance strengthens SOLV's competitive position in the advanced wound care market, which is projected to reach $19.32 billion by 2030. The combined therapy may reduce dressing changes, streamline workflows, and support recurring revenue growth, though commercial impact depends on market adoption.

items.title: Top 3 Crypto & Blockchain Stocks to Watch as Digital Finance Expands
items.summary: Cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology are transforming financial infrastructure beyond trading, with applications in digital payments, tokenized securities, and automated settlement. Institutional adoption is growing, with 86% of surveyed institutional investors using or interested in stablecoins and 73% planning to increase digital-asset allocations. Regulatory clarity from the GENIUS Act is expected to encourage broader financial institution participation. Three key players—Robinhood Markets, Circle Internet Group, and Figure Technology Solutions—are positioned to benefit through their respective digital-asset platforms, stablecoin networks, and blockchain-powered lending markets.

items.title: BE Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Product Sales, View Up
items.summary: Bloom Energy (BE) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 76 cents per share, beating estimates by 35.71%, with revenues surging 138.1% to $1.236 billion. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $4.4-$4.6 billion and earnings guidance to $3.10-$3.40 per share, reflecting improved margins and expanding customer backlog.

items.title: C.H. Robinson Gears Up for Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: C.H. Robinson is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 28, with consensus estimates projecting 22.86% earnings growth and 9.84% revenue growth. However, the company faces headwinds from elevated truckload spot costs, contractual margin pressures, soft freight demand, and rising insurance expenses. items.title: Cintas (CTAS) Up 13.3% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?

items.title: Constellation Energy vs. GE Vernova: Which Utilities Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

items.title: American Express Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Card Fees

items.title: HWM vs. ATI: Which Aerospace & Defense Stock Has More Upside Potential?

items.title: FMS Launches multiFiltratePRO System for U.S. Patients With Acute AKI
items.summary: Fresenius Medical Care (FMS) announced the U.S. launch of its FDA-cleared multiFiltratePRO System for treating acute kidney injury in critically ill patients. The integrated continuous kidney replacement therapy system automates regional citrate anticoagulation procedures in ICUs. FMS stock gained 3.1% following the announcement. The company plans a phased U.S. rollout targeting growth in the hospital-based acute kidney care market, with the global CRRT market expected to grow at 8.2% CAGR through 2034.

items.title: U.S. Stock Futures Fall on AI Trade Concerns
items.summary: Stock futures declined in pre-market trading as Meta's AI infrastructure concerns spooked markets, affecting tech and industrial stocks. items.title: Deckers' Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Margins, Revenues Miss

DECK lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $5.70-$5.725 billion while raising EPS guidance to $7.80-$7.95, citing softer consumer demand and reduced growth expectations for both HOKA and UGG brands.

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. This Little-Known Chip Stock Is the AI Boom's Best-Kept Secret.
items.summary: Credo Technology Group (CRDO) designs connectivity chips and active electrical cables that link AI accelerators in data centers. In October 2026, Credo unveiled a 1.6-terabit optical cable using silicon photonics technology acquired from DustPhotonics, positioning itself for a transition from copper to optical connectivity in data centers.

items.title: Nokia Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Growth and 2027 Outlook
items.summary: Nokia reported Q3 2026 earnings beating estimates with AI and cloud sales surging 123% year-over-year. items.title: Salesforce vs. Snowflake: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

items.title: HON Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Outlook and Energy Demand

items.summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings of $2.00 per share (up 1%) and revenues of $23.28 billion (up 4%), both beating estimates. items.title: Ciena vs. Nokia: Which Optical Networking Stock is the Better Buy?

items.title: Western Digital: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Western Digital reported 55% year-over-year revenue growth to $4.4 billion in Q1 FY2027, driven by expanding cloud storage demand from AI. The company is leveraging ePMR technology to increase storage capacity without additional factory investments, expanded gross margins to 58% through higher-capacity drives and pricing discipline, and has improved customer visibility through 2030 as AI workloads drive demand across cloud, enterprise, and neocloud markets.

items.title: Newmont: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Newmont reported $1.9 billion in free cash flow for Q3 2026 and reduced its full-year gold production cost guidance by 10% to $1,520 per ounce. items.summary: Warren Buffett's cautionary stance on IPOs is examined through historical performance data. items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has 32% of Berkshire Hathaway's $364 Billion Portfolio Invested in 3 Unstoppable AI Stocks
items.summary: Greg Abel, who took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway after Warren Buffett's retirement on Dec. 31, has significantly shifted the company's investment strategy toward technology and AI stocks. Nearly $116 billion (32%) of Berkshire's $364 billion portfolio is now concentrated in three AI-focused companies: Apple ($78.28 billion), Alphabet ($36 billion), and Bending Spoons ($1.44 billion). Both are Dividend Kings with reliable payout histories.

items.title: INV DEADLINE NOTICE: ROSEN, SKILLED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Innventure, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 27 Deadline in Securities Class Action - INV
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces a securities class action lawsuit against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) for investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding Accelsius Holdings LLC's transformative deal with DarkNX, which was unlikely to materialize, and overstated revenue and cash flow targets for 2026. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 27, 2026.

items.title: Why Intel Stock Fell Today
items.summary: Intel stock fell 8.1% on October 22, 2026, as rising oil prices above $112/barrel and concerns about AI infrastructure funding weighed on chip stocks. Meta's report of negative free cash flow and aggressive capex spending raised questions about how companies will finance the AI build-out, threatening sustained demand for Intel's chips.

items.title: The Cooper Companies, Inc. Investor News: If You Have Suffered Losses in The Cooper Companies, Inc., You Are Encouraged to Contact The Rosen Law Firm About Your Rights
items.summary: The Rosen Law Firm is investigating potential securities claims against The Cooper Companies, Inc. following a 14.6% stock decline on September 10, 2026, after disappointing earnings guidance and a decision not to sell Cooper Surgical. Investors who purchased Cooper Companies securities may be eligible for compensation through a class action lawsuit.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 22: Netflix Rises as Investors Capitalize on Post-Earnings Sell-Off
items.summary: Netflix stock rose 3.09% on Oct. 22 as investors bought the dip following a sharp post-earnings sell-off. The company reported stronger-than-expected Q3 EPS and operating margins, but disappointed with softer Q4 guidance and reduced 2026 ad revenue targets. Netflix's aggressive capital return program, including a record $4.8 billion stock buyback, supported investor confidence despite broader market weakness.

items.title: Up 3,700%, Should You Buy Sandisk Right Now?
items.summary: Sandisk stock has surged 3,700% since its February 2025 spinoff from Western Digital, driven by AI-driven demand for flash storage and strong financial performance. However, the article cautions investors that memory and storage stocks are historically volatile and prone to severe downturns when industry cycles turn, suggesting the current boom may not be sustainable.

items.title: Why Waste Connections Stock Is Up Today
items.summary: Waste Connections stock surged 10.74% after the garbage hauler reported strong Q3 results with 7% revenue growth to $2.6 billion and raised its full-year financial guidance. The company boosted its quarterly dividend by 10% to $0.385 per share, marking its sixteenth consecutive annual increase. Strong pricing power in exclusive markets and a growth-through-acquisition strategy helped offset rising fuel costs.

items.title: Honeywell Aerospace Shareholder Alert: ClaimsFiler Reminds Investors With Losses In Excess Of $100,000 Of Lead Plaintiff Deadline In Class Action Lawsuit Against Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. - HONA
items.summary: Honeywell Aerospace faces a securities class action lawsuit alleging failure to disclose material information including supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, potential false Claims Act violations related to cybersecurity requirements, and misleading statements about business prospects. Investors with losses exceeding $100,000 must file lead plaintiff applications by October 30, 2026.

items.title: Duolingo Shareholder Alert: ClaimsFiler Reminds Investors With Losses In Excess Of $100,000 Of Lead Plaintiff Deadline In Class Action Lawsuit Against Duolingo, Inc. - DUOL
items.summary: Duolingo is facing a securities class action lawsuit alleging that the company and its executives failed to disclose that they deliberately added friction to the user experience through increased ads, subscription upselling, and declining product quality to drive users away. The lawsuit also claims that Duolingo's AI-generated content was degrading product quality and harming user retention, contrary to public statements about growth and improvements. Investors with losses exceeding $100,000 have until December 7, 2026 to file lead plaintiff applications.

items.title: DaVita Stock Gains 55.6% Year to Date: What's Behind the Rally?
items.summary: DaVita (DVA) shares have gained 55.6% year-to-date, outpacing industry growth, driven by better operating execution, improved treatment-volume outlook, and growing confidence in value-based kidney care. The company reaffirmed 2026 guidance with expected earnings growth of 50.6% on 3.2% sales growth, supported by higher revenue per treatment and labor productivity gains. However, risks include insurance-mix headwinds from ACA subsidy losses, rising patient-care costs, and uncertain Medicare reimbursement policies.

items.title: BDX Stock Gains 25.5% in Six Months: What's Behind the Rally?
items.summary: Becton, Dickinson and Company (BDX) has gained 25.5% over six months, driven by successful portfolio realignment following its Life Sciences separation, strong earnings growth across high-growth platforms, and a major $19 billion U.S. manufacturing partnership agreement. The company raised its fiscal 2026 EPS guidance and returned $3.1 billion to shareholders, though it faces headwinds from tariffs, Alaris remediation, and China vaccine weakness.

items.title: DGX Q3 Earnings & Revenues Beat, '26 View Raised, Stock Down in Pre-Market
items.summary: Quest Diagnostics (DGX) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.00 per share (up 15.4% YoY) and revenues of $3.10 billion (up 10% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12.065-$12.105 billion and adjusted EPS outlook to $11.25-$11.35. Despite strong results, DGX shares fell 1.6% in pre-market trading. Operating margins improved 40 basis points to 16.7%, driven by strong testing demand and organic requisition volume growth of 14.4%.

items.title: Valero Energy Q3 Earnings Top Estimates on Refining Strength
items.summary: Valero Energy (VLO) reported exceptional third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS surging 553% to $23.90 and revenues jumping 43.3% to $46.10 billion. The company benefited from substantially stronger refining margins, particularly in gasoline and distillate products, with refining margin per barrel reaching $39.24. Renewable diesel and ethanol segments also showed improved profitability, while operating cash flow hit $6.93 billion.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alphabet Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding Gemini 3.5 Pro, claiming the AI model delivered disappointing training results and would face significant launch delays. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026. Investors have until December 1, 2026 to request lead plaintiff status.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bank of America Corporation alleging the bank made false and misleading statements regarding its Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering compliance program. The complaint claims BAC failed to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions, missed or delayed suspicious activity reports, and had unaddressed compliance deficiencies despite a 2024 Consent Order. Investors who purchased BAC securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 15, 2026.

items.title: NextEra Energy: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: NextEra Energy announced Q3 2026 results targeting the high end of its earnings guidance, driven by surging electricity demand from data centers and electrification. The company added 3.7 gigawatts of renewables to its backlog, achieved over two-thirds of its 2026-2029 development targets, and recontracted 1,400 megawatts of renewables at a $20/MWh premium. NextEra's fee-based federal hubs strategy allows it to monetize data center demand without capital risk, while the pending Dominion Energy merger is expected to close in H2 2027.

items.title: Tractor Supply Q3 Earnings Beat on Sales Growth, Margins Fall
items.summary: Tractor Supply (TSCO) reported Q3 2026 earnings of 43 cents per share, down 11.6% YoY but beating consensus estimates. Net sales rose 5.1% to $3.91 billion, driven by new stores and the VIP Petcare acquisition. However, gross margins contracted 100 bps due to higher transportation costs and price investments. The company reaffirmed 2026 guidance projecting 2.5-3.5% net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $1.90-$2.00, while comparable-store sales are expected to range from -1% to flat.

items.title: Crown Castle's Q3 AFFO Beats Estimates on Lower Expenses
items.summary: Crown Castle (CCI) reported Q3 2026 AFFO per share of $1.24, up 10.7% YoY and beating estimates by 3.3%, benefiting from lower interest costs. However, revenues fell 7.2% to $995 million due to DISH terminations and Sprint cancellations impacting site rentals. The company raised its 2026 AFFO and EBITDA guidance, with AFFO now expected between $1.955-$2.005 billion.

items.title: UNP Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Volume Growth, Pricing Gains
items.summary: Union Pacific (UNP) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.53 per share, beating consensus by 1.7%, with revenues rising 15.3% to $7.20 billion. Freight revenues grew 14.9% driven by higher carloads and pricing gains, though fuel expenses surged 68.8%. The company maintains high-single-digit EPS growth outlook for 2026. Other transportation companies showed mixed results: Alaska Air Group beat earnings estimates but faced fuel headwinds, Wabtec beat earnings but missed revenue targets, and J.B. Hunt exceeded both earnings and revenue expectations.

items.title: Globe Life Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Weak Underwriting Income
items.summary: Globe Life reported Q3 2026 operating EPS of $4.84, slightly missing estimates but growing 0.6% year-over-year. Premium revenues rose 6.5%, but underwriting income fell 4.2% and expenses surged 11.5%, pressuring profitability. The company revised its 2026 EPS guidance downward to $15.35-$15.65 due to adverse results at United American, while raising share repurchase forecasts. Book value per share increased 22.8% year-over-year.

items.title: Prediction: Sandisk Stock Will Soar After Oct. 29. Here Are 379 Billion Reasons Why
items.summary: Sandisk stock has declined 32% since July despite strong fundamentals, as investors worry about AI infrastructure sustainability. However, the article argues the selloff is unjustified given robust NAND flash demand, expected 357% revenue growth in fiscal Q1, and a $379 billion addressable market opportunity in 2027. With the stock trading at just 8x forward earnings versus the S&P 500's 19x multiple, the author expects stronger-than-expected results on Oct. 29 could trigger a significant rally.

items.title: ROL's Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Weak Demand & Higher Costs
items.summary: Rollins, Inc. reported disappointing Q3 2026 results with earnings declining 2.9% year-over-year to 34 cents per share, missing consensus estimates. While revenues grew 6.2% to $1.09 billion, operating margins contracted 140 basis points to 20.5% due to rising costs and weak residential customer acquisition. Commercial and termite operations provided growth, but profitability suffered. The company is restructuring its marketing strategy and generated strong free cash flow of $235.5 million, up 28.8% year-over-year.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Innventure, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. and its officers for alleged securities fraud. The complaint alleges that the company made false statements about its subsidiary Accelsius's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly lacked evidence of feasibility, and that revenue and cash targets for 2026 were not reasonably plausible. Investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 may be eligible to join the case.

items.title: LUV Q3 Earnings Beat on Record Revenues and Higher Fares
items.summary: Southwest Airlines (LUV) delivered exceptional Q3 2026 results with adjusted EPS surging 500% to 66 cents, beating estimates by 8.2%, and record revenues reaching $8.42 billion. Strong pricing power drove a 26.9% jump in average fares, though passenger volumes declined 3.2%. Despite a 61.7% surge in fuel costs, the airline expanded operating margins to 5.4%. The company provided Q4 guidance of 55-80 cents EPS and full-year 2026 guidance of $2.60-$2.85 EPS.

items.title: HON Q3 Earnings Beat on Automation Strength, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Honeywell Technologies (HON) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.27, beating estimates of $2.17, with 34% year-over-year growth. Organic sales grew 7% across all segments. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.40-$8.45 and free cash flow expectations to $2.1 billion, driven by strength in building automation, industrial measurement, and process automation projects.

items.title: ROP Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Solid Organic Growth
items.summary: Roper Technologies reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.89, beating estimates by 1.7% with 15% year-over-year growth. Organic revenues grew 7%, driven by strong performance across all three segments, particularly Technology Enabled Products which grew 10%. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $22.35-$22.40 and expects revenue growth above 8%.

items.title: ALLE Q3 Earnings Beat on Americas Strength, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Allegion plc (ALLE) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $2.60 per share, up 13% YoY and beating estimates by 4.4%, with revenues growing 9.6% to $1.17 billion. The Americas segment drove growth with 11.7% revenue increase on strong non-residential demand. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.05-$9.10 and revenue growth outlook to 9.5-10.5%, reflecting confidence in continued momentum.

items.title: AMG or BLK: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a value investor comparison, Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) emerges as the more attractive option compared to BlackRock (BLK). AMG holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook, a lower forward P/E of 10.68 versus BLK's 20.00, and a superior PEG ratio of 0.50 compared to BLK's 1.20. AMG also has a better Value grade of B versus BLK's F grade.

items.title: BGC vs. EVR: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of two Financial-Investment Bank sector stocks reveals BGC Group as the superior value opportunity. BGC holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 8.30 and PEG ratio of 0.42, while Evercore carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) with a forward P/E of 13.86 and PEG ratio of 1.14. BGC's improving earnings outlook and stronger valuation metrics make it the preferred choice for value investors.

items.title: United Rentals Tops Q3 Earnings & Revenue Estimates, Raises 2026 View
items.summary: United Rentals (URI) delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS surging 32.9% to $15.55 and revenues rising 15.7% to $4.89 billion, both beating consensus estimates. The specialty rental segment led growth with a 34.7% revenue jump and 250 bps margin expansion. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $18-$18.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $8.3-$8.4 billion, citing strong customer confidence and large-project momentum.

items.title: Lockheed Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Sales Increase Year Over Year
items.summary: Lockheed Martin reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $7.97, beating consensus estimates by 6.4%, with sales climbing 11.3% to $20.71 billion. The company's backlog surged to $291.98 billion, driven by strong performance in Missiles and Fire Control (up 24% YoY). LMT raised its 2026 full-year sales guidance to $80-$82 billion and adjusted EPS outlook to $30.35-$30.75.

items.title: KMI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Natural Gas Pipeline Strength
items.summary: Kinder Morgan (KMI) beat Q3 2026 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of 35 cents (up 20.7% YoY) and revenues of $4.53 billion (up 9.3% YoY). The company achieved record EBITDA of $2.18 billion, driven by higher natural gas transportation and gathering volumes. With a $14.4 billion project backlog and improved 2026 guidance expecting EBITDA to exceed budget by over 6%, KMI raised its quarterly dividend by 2%.

items.title: AutoZone (AZO) Up 11% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: AutoZone reported Q4 fiscal 2026 EPS of $56.05, beating consensus estimates by 2.8%, driven by gross margin expansion. However, net sales missed expectations at $6.60 billion. The company expanded its store footprint to 8,031 locations and maintained strong commercial business momentum. Despite the earnings beat, estimates have been trending downward in the past month, and the stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with an aggregate VGM Score of D.

items.title: Costco's Last Stock Split Was in 2000. Is Its Board Close to Another?
items.summary: Costco's stock price has reached ~$994 per share since its last 2-for-1 split in January 2000, prompting investor questions about another split. However, CEO Ron Vachris and CFO Gary Millerchip have repeatedly stated there are no immediate plans, citing that fractional share purchases now make splits less economically necessary. The company continues to review the possibility with its board, but the author believes a split is unlikely in the near term and suggests a special dividend would be more beneficial to shareholders.

items.title: SpaceX Just Became an AI Company. The Numbers Prove It.
items.summary: SpaceX's AI segment (called 'super intelligence') generated $7.6 billion in Q3 revenue, up 830% year-over-year, becoming the company's largest revenue source at over 50% of sales. The segment turned profitable with $431 million in operating income after losing $1.26 billion last quarter, driven by cloud services agreements with Alphabet and Anthropic, plus the Cursor acquisition contribution of $608 million in just 6.5 weeks.

items.title: Is IBM Worth Buying as Software Growth Meets a Premium Valuation?
items.summary: IBM's software segment demonstrated solid growth with 9% revenue increase and 8% recurring revenue growth to $24.9 billion in Q3 2026. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation of 19.28X forward earnings versus its 5-year median of 17.3X. While free cash flow improved and software momentum is positive, weak consulting growth of just 2%, elevated debt of $63.8 billion, and challenges in converting AI backlog into revenue limit the investment case. IBM holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Snowflake vs. Broadcom: Which Enterprise AI Stock Is the Smarter Buy?
items.summary: Snowflake and Broadcom are both major players in the enterprise AI boom, but Snowflake emerges as the stronger pick. Snowflake benefits from accelerating product revenue growth (37% YoY), strong customer expansion, and high earnings surprises (22.77% average), earning a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Broadcom, despite impressive AI semiconductor revenue growth (221% YoY), faces headwinds from customer concentration, margin pressure, debt burden, and execution risks, warranting a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

items.title: LVS Q3 Earnings & Revenues Miss on Soft Premium Gaming & Higher Costs
items.summary: Las Vegas Sands (LVS) reported disappointing third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS of 54 cents missing estimates by 23.9% and revenues declining 3.5% year-over-year to $3.22 billion. Softer premium gaming demand in Macao and Singapore, combined with elevated operating expenses, drove property EBITDA down 16.7%. Despite the weak results, the company approved a 20% dividend increase and repurchased $950 million in shares.

items.title: GEHC Expands Theranostics Imaging With 5 Global Collaborations
items.summary: GE HealthCare announced five new global clinical collaborations to evaluate its StarGuide GX digital SPECT/CT system, a next-generation nuclear medicine imaging platform using advanced detector technology and NVIDIA computing. The system has received CE Mark approval in Europe but awaits FDA clearance in the US. The collaborations with leading institutions aim to advance quantitative imaging, dynamic imaging, and theranostics applications, supporting GEHC's competitive positioning in the growing precision oncology market.

items.title: Packaging Corp Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Favorable Price & Mix
items.summary: Packaging Corporation of America (PKG) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.04, beating consensus estimates and guidance, driven by favorable pricing in the Packaging segment and contributions from the Greif acquisition. Net sales rose 12.5% year-over-year to $2.6B with gross margin expansion to 23.2%. However, the company faces headwinds from higher labor, operating, and freight costs. Q4 guidance of $2.81 EPS reflects anticipated maintenance expenses and seasonal pressures.

items.title: Oil Prices Climb: 3 Energy Stocks Poised to Benefit From the Rally
items.summary: With crude oil prices climbing amid geopolitical tensions, three major energy companies—Chevron, Diamondback Energy, and APA Corporation—are positioned to benefit from higher oil prices. Chevron reported 20% production growth and record refinery throughput, Diamondback generated $2.3 billion in free cash flow with raised 2026 guidance, and APA exceeded oil production guidance with $738 million in free cash flow. However, benefits depend on production volumes, operating costs, and hedging strategies.

items.title: Nokia's Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI & Cloud Strength
items.summary: Nokia exceeded Q3 2026 earnings estimates by 29.45% with revenues up 10% YoY to €5.15 billion, driven by robust AI & Cloud demand surging 123%. IP Networks grew 43% and Optical Networks 18%. However, the company lowered its free cash flow conversion forecast to 35-55% from 55-75% due to working capital investments and restructuring costs. Nokia maintained its 2026 operating profit outlook of €2.1-€2.6 billion.

items.title: PHM Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Lower Closings & Margins
items.summary: PulteGroup (PHM) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.53 per share, missing consensus estimates and declining 14.5% year-over-year. Revenues fell 9.8% to $3.97 billion, driven by lower home closings (down 8.7%), softer average selling prices, and margin compression to 24.8%. While net new orders declined 6.5%, backlog improved 4.1% to 10,298 homes valued at $6.44 billion. The company faces persistent housing affordability challenges and rising mortgage rates.

items.title: ROAD's Florida Expansion: Can Infrastructure Demand Drive Growth?
items.summary: Construction Partners, Inc. (ROAD) acquired P&S Paving to expand its Florida footprint and strengthen its position along the I-95 corridor. The company secured $80M in Florida DOT contracts and achieved a record backlog of $3.36B with 28.2% quarterly revenue growth. However, rising energy costs, weather disruptions, and acquisition integration risks pose challenges. ROAD stock has declined 30.2% over six months and carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

items.title: TXN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Analog, Data Center Demand
items.summary: Texas Instruments (TXN) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.62 per share, up 77% year-over-year and beating estimates by 9.2%. Revenues surged 28% to $6.06B, driven by strong growth in analog (32%), data center (95%), and industrial (40%+) segments. Operating margins expanded to 47.5%, and the company raised its dividend by 7% for the 23rd consecutive year. Q4 guidance ranges from $5.80B to $6.30B in revenues.

items.title: LRCX Q1 Earnings Call Highlights $200B-Plus WFE Outlook for 2027
items.summary: Lam Research (LRCX) projects wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending will exceed $200 billion in 2027, driven by AI demand and chip manufacturing complexity. The company guided December-quarter revenues to $8.6B and raised its Aether dry resist technology revenue outlook to $2.5B by decade-end. Supply chain constraints are impacting near-term shipments, though customer demand visibility extends through 2028.

items.title: Can PepsiCo's $3.5B Multipack Business Support Snack Growth?
items.summary: PepsiCo is strengthening its North American snacks business through portion-controlled formats and innovation, with volumes improving to low-single-digit growth in 2026. Keurig Dr Pepper and Coca-Cola are leveraging product innovation, affordable packaging, and portfolio diversification to drive growth amid consumer spending pressures. However, PepsiCo faces persistent margin headwinds and rising input costs, with its stock rated a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

items.title: Procter & Gamble Q1 Earnings Beat on Volume Growth & Favorable Mix
items.summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported Q1 FY27 core EPS of $2.00, up 1% YoY and beating consensus estimates of $1.89. Net sales rose 4% to $23.28B with 4% organic sales growth driven by volume and favorable mix. The company raised FY27 sales guidance to 2-4% but maintained core EPS guidance of $6.89-$7.11. Core operating margins contracted 80 bps due to elevated commodity costs and product reinvestments, despite 250 bps in productivity savings.

items.title: How to Approach Genuine Parts Stock Post its Q3 Earnings Release
items.summary: Genuine Parts Company (GPC) continues to struggle with elevated operating expenses, geopolitical disruptions, and uneven automotive demand that are offsetting gross margin gains. The Iran conflict reduced Q3 2026 EBITDA by $16 million, while the planned 2027 separation of its Automotive and Industrial businesses is expected to add $350 million in annual corporate costs, raising execution risks.

items.title: Lam Research Q1 Earnings Beat on Systems Sales and Margin Gains
items.summary: Lam Research (LRCX) delivered exceptional Q1'27 results with EPS of $2.20 (up 74.6% YoY) and revenues of $8.22B (up 54.4% YoY), beating consensus estimates. Systems revenues surged 61.6% driven by strong NAND and foundry demand, while gross margin hit a record 52.4%. The company generated record free cash flow of $3.24B and projects Q2 EPS of $2.33, with expectations for wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200B in 2027.

items.title: Investing in Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks Can be Risky, but This Might be a Great Way to Do It
items.summary: AI stocks have delivered strong returns but face rising volatility as investors question the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. The iShares Future AI and Tech ETF (ARTY) offers diversified exposure to 50 leading AI companies across infrastructure, software, and services. While the ETF has surged 130% since its August 2024 restructure, investors should be cautious about concentration risk and its higher 0.47% expense ratio compared to passive index funds.

items.title: Dutch Bros vs. Chipotle Mexican Grill: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Dutch Bros and Chipotle Mexican Grill represent different investment strategies in the consumer discretionary sector. Dutch Bros offers faster growth (27.9% revenue growth) but trades at a higher valuation (44.7x forward P/E) with improving profitability. Chipotle provides established scale, stronger profitability (12.9% net margin), and lower valuation (26.0x forward P/E) but slower growth (5.4% revenue growth). The article suggests Dutch Bros may appeal to growth-focused investors as it closes the profitability gap, while Chipotle suits value-oriented investors seeking stability.

items.title: History Says This Will Happen to Sandisk Stock Heading Into Its Oct. 29 Report
items.summary: Sandisk stock has surged 478% in 2026 driven by extraordinary demand for NAND flash memory from AI data centers, where supply remains critically scarce. The company reports Q1 fiscal 2027 results on Oct. 29, with management guiding for $10.5B revenue (357% YoY growth) and $45 EPS. Historically, the stock has climbed before earnings reports since its February 2025 spinoff from Western Digital, though recent patterns show volatility as investors worry about the inevitable memory cycle downturn.

items.title: UNION PACIFIC ($UNP) Releases Q3 2026 Earnings - Quiver Quantitative
items.summary: UNION PACIFIC ($UNP) Releases Q3 2026 Earnings    Quiver Quantitative

items.title: Breakfast News: Tesla’s Slow Wheels, Fast Dreams
items.summary: Tesla's stock dipped despite beating earnings, as the market focuses on its pivot to AI and robotics rather than EV sales. Meta surged on AI assistant success with 26% revenue growth, while IBM stabilized mainframe demand. The broader AI sector faces headwinds with chip stocks down 15% in three weeks. Corning targets $355 per share on strong data center demand, and three companies report earnings today.

items.title: Own Starbucks by Nov. 13 to Qualify for Its Nov. 27 Dividend. Here's How Many Shares You'd Need for $500 in Yearly Dividends.
items.summary: Starbucks raised its dividend for the 16th consecutive year to $0.63 per quarter ($2.52 annualized), offering a 2.6% forward yield. Investors would need 199 shares (~$19,406) for $500 in yearly dividends. After years of flat growth, Starbucks is executing a turnaround strategy focused on restoring its 'third place' coffeehouse experience, improving margins, and operational efficiency rather than rapid expansion. The strategy is showing early success with improved same-store sales and margin expansion guidance.

items.title: Spotify (SPOT) Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates
items.summary: Spotify reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.85 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $3.1 per share, representing an 8.07% earnings surprise. While revenue of $5.72 billion slightly exceeded expectations, the company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revisions. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 22.8% year-to-date.

items.title: Honeywell International Inc. (HON) Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Honeywell International reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.27 per share, beating consensus estimates of $2.17, but revenues of $4.99 billion missed expectations by 0.42%. The stock has declined 45% year-to-date versus the S&P 500's 13.3% gain. Despite the earnings beat, the company received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating due to unfavorable estimate revision trends, suggesting underperformance ahead.

items.title: McDonald's Is 29% Below Its 52-Week High and Yields 3.2%. Is This the Best Entry Point in Years?
items.summary: McDonald's stock has declined 20.6% in 2026, trading 29% below its 52-week high, making it one of the worst Dow performers. However, the company's 3.2% dividend yield, 50-year consecutive dividend increase streak (Dividend King status), and new NEXT strategic plan focusing on AI, store revamps, and menu simplification may present a buying opportunity for patient investors seeking inflation-hedging dividend growth.

items.title: Greg Abel Says Every Point of BNSF Profit Margin Adds About $230 Million of Cash Flow for Berkshire Hathaway
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's CEO Greg Abel is targeting significant margin improvements at BNSF railroad, stating that each 1% improvement in operating margin generates approximately $230 million in incremental operating cash flow. With current 34.5% margins and competitors operating at 38-40%, BNSF has substantial room for improvement that could potentially double its contribution to Berkshire's bottom line within five years.

items.title: Nvidia Has 80% of Its Portfolio Invested in 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks
items.summary: Nvidia has concentrated 80% of its investment portfolio in two AI stocks: SpaceX (33%) and Intel (47%). SpaceX shows strong AI revenue growth with $41 billion in annual customer commitments but trades at an expensive 68x sales valuation. Intel reported its fastest quarterly growth in 15 years but continues losing market share to AMD and Arm despite strong CPU demand.

items.summary: Accenture, Hasbro, and MSCI all posted strong Q3 2026 earnings results, driving positive stock reactions. Accenture reported 6% revenue growth and exceeded guidance, Hasbro saw 15% revenue growth with Magic: The Gathering sales surpassing $600 million for the first time, and MSCI delivered record results with 12-14% growth across key metrics.

items.title: Netflix Stock Is on Track for Its Worst Year Since 2022. Is It Finally a Buy?
items.summary: Netflix stock has declined 27% in 2026, approaching its worst year since 2022, despite strong business fundamentals. The company reported Q3 revenue growth of 12% to $12.9 billion and operating income up 37%, with an operating margin of 34.6%. However, revenue growth is decelerating and the company cut its 2026 ad revenue guidance from $3 billion to $2.7 billion. At a P/E ratio of 17-18, Netflix trades in line with the S&P 500 despite double-digit revenue growth and a 35% operating margin, making it worth considering for long-term investors willing to build positions gradually.
