items.title: Boeing's Turnaround Just Hit a Pivot Point. Here's What It Means for the Entire Aerospace Supply Chain.
items.summary: Boeing's ramp-up of 737 MAX production to 52-57 aircraft per month is a critical pivot point for its turnaround and will significantly benefit its aerospace supply chain partners. CEO Kelly Ortberg confirmed the supply chain is in good shape, with production delays related to Boeing's own wing manufacturing rather than supplier issues. As Boeing clears pre-built inventory and reaches higher production rates in 2027, suppliers' revenue, cash flow, and profitability are expected to improve substantially.

items.title: Las Vegas Sands: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Las Vegas Sands reported Q3 2026 earnings with near-term softness in high-end customer visits across Asian markets, but management remains optimistic about long-term growth. The company has repurchased 19% of outstanding shares over 12 quarters, approved a 20% dividend increase for 2027, and gained gaming market share in Macao through strategic service investments and customer experience improvements.

items.title: Lam Research: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Lam Research reported record quarterly revenue and profitability driven by AI-induced semiconductor demand. The company raised its Aether dry resist technology revenue forecast by $1 billion to $2.5 billion by decade's end, expects its Customer Support Business Group to grow over 30% annually, and projects increased NAND wafer capacity needs due to AI storage architecture shifts toward single-level cell memory.

items.title: Zoom 以全新统一上下文层推进 AI 战略，让会议对话转化为工作成果
items.summary: Zoom Communications announced a new Unified Context Layer and multiple AI-powered products at its Zoomtopia 2026 conference. The platform aims to connect conversation history with relevant documents and data to help teams convert meetings into actionable outcomes. Zoom Virtual Agent customer numbers surged 256%, with users reporting doubled task completion speeds and 72% reporting high business impact. The company expects full-year revenue to exceed $5 billion.

items.title: ROSEN, SKILLED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages AppLovin Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action – APP
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying investors in AppLovin Corporation, Beta Bionics, Inc., and Netcapital Inc. about ongoing securities class action lawsuits. AppLovin investors who purchased shares between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026 must act by November 16, 2026 deadline. The lawsuit alleges AppLovin made false statements about AI video features, overstated AI model improvements, and misrepresented the benefits of its AI platform's 'virtuous cycle' value proposition.

items.title: Cathie Wood Trimmed Ark's Alphabet Stake Even as Google Search Revenue Grew, While Ark Piled Into Rocket Lab Even After Its Neutron Launch Delay. Is Ark Betting Against the Wrong AI Winner?
items.summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest is reducing its Alphabet position while increasing bets on Rocket Lab despite the latter's Neutron rocket launch delay to 2027. Alphabet shows strong AI monetization through search and cloud growth, while Rocket Lab trades at a premium valuation with significant execution risks dependent on Neutron's commercial success.

items.title: ROSEN, A LEADING INVESTOR RIGHTS LAW FIRM, Encourages Bank of America Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BAC
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a securities class action lawsuit against Bank of America Corporation on behalf of investors who purchased common stock between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Bank of America failed to disclose systemic weaknesses in its subsidiary BANA's BSA/AML compliance program, including failure to properly monitor trillions in transactions and file accurate suspicious activity reports. The firm claims defendants made materially false statements about compliance progress and expected costs, causing investor damages when the true details emerged.

items.title: Why Netflix Stock Dropped Today
items.summary: Netflix stock fell over 5% after the company cut its full-year advertising revenue forecast from $3 billion to $2.7 billion. While Q3 revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $12.9 billion and earnings per share jumped 47%, the slower growth rate and reduced ad revenue guidance disappointed investors concerned about competition from YouTube and other streaming rivals.

items.title: Brown & Brown, Inc. announces 9% increase in quarterly cash dividend rate
items.summary: Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO) announced a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.18 per share, representing a 9% increase from the previous $0.165 per share. This marks the company's 33rd consecutive annual dividend increase, payable on November 11, 2026. The insurance brokerage firm also announced it was named one of the 2026 Healthiest 100 Workplaces in America, ranking No. 25 nationally.

items.title: Q3 Earnings Beats for Meta, Tesla, IBM and T.I.
items.summary: Meta Platforms, Tesla, IBM, and Texas Instruments all beat Q3 earnings estimates. Meta reported record quarterly revenues of $64.6 billion (up 26% YoY) with EPS of $3.83, announced a 2-for-1 stock split, and raised guidance. Tesla delivered EPS of $0.48 and revenues of $28.05 billion with improved auto gross margins. IBM and Texas Instruments also exceeded consensus estimates on both earnings and revenues.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 21: AT&T Beats Earnings on Strong Fiber Growth, Raises 2026 Profit Outlook
items.summary: AT&T reported better-than-expected earnings with record internet additions and raised its 2026 profit outlook, but the stock fell 6.45% as investors focused on higher spending needs and growing competition from SpaceX's direct-to-device connectivity plans. The company also agreed to sell its Mexico wireless unit for $2 billion.

items.title: Netflix Is Down 38% Since Completing Its 10-For-1 Stock Split. Here's Why the Sell-Off Is Worsening After Its Latest Earnings.
items.summary: Netflix stock has fallen 37.9% since completing its 10-for-1 stock split in November 2025, with further declines following Q3 2026 earnings. While the company reported solid revenue growth of 11.8% and improved operating margins, it lowered full-year ad revenue guidance by 10% due to slower ad product rollout. The sell-off reflects concerns about slowing growth, increased competition from mobile-focused platforms like YouTube and TikTok, and the impact of recent price increases on price-sensitive subscribers. However, Netflix maintains a strong balance sheet with $8.19 billion in cash and trades at a relatively attractive 17x forward earnings multiple.

items.title: Deadline Alert: Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. Investors Have Until November 23, 2026 to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role in Securities Fraud Class Action, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Reminds
items.summary: Honeywell Aerospace investors have until November 23, 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status in a securities fraud class action. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased shares between June 29 and September 1, 2026. The company allegedly failed to disclose material adverse facts including supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, cybersecurity compliance issues with defense contracts, and a $2 million false Claims Act settlement. The stock fell 23.16% on August 6, 2026 following disappointing earnings and guidance cuts.

items.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific raised its full-year 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 4% following strong Q3 results with $12.14 billion in revenue and 6% organic growth. The company is leveraging AI integration to reduce manual laboratory setup time by 90%, accelerating workflows and boosting recurring sales. Strategic acquisitions like Clario are expanding clinical development capabilities and creating revenue synergies, positioning the company for durable margin expansion amid strengthening biopharmaceutical research activity.

items.title: Unveiling Cincinnati Financial (CINF) Q3 Outlook: Wall Street Estimates for Key Metrics
items.summary: Cincinnati Financial is expected to report Q3 earnings of $1.99 per share, down 30.2% year-over-year, with revenues forecast at $3.03 billion, up 5.5%. Key metrics show mixed results: investment income rising 9.6%, earned premiums up 5%, but the combined ratio deteriorating to 96.4% from 88.2%, indicating higher losses and expenses across insurance segments.

items.title: Skydance Trades at a Fraction of Netflix's Valuation. Is the Discount Deserved?
items.summary: After acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery, Skydance trades at roughly one-eighth Netflix's valuation. However, the discount appears justified given Skydance's $78.9 billion net debt (more than double its market cap), single-digit operating margins, and shrinking cable networks, compared to Netflix's clean balance sheet, powerful cash generation, and 33.4% operating margins.

items.title: 5 Strong Buy Growth Stocks With High Margins to Grab Before Earnings
items.summary: As October 2026 earnings season approaches, five companies with Zacks Rank #1 and Growth Score A ratings stand out for combining strong revenue growth with high operating margins. Chord Energy, Halozyme, Sezzle, SanDisk, and Teradyne are positioned to benefit from trends in energy, healthcare technology, digital payments, semiconductors, and AI infrastructure.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against XTI Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: XTIA) alleging that company executives made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts during the Class Period (April 15, 2026 - August 17, 2026). The complaint claims senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities that required Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to file timely earnings reports. Investors who purchased XTI Aerospace securities during this period are encouraged to join the lawsuit, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. alleging that the company made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts during the Class Period (June 29 - September 1, 2026). The complaint alleges undisclosed supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, a false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts, and that positive statements about the company lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Honeywell securities during this period are urged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 23, 2026.

items.title: Is Berkshire Hathaway's Greg Abel Is Changing the Script? Here's the Latest Tech Stock He Just Bought.
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway, under CEO Greg Abel, has expanded its investment in Bending Spoons with an additional $330 million purchase, bringing its stake to 4%. Bending Spoons is an Italian holding company that acquires and improves underperforming tech companies like Vimeo, Evernote, and AOL. While the company shows strong growth (126% revenue increase in Q2), it carries significant debt ($4.09 billion net debt). Abel's move signals a willingness to venture into tech and international opportunities beyond Berkshire's traditional industries.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims the company made false statements regarding its capital requirements, liquidity position, competitive standing in the satellite direct-to-cell market, and user adoption rates between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026. Investors have until November 13, 2026 to request lead plaintiff status.

items.title: No, I'm Not Selling You My Netflix Stock Today
items.summary: Netflix stock fell to a two-year low after Q3 earnings beat expectations but guidance disappointed. Revenue grew 11.8% to $12.87B and earnings rose 44% to $0.87/share, but Q4 guidance projects only 11.5% revenue growth and 15% earnings growth—the weakest performance in over three years. Despite six consecutive quarters of decelerating growth and key executive departures, the author maintains his long-term position, citing Netflix's historical resilience and current valuation at 17x forward earnings.

items.title: AppLovin vs. Pinterest: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares AppLovin and Pinterest as investment opportunities in the digital advertising space. AppLovin demonstrates explosive growth with 70% revenue increase, exceptional profitability (60.8% net margin), and strong free cash flow, making it the author's preferred choice. Pinterest offers a massive 640 million user base and improving AI-powered ad tools but faces challenges with lower profitability (9.9% net margin) and GAAP net losses, though it maintains a conservative balance sheet.

items.title: Wabtec Q3 Earnings Beat on Margin Expansion, Revenues Miss
items.summary: Wabtec Corporation reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.83 per share, beating consensus estimates by 4%, with revenues of $3.12 billion slightly missing expectations. The company raised its full-year 2026 earnings guidance to $10.85-$11.05 per share. Both Freight and Transit segments showed strong margin expansion (190 and 260 basis points respectively), driven by organic growth, acquisitions, and operational efficiencies. Total backlog reached $31.44 billion, up 22.9% year-over-year.

items.title: PAHC or SYK: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two medical products sector stocks reveals Phibro Animal Health (PAHC) as the superior value opportunity. PAHC holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) with a forward P/E of 11.12 and Value grade of B, while Stryker (SYK) has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with a forward P/E of 20.39 and Value grade of D. PAHC's stronger earnings outlook and more attractive valuation metrics make it the better choice for value investors.

items.title: KUBTY or DE: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two manufacturing farm equipment companies reveals that Kubota Corp. (KUBTY) presents a better value opportunity than Deere (DE) based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook. KUBTY has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 10.74 and Value grade of A, while DE has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 34.91 and Value grade of D.

items.title: CBZ vs. EFX: Which Stock Should Value Investors Buy Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two consulting services stocks reveals that CBIZ (CBZ) presents a better value opportunity than Equifax (EFX). CBZ has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook, a lower forward P/E of 13.17 versus EFX's 20.79, and a superior Value grade of A compared to EFX's C grade.

items.title: ZTS vs. ICCC: Which Animal Health Stock Is the Better Investment Bet?
items.summary: Zoetis (ZTS) and ImmuCell (ICCC) operate in animal health but with different profiles. Zoetis offers diversification across companion animals, livestock, and diagnostics but faces near-term headwinds from declining companion animal demand and reduced 2026 guidance. ImmuCell shows stronger recent growth with 20.9% sales increases and expanding market share in calf scours prevention, but carries higher execution risks due to narrow product focus and margin pressures during manufacturing expansion.

items.title: ISRG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Pricing and Growth Strategy
items.summary: Intuitive Surgical reported Q3 2026 earnings beating consensus estimates with $3.05B in revenue. The company announced planned instrument pricing reductions of 3-5% to expand robotic surgery adoption, narrowed 2026 procedure growth guidance to 14-15%, and raised gross margin outlook to 68.7-69.3%. U.S. procedure growth slowed to 10% while international placements surged 29%, with strong expansion in Europe and Asia.

items.title: ELV Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Carelon Strength, Raises 2026 Outlook
items.summary: Elevance Health reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $6.99, significantly beating estimates by 50%, with revenue reaching $50.4B. The Carelon segment drove growth with 5.4% revenue increase and 17.2% operating gain growth. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $29.00 and increased its earnings baseline to at least $26.75.

items.title: These 3 Stocks Surged Following Strong Quarterly Results
items.summary: Three major companies delivered positive Q3 earnings results. Accenture reported 6% YoY revenue growth to $18.7B with strong bookings of $22.2B. Hasbro posted 15% YoY revenue growth to $1.6B, with Magic: The Gathering sales exceeding $600M for the first time, prompting raised FY26 guidance. MSCI achieved record results with 12% YoY revenue growth to $892M and record asset-based fees, with all three stocks experiencing favorable post-earnings reactions.

items.title: Pre-Markets in Green on Strong Earnings Results
items.summary: Markets open higher ahead of major Mag 7 earnings reports. SpaceX posts impressive Q3 results with 161% revenue growth. Early morning earnings from NextEra Energy, Abbott Labs, and CME Group show mixed results, with Abbott declining on nutrition spinoff concerns. Meta and Tesla earnings expected after close, with Meta facing -52.4% earnings decline despite strong revenue growth, while Tesla carries a Sell rating heading into its report.

items.title: PM Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Pricing & Sales Growth
items.summary: Philip Morris International (PM) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.36 (up 5.4% YoY) and revenues of $11.44 billion (up 5.5% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. Strong combustible pricing and smoke-free product demand, particularly ZYN in the U.S., drove growth. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.29-$8.44 and maintained its 5-7% organic revenue growth forecast, while also increasing its quarterly dividend by 8.8%.

items.title: DHR Q3 Earnings Beat on Biotechnology Strength, Sales in Line
items.summary: Danaher Corporation reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.11, beating estimates by 9.9%, with revenues of $6.55 billion in line with expectations. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.57-$8.62 and expects 2.5% core revenue growth. Diagnostics segment sales jumped 17% driven by acquisitions, though respiratory testing revenues declined significantly from $500M to $350M year-over-year.

items.title: Is Raymond James Well-Positioned to Sustain Strong Capital Returns?
items.summary: Raymond James Financial (RJF) returned nearly $2 billion to shareholders over the trailing 12 months through dividends and share buybacks, while maintaining strong capital positions to support organic growth and strategic acquisitions. The company announced an 8% dividend increase and repurchased 9.8 million shares, supported by solid earnings growth projections of 13.8% for fiscal 2026 and 17.1% for fiscal 2027. However, regulatory capital requirements and elevated expenses remain risk factors.

items.title: NextEra Energy Q3 Earnings Beat on FPL Strength, Revenues Miss
items.summary: NextEra Energy (NEE) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.24, beating consensus estimates by 3.3%, driven by strong performance from Florida Power & Light and NextEra Energy Resources. The company added 3.7 GW to its renewables backlog and maintained its 2026 EPS guidance of $3.92-$4.02. However, total revenues missed expectations. NEE continues advancing its pending merger with Dominion Energy, expected to close in H2 2027.

items.title: Steel Dynamics: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Steel Dynamics reported record Q3 2026 quarterly steel shipments of 3.8 million tons with mills operating at 92% capacity, significantly outperforming the domestic industry average of 80%. The company resolved aluminum production bottlenecks and is benefiting from strong demand in nonresidential construction and domestic manufacturing reshoring, with fabrication order backlogs up 50% year-over-year. Management expects higher-margin cash generation as new capacity ramps up.

items.title: MMM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Deals and Higher Outlook
items.summary: 3M raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.10-$9.15, driven by strong industrial demand, expanding data center opportunities, and productivity improvements. The company expanded its Amazon partnership targeting $6 billion in cumulative sales over 7 years and achieved 110 basis points of operating margin expansion to 26.2%. However, consumer electronics weakness persists, particularly in LCD displays and Chinese device manufacturers.

items.title: CAT Keeps Dividend Unchanged: Is Another Hike on the Horizon?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) maintained its $1.63 quarterly dividend and returned $7.9 billion to shareholders in H1 2026. The company raised its full-year 2026 sales growth outlook to mid-to-high teens, supported by a record $72 billion backlog and improved business conditions. CAT has increased its dividend for 33 consecutive years and maintains a sustainable dividend profile with a 0.30 dividend-to-free-cash-flow ratio.

items.title: Is it Wise to Retain Public Storage Stock in Your Portfolio Now?
items.summary: Public Storage (PSA) is expanding through strategic acquisitions, including a $1.2 billion Canadian portfolio purchase, and leveraging AI-powered tools to drive growth. However, the company faces challenges from declining same-store revenues (-0.6% YoY), rising interest expenses ($84.8M in Q2), and competitive pressure from peers like Extra Space Storage and CubeSmart. Management expects same-store revenue recovery by Q4, though the pace remains uncertain.

items.title: GE Vernova (GEV) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
items.summary: GE Vernova (GEV) is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings of $4.03 per share with revenues of $12.1 billion on October 28. The company shows a positive Earnings ESP of +5.47% combined with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting a likely earnings beat. However, the company missed estimates significantly in the last quarter with a -22.08% surprise.

items.title: NUE Rides on Expansion Actions, Higher Steel Prices & Acquisitions
items.summary: Nucor Corporation is expanding production capacity with major projects including a 3 million ton per annum sheet mill in West Virginia expected to complete in late 2026. The company projects Q3 2026 earnings of $5.55-$5.65 per share, driven by higher steel prices and volumes. U.S. steel prices have surged above $1,300 per short ton recently, benefiting major producers. Peer steel companies Steel Dynamics, Cleveland-Cliffs, and ArcelorMittal are also reporting strong earnings guidance and improved market conditions.

items.title: NOC's Q3 Earnings Call Highlights 2027 Growth and B-21 Spending
items.summary: Northrop Grumman raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $29.35-$29.75 and projects 5%-7% sales growth in 2027 with expanding margins. The company reported Q3 EPS of $7.89, exceeding expectations, and maintains a record $109.6 billion backlog. Management is investing $2.1 billion in B-21 production capacity while preserving $3.3-$3.7 billion free cash flow outlook, though acknowledges execution risks and timing uncertainties.

items.title: General Motors Q3 Earnings Call Weighs 2027 Cost Risks Against Cash Gains
items.summary: General Motors raised its 2026 automotive free cash flow guidance to $11.5B-$12.5B following Q3 earnings and revenue beats. However, the company warned that sustained commodity inflation could add $1B-$1.5B in EBIT pressure for 2027, potentially complicating earnings growth. GM expects a 35,000-pickup Q4 shortfall due to changeovers and plans flat pickup production in 2027 before growth resumes in 2028. The company is betting on next-generation Silverado and Sierra pickups, expanding software/services revenue, and achieving EV cost reductions to drive future growth.

items.title: Apple vs. Broadcom: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Apple and Broadcom as investment options for 2026. Apple dominates consumer hardware with $416.2B revenue and 26.9% net margin but faces antitrust scrutiny and size constraints. Broadcom leads infrastructure semiconductors with 23.9% revenue growth and 36.2% net margin, benefiting from AI tailwinds. The author favors Broadcom for stronger growth prospects despite Apple's stability, citing Broadcom's superior performance over the past decade.

items.title: Buy 2 Undervalued AI EMS Stocks Amid Massive Short-Term Price Upside
items.summary: Sanmina (SANM) and Jabil (JBL) are positioned as top investment picks in the electronics manufacturing services sector, benefiting from surging AI data center demand. Both companies trade below industry-average P/E multiples and offer significant short-term price upside potential, with SANM expected to grow 18.6% in revenue and JBL projected at 24.1% revenue growth for their respective fiscal years.

items.title: MCO Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Costs Rise & MIS Revenues Fall
items.summary: Moody's reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $4.14 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $4.25, though earnings grew 6% year-over-year. Revenues rose 1% to $2.02B but fell short of expectations. The results were pressured by increased operating expenses and a 1% decline in Moody's Investors Service revenues due to lower leveraged finance issuance, partially offset by 3% growth in Moody's Analytics. The company reaffirmed its 2026 guidance.

items.title: NextEra Energy (NEE) Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates
items.summary: NextEra Energy (NEE) reported quarterly earnings of $1.24 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.20 and surpassing the prior year's $1.13. However, the company missed revenue expectations with $8.09 billion versus the estimated $8.89 billion. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 14.5% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

items.title: Capital One Stock Gains as Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher NII
items.summary: Capital One reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $6.69 per share, beating consensus estimates of $5.45, with a 12% year-over-year increase. Net interest income rose 4% to $12.89 billion and net interest margin expanded 5 basis points to 8.41%. However, the company faced headwinds from higher expenses (up 7%), increased provisions (up 7%), and sequential deposit declines. Credit quality improved with net charge-offs falling 10% year-over-year. Capital One carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: If I Could Only Invest $500 in AI This Month, I'd Buy This 1 Stock.
items.summary: Netlist has secured major patent settlement deals with Samsung and Micron worth $897 million and $600 million respectively over five years, generating nearly $100 million in annual recurring revenue. The company is leveraging these proceeds to scale its AI memory hardware business, with products like CXL NVvault addressing memory bottlenecks in AI systems. With a market cap of $2.1 billion and strong growth momentum, Netlist is positioned similarly to Rambus and could see significant upside from hyperscaler deals and agentic AI adoption.

items.title: Netflix Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Ad Revenue View Trimmed
items.summary: Netflix reported Q3 2026 EPS of 87 cents, up 49% YoY and beating consensus by 6.1%, with operating margin expanding to 34.6%. However, the company trimmed its 2026 ad revenue outlook to $2.7B and free cash flow forecast to $12B due to slower-than-expected ad product rollout. Subscription revenue growth and strong performance in India offset advertising headwinds.

items.title: Capital One: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Capital One reported $1.8 billion in annualized Discover integration synergies, exceeding initial timelines. The company is accelerating debit account conversions and cost reductions while increasing marketing spend to drive customer acquisition across credit cards and national banking. Management is investing heavily in AI and technology to strengthen premium customer relationships and maintain credit discipline.

items.title: Oracle vs. Microsoft: Which Is the Better AI Cloud Stock to Own for the Next 5 Years?
items.summary: Oracle's cloud infrastructure revenue is growing rapidly at 121% year-over-year, but the company faces significant financial strain with negative free cash flow of $5.4 billion and record-high debt insurance costs. Microsoft's cloud business grows more slowly at 43% but maintains strong free cash flow of $20 billion and lower debt levels. While Oracle has greater upside potential if execution succeeds, Microsoft's financial flexibility makes it the better 5-year investment choice due to its ability to weather potential delays in AI infrastructure projects.

items.title: If Alphabet Does This on Oct. 28, the Stock Could Skyrocket
items.summary: Alphabet is expected to report strong Q3 earnings on Oct. 28, with Google Cloud as the key catalyst. Google Cloud's revenue growth accelerated to 82% in Q2, significantly outpacing competitors Microsoft Azure (43%) and Amazon Web Services (37%). The growth is driven by massive AI workload demand and Alphabet's $195-205 billion capital expenditure investment in data centers. items.title: Bloom Energy vs. Vistra: Which Energy Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

items.title: Microsoft vs. Oracle: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Microsoft and Oracle as investment options in 2026. Microsoft is positioned as the safer choice with strong cash flow, low debt (0.1x debt-to-equity), and a 40% net margin, but trades at a premium valuation (27.2x forward P/E). Oracle offers higher growth potential (23% vs 15% expected annual earnings growth) at a more attractive valuation (16.5x forward P/E), but carries higher risk due to significant debt (2.3x debt-to-equity) and negative free cash flow from heavy data center investments. The author ultimately recommends Oracle for its competitive cloud database position and better value relative to growth prospects.

items.title: Interesting News for Netflix Stock Investors
items.summary: Netflix is undergoing a business reconfiguration to align with current market realities. The company's cost-cutting efforts appear to be a restructuring initiative rather than a simple reduction. Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos provided investors with concerning news ahead of earnings announcements.

items.title: Is Applied Digital Stock Stock an Undervalued AI Stock to Buy Right Now?
items.summary: Applied Digital (APLD) faces investor concerns about its large cash needs despite holding $36 billion in contracted revenue. The article examines whether the AI infrastructure stock represents an undervalued buying opportunity or if durability concerns around AI spending warrant caution.

items.title: Innventure, Inc. Stockholders Should Contact Robbins LLP for Information About Recovering Their Losses Before the October 27, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. for allegedly misleading investors about its DarkNX venture with Accelsius. The company claimed a transformative deal to build a 300MW AI data center in Ontario, Canada, but a May 2026 report revealed the project was fabricated with no evidence of DarkNX's existence or capability. Following the disclosure, Innventure's stock plummeted 55% on August 14, 2026, and the company suspended its 2026 revenue targets and removed the DarkNX project from its bookings.

items.title: The Cooper Companies, Inc. Investor News: If You Have Suffered Losses in The Cooper Companies, Inc., You Are Encouraged to Contact The Rosen Law Firm About Your Rights
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is investigating potential securities claims against The Cooper Companies, Inc. (NASDAQ: COO) for allegedly issuing materially misleading business information. The investigation was prompted by Cooper Companies' disappointing earnings report on September 10, 2026, which included weak guidance and a decision not to sell Cooper Surgical, causing the stock to fall 14.6% that day. Investors who purchased Cooper Companies securities may be eligible for compensation through a class action lawsuit.

items.title: GDDY DEADLINE TOMORROW: ROSEN, LEADING INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages GoDaddy Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 20 Deadline in Securities Class Action – GDDY
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against GoDaddy Inc. for allegedly making materially false and misleading statements about customer growth and average order size. The company promoted short-term contracts with smaller valuations that contradicted its public statements, leading to decreased bookings growth. Investors who purchased GoDaddy stock between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The deadline to serve as lead plaintiff is October 20, 2026.

items.title: J.B. Hunt Investor News: If You Have Suffered Losses in J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc., You Are Encouraged to Contact The Rosen Law Firm About Your Rights
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is investigating potential securities claims against J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc. after the company issued a profit warning on September 16, 2026, citing $25 million in additional costs for recruiting, advertising, and training in Q3. The announcement caused J.B. Hunt's stock to plunge 10% intraday. Investors who suffered losses are encouraged to join a prospective class action lawsuit.

items.title: INV DEADLINE: ROSEN, RECOGNIZED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Innventure, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important October 27 Deadline in Securities Class Action - INV
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is urging investors who purchased Innventure, Inc. securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 to secure legal counsel before the October 27, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline. The lawsuit alleges that Innventure made materially false statements regarding Accelsius Holdings' transformative deal with DarkNX, which was unlikely to materialize, resulting in overstated revenue and cash flow targets for 2026.

items.title: Alphabet Stock Slipped After Q2 Earnings. Here's What Investors Need to See in Q3.
items.summary: Alphabet's stock fell 6% after Q2 earnings despite impressive results, including 82% Google Cloud revenue growth, due to investor concerns about massive AI capital expenditure increases ($44.9B in Q2, with full-year guidance raised to $195-205B). Investors are in a 'show-me' phase, demanding tangible evidence of AI investment returns rather than just ambitious spending announcements. For Q3, investors will focus on Google Cloud's ability to sustain momentum and the commercial viability of Alphabet's custom Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chip business.

items.title: Dorchester Minerals, L.P. Announces Agreement to Acquire Mineral and Royalty Interests
items.summary: Dorchester Minerals, L.P. announced on October 19, 2026, that it has entered into an agreement to acquire approximately 4,300 net royalty acres of mineral and royalty interests located in three counties across the Williston Basin in North Dakota. The Partnership will issue 1,250,000 common units in exchange for these interests, with the acquisition expected to close on October 30, 2026.

items.title: Steel Dynamics (STLD) Reports Q3 Earnings: What Key Metrics Have to Say
items.summary: Steel Dynamics reported Q3 2026 revenue of $6.51 billion, up 34.8% year-over-year, beating consensus estimates by 6.6%. However, EPS of $5.26 missed expectations of $5.42 by 2.95%. The company showed strong performance across most operational metrics, with significant growth in steel fabrication, metals recycling, and other segments. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Steel Dynamics (STLD) Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates
items.summary: Steel Dynamics reported Q3 2026 earnings of $5.26 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $5.42, though revenues of $6.51 billion exceeded expectations by 6.60%. The stock has gained 42% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500's 11.9% gain. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, the stock is expected to perform in line with the market. Peer Nucor is expected to report results on October 26 with anticipated earnings of $5.71 per share, representing 117.1% year-over-year growth.

items.summary: XTI Aerospace investors have until October 27, 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status in a securities fraud class action. The lawsuit alleges the company failed to disclose material adverse facts about senior executives' undisclosed activities and governance issues. The stock fell 15.9% on August 18, 2026 after the company announced it could not timely file its quarterly report due to an internal review of its former CEO who resigned that day.

items.title: Deadline Alert: GoDaddy Inc. Investors Have Until October 20, 2026 to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role in Securities Fraud Class Action, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP Reminds
items.summary: A securities fraud class action has been filed against GoDaddy Inc. for allegedly failing to disclose material adverse facts about its business. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased GoDaddy securities between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026. The complaint alleges the company did not disclose that its high-intent customer strategy was failing and that promotional pricing on .com domains was negatively impacting bookings. GoDaddy's stock fell 14.26% on February 25, 2026 when the company disclosed these issues. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 20, 2026.

items.title: Top Stock Picks for Week of October 19, 2026
items.summary: Zacks highlights Target Corporation and SanDisk as compelling investment opportunities. Target benefits from strengthening consumer engagement, diversified revenue streams through Roundel advertising and Circle memberships, and strategic category momentum. SanDisk is capitalizing on AI inference demand and enterprise SSD growth, with impressive fiscal Q4 earnings that beat estimates by 14.63% and revenue surging 371.6% year-over-year. Both stocks are rated as Zacks Rank #1 Strong Buy.

items.title: Dario Amodei Predicted at Davos in January 2025 That AI Could Surpass Humans "at Almost Everything" Within Two to Three Years. With Anthropic Now Filing for a $2 Trillion IPO, Is That Timeline Still on Track?
items.summary: Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI as the leading AI lab, with higher revenue ($16.8B run rate), profitability on an adjusted basis, and an expected IPO in November ahead of OpenAI's delayed 2027 offering. CEO Dario Amodei predicted AI would exceed human capacity by 2027-2028, a timeline that appears on track as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang claims AGI has already arrived with recent breakthroughs like GPT-6 Astra solving long-standing math and computer science problems.

items.title: If You Invest $200 a Month in Coca-Cola (KO) Stock, Here's the Dividend Income It Could Generate Over 10 Years.
items.summary: Coca-Cola is highlighted as a reliable dividend stock for income investors. A $200 monthly investment over 10 years would have grown from $24,000 to nearly $37,800 with over $3,800 in cumulative dividends. The company's scale, diversification, asset-light business model, and 64-year dividend increase streak position it as a dependable long-term investment for the next decade.

items.title: 2 Industries Beyond AI With Long-Term Demand Drivers for 2027
items.summary: As AI dominates investment focus, healthcare and waste management sectors offer alternative diversification opportunities. Healthcare benefits from an aging population and rising medical needs, while waste management provides recurring revenue from essential services. Key companies like Abbott, Johnson & Johnson, Stryker, Waste Management, and Republic Services are positioned to capitalize on these structural trends.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alphabet Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alphabet Inc. alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding Gemini 3.5 Pro's performance. The complaint claims the AI model delivered disappointing training results, leading to significant launch delays, and that management's positive statements about the company's business and prospects lacked a reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Alphabet securities between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026.

items.title: Arista Networks Is Heading for a Big Test on Nov. 3. Here's What Could Send the Stock Soaring.
items.summary: Arista Networks will report Q3 earnings on Nov. 3, but the key focus should be on Q4 guidance. The AI networking equipment supplier is expected to beat Wall Street's Q4 targets of $3.6B revenue and $1.15 EPS. Strong forward guidance would signal sustained demand for Arista's high-speed networking switches used in AI data centers, potentially driving the stock higher.

items.title: CME vs. Coinbase Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: CME Group and Coinbase Global represent two different approaches to financial infrastructure. CME operates a high-margin derivatives marketplace with a 62% net margin and strong cash generation, while Coinbase scales rapidly in crypto trading but faces regulatory uncertainty. The author recommends CME due to its superior profitability, lower valuation multiple, dividend payment, and skepticism about crypto's fundamental value.

items.title: APA (APA) is a Great Momentum Stock: Should You Buy?
items.summary: Apache Corporation (APA) is highlighted as a strong momentum pick with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and Momentum Style Score of B. items.summary: Microsoft canceled a U.K. AI data center lease due to power unavailability until the 2030s, highlighting infrastructure bottlenecks in AI expansion. This underscores risks in AI IPOs relying on future revenue projections. Markets fell last week amid sticky inflation concerns, with the Fed potentially raising rates again. Multiple major tech companies report earnings this week, including Netflix, Meta, and Tesla, while Cisco continues gaining momentum as a key AI infrastructure player.

items.title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock Has the Most Upside Through 2030.
items.summary: The article argues that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) offers better long-term AI investment potential than Nvidia and Micron through 2030. While Nvidia faces competition from custom chips developed by hyperscalers and Micron faces cyclical memory market pressures, TSMC benefits from its foundry position serving all chip architectures. TSMC's Q3 earnings showed 41% YoY revenue growth with 66.4% gross margins, positioning it to capitalize on the broader evolution of AI workloads beyond just training models.

items.title: DD Gains on Innovation, Productivity and Strategic Acquisitions
items.summary: DuPont delivered 4% organic sales growth in Q2 2026 driven by high-growth markets including healthcare, water, aerospace, and EVs. The company raised its full-year 2026 EBITDA and earnings guidance following acquisitions of Spectrum Plastics and Donatelle Plastics, and is targeting 3% productivity gains. Peer chemical companies Dow, Air Products, and Eastman Chemical also raised their 2026 guidance.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Greg Abel Just Took a Page Out of Warren Buffett's Playbook, Plowing $930 Million Into a 'Wonderful Company at a Fair Price'
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Greg Abel has invested $930 million in Bending Spoons, a digital business roll-up company, following Warren Buffett's philosophy of buying wonderful companies at fair prices. Berkshire invested $600 million in Bending Spoons' IPO in July and an additional $330 million recently, bringing its stake to about 4%. The company has acquired 50 businesses including AOL, Eventbrite, and Vimeo, with strong Q2 results showing 126% revenue growth and 163% EPS growth. However, the stock now trades at $54.50 (up from $29-$33 IPO price) at a valuation of 39x forward earnings, making it less of a bargain despite solid fundamentals.

items.title: M&T Bank: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: M&T Bank reported 17% year-to-date growth in net operating earnings per share in Q3 2026. The bank transferred $8.3 billion in mortgage-backed securities to held-to-maturity status to protect capital from regulatory changes, reduced wholesale borrowings by $2.8 billion through deposit growth, and maintains strict underwriting standards over aggressive loan pricing. Management remains optimistic about net interest income and margin outlook.

items.title: Morgan Stanley: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reported Q3 2026 earnings with $20.3 billion in firmwide revenue and $10.5 trillion in client assets. The company highlighted three key strengths: a durable asset growth funnel from its E*TRADE acquisition that added $2 trillion in net new assets over six years, strategic positioning in AI advisory services with $1 trillion in annual hyperscaler capital expenditure, and a strong balance sheet with 300 basis points of excess regulatory capital providing operational flexibility.

items.title: Fifth Third Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on NII & Fee Income Growth
items.summary: Fifth Third Bancorp reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.13, beating estimates of $1.09, driven by strong net interest income growth of 49% year-over-year following the Comerica acquisition and solid fee income growth of 29%. However, non-interest expenses surged 62% year-over-year, and capital ratios weakened. The company provided Q4 guidance expecting continued modest loan and NII growth.

items.title: Cincinnati Financial (CINF) Expected to Beat Earnings Estimates: Should You Buy?
items.summary: Cincinnati Financial is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings of $2.01 per share (down 29.5% YoY) with revenues of $3.03 billion (up 5.5% YoY) on October 26. The company has a positive Earnings ESP of +13.87% combined with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), suggesting a likely earnings beat. However, the company missed estimates significantly in the last quarter (-21.43% surprise).

items.title: Can WDAY's New AI Offerings Across Business Functions Drive Growth?
items.summary: Workday has introduced Decision Intelligence, an AI-powered platform that helps HR and finance teams make faster, more informed decisions by unifying workforce and financial data. The solution enables real-time analysis of costs, risks, margins, and forecasts while reducing reliance on spreadsheets. Unity Technologies has already reported benefits from using the platform for revenue variance investigation and financial reporting.

items.title: Here's How Tempus AI Demonstrates Improving Operating Leverage
items.summary: Tempus AI demonstrated improving operating leverage in Q2 2026 with 22% revenue growth to $382.5M and adjusted EBITDA reaching $8M (a $13.6M improvement). The company completed a $460M convertible notes offering expected to reduce annual interest expenses by over $30M. Tempus raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $1.595-$1.605B while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance of $65M, supporting its goal of achieving positive free cash flow by year-end 2026.

items.title: Is GE Aerospace (GE) Stock Outpacing Its Aerospace Peers This Year?
items.summary: GE Aerospace is outperforming its Aerospace peers with a year-to-date gain of 1.9% compared to the sector's average loss of 12.2%. items.title: AbbVie's Neuroscience Franchise: What to Expect Ahead of Q3 Results
items.summary: AbbVie's neuroscience revenues are projected to reach $3.29 billion in Q3 2026, representing approximately 16% year-over-year growth. Key contributors include established drugs Vraylar ($1.08B) and Botox Therapeutic ($1.07B), along with newer products like Vyalev ($283M) and the recently FDA-approved Juvmo. The company faces competition from Biogen and Johnson & Johnson in the neuroscience market.

items.title: APLD's Interest Costs Surge: Can AI Growth Restore Profitability?
items.summary: Applied Digital (APLD) is struggling with profitability despite 322% revenue growth to $341.9M in Q1 FY27, as interest expenses surged 866% to $77.4M and the company posted a $221M net loss. With $6.4B in debt and $2.16B in future interest payments, APLD must balance aggressive infrastructure investments with financing costs. Peers CoreWeave and Core Scientific face similar challenges converting strong AI demand into sustainable profitability.

items.title: Can Ad-Supported Streaming Momentum Boost Netflix's Q3 Results?
items.summary: Netflix is projected to report Q3 2026 revenues of $12.86 billion (12% YoY growth) with a 33.2% operating margin. Ad revenues are expected to double to $3 billion in 2026, driven by strong U.S. Upfront commitments and expanded programmatic access. However, sluggish 2% first-half view hour growth, intense competition, and delayed EMEA ad-tier expansion (March 2027) limit near-term upside. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Can HPQ Protect Margins Amid Rising Memory & Storage Costs?
items.summary: HP Inc. reported a 60 basis point decline in non-GAAP operating margin to 6.5% in fiscal Q3 2026 due to rising memory and storage costs impacting its Personal Systems business. The company is implementing a four-pillar strategy including supply security, demand shaping, cost reductions, and disciplined pricing. Personal Systems margins are expected to bottom in Q4 fiscal 2026 before improving in fiscal 2027. HP trades at a discount valuation with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating.

items.title: Prediction: Microsoft Stock Is Going to Soar After Oct. 28
items.summary: Microsoft is expected to report strong Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings on Oct. 28, with focus on Azure cloud platform and Copilot AI assistant growth. items.title: Is iShares U.S. Infrastructure ETF (IFRA) a Strong ETF Right Now?
items.summary: IFRA is a smart beta ETF launched in 2018 that tracks the NYSE FactSet U.S. Infrastructure Index with over $4 billion in assets. Managed by BlackRock, it offers low expenses at 0.30% and focuses on U.S. companies with infrastructure exposure. The fund has performed well year-to-date with a 9.59% gain and maintains a 1.79% dividend yield, with top holdings including Caterpillar, Quanta Services, and Union Pacific.

items.title: Not So Fast! One Warren Buffett's Core Positions at Berkshire Hathaway May Not Get the Heave-Ho by Successor Greg Abel After All.

Recent catalysts including BofA's improved valuation (30% premium to book value vs. 65% premium in August) and the Federal Reserve's new rate-hiking cycle have made the interest-sensitive bank more attractive again, potentially keeping it as a core holding under CEO Greg Abel.

items.title: If You Invested $100 a Month in This High-Yield Dividend Stock, Here's the Dividend Income It Produced Over 10 Years
items.summary: Altria Group (MO), the largest U.S. tobacco company, demonstrated strong dividend performance over the past decade. A $100 monthly investment ($12,000 principal) generated approximately $4,800 in dividends while growing to $13,800. With a 5.9% forward dividend yield and 57 consecutive years of annual dividend increases (Dividend King status), Altria maintains a cheap valuation at 13x forward earnings. The company offsets declining smoking rates through price increases, cost cuts, share buybacks, and expansion into smoke-free products, with expectations to generate $5 billion in smoke-free revenue by 2028.

items.title: The Trillion-Dollar AI Bet: What It Means for Hyperscaler Investors
items.summary: The five major hyperscalers (Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta Platforms, and Oracle) are projected to spend nearly $780 billion on AI capital expenditures in 2026, escalating to over $1 trillion annually from 2027-2030. While this massive investment presents significant financial risks—including soaring debt levels and negative free cash flow—the long-term payoff remains uncertain. Success requires the AI economy to generate $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031, with most value potentially shifting away from hyperscalers toward companies offering differentiated end-customer products.

items.summary: ServiceNow and Workday both demonstrate steady revenue growth in their enterprise software businesses, but ServiceNow is pulling ahead with faster expansion. items.title: BNY Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and AI Push

The company beat earnings estimates with $5.68B in revenue and $2.37 EPS, while expanding digital asset capabilities and maintaining disciplined capital allocation.

items.title: Starbucks Stock Gains 15% YTD: Can Its Turnaround Drive More Upside?
items.summary: Starbucks delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of positive comparable-store sales growth at 7.9%, with operating margins expanding 430 basis points to 14.4% and EPS increasing 70% to 85 cents. The company raised fiscal 2026 guidance, supported by improved customer traffic, menu innovation, and the revamped Rewards program. However, coffee cost pressures, potential store closures, and execution risks remain concerns.

items.title: Are Investors Undervaluing Occidental Petroleum (OXY) Right Now?
items.summary: Occidental Petroleum (OXY) is identified as an attractive value stock investment, holding a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating and an 'A' Value grade. The company's valuation metrics, including P/B ratio of 1.63, P/S ratio of 2.37, and P/CF ratio of 4.59, are all favorable compared to industry averages, suggesting the stock is undervalued with strong earnings outlook.

items.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights S&P Global, CME, Intercontinental Exchange, Nasdaq and Cboe Global Markets
items.summary: Zacks analyzes five securities exchange stocks amid industry headwinds. While diversified revenue streams, higher trading volumes, and technology investments support growth, the Securities and Exchanges industry faces challenges from regulatory changes, cybersecurity threats, and competition. The industry ranks #166 out of 247 Zacks industries with negative earnings outlook, having underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date. Five Hold-rated stocks are highlighted for consideration.

items.title: La Rosa Holdings Corp. to Change Its Name to Stratum Holdings Corp., Reflecting Its Transformation into an AI Infrastructure Company
items.summary: La Rosa Holdings Corp. is rebranding to Stratum Holdings Corp. effective October 19, 2026, with its stock ticker changing to SRTM on Nasdaq. The company is pivoting from real estate services to AI infrastructure, focusing on GPU leasing and high-performance compute after acquiring next-generation NVIDIA B300 GPUs under a long-term lease expected to generate recurring revenue.

items.title: FIS Stock Down Nearly 48% From 52-Week High: Is a Rebound Ahead?
items.summary: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) has declined 48% from its 52-week high amid growth concerns, but improving cash flow and margin expansion offer recovery prospects. Second-quarter free cash flow surged 220% to $525 million, and the Global Payments Issuer Solutions acquisition is expected to add $700 million in free cash flow by 2028. However, lowered 2026 guidance for revenue growth (4.5-5%) and EBITDA growth (5.9-6.9%) highlight ongoing execution challenges. Recovery depends on translating integration benefits into sustainable margin gains and debt reduction rather than rapid revenue acceleration.

items.title: Truist Financial Corporation (TFC) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Miss Estimates
items.summary: Truist Financial reported Q3 earnings of $1.16 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $1.17, and revenues of $5.19 billion, falling short of expectations by 2.19%. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 18.5% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. The company's industry, Banks - Major Regional, ranks in the bottom 33% of Zacks industries.

items.title: Citizens Financial Group (CFG) Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates
items.summary: Citizens Financial Group reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.41 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.38, with a 2.17% earnings surprise. However, revenues of $2.32 billion slightly missed expectations. The stock has gained 8.6% year-to-date, underperforming the S&P 500's 13.1% gain. The company received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

items.title: Better AI Stock: SpaceX vs. Nvidia
items.summary: Nvidia and SpaceX are compared as AI investment options. Nvidia, valued at $5.5 trillion, is a hardware play providing GPUs for AI workloads, while SpaceX, valued at $2 trillion, is an application play through its xAI subsidiary producing the Grok AI model. Despite SpaceX's faster growth, Nvidia is recommended as the better AI stock due to its established market dominance, doubling revenue, and significantly cheaper valuation relative to revenue.

items.title: This Dividend King Is Getting In on the AI Energy Boom With Its Recent Deal with Google. Is It a Buy?
items.summary: Black Hills, a Dividend King with 56 years of consecutive dividend growth, signed a long-term agreement with Google to supply 2.7 gigawatts of power to its Wyoming data center campus through 2048. The deal is projected to generate $150 million in annual net income by 2030, significantly boosting the utility's position as Wyoming emerges as a major AI data center hub with investments from Microsoft, Meta, and Alphabet.

items.title: Billionaires Are Selling These 6 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks. Should You Follow?
items.summary: Several billionaire investors sold major AI stocks in Q2, including Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet, citing concerns about AI infrastructure returns and valuations. However, the article advises against simply following these sales, recommending a company-by-company evaluation. Amazon and Apple are highlighted as top picks due to AWS growth and Apple's lower capex exposure to AI, while Tesla is flagged as overvalued given its unproven autonomous technology.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has Over 45% of Berkshire Hathaway's $356 Billion Portfolio Invested in 3 Undeniable Winners
items.summary: Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, has maintained the company's portfolio concentration strategy with over 45% ($160.6 billion) of invested assets in three major holdings: Apple ($76.73 billion), American Express ($46.72 billion), and Alphabet ($37.17 billion). While Buffett sold 75% of Apple before retirement, Abel views it as a long-term compounder. Abel has significantly increased Berkshire's Alphabet stake, tripling it in Q1 and adding $17 billion in Q2, attracted by Google's search dominance and AI ambitions in Google Cloud.

items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Just Shared Bad News for Nvidia and Great News for This Rival Chipmaker
items.summary: Microsoft plans to significantly expand its custom-designed Maia chips in Azure data centers starting next year, reducing reliance on Nvidia GPUs. The company will make Maia 300 chips its primary inference system for its products and services. This shift benefits Marvell Technology, which partners on the Maia chips, while pressuring Nvidia as major cloud providers develop custom AI accelerator alternatives.

items.title: Buy 5 Top-Ranked Non-Tech Nasdaq Stocks to Maximize Q4 Gains
items.summary: Despite the Nasdaq's tech-heavy composition, five non-tech Nasdaq-listed stocks with Zacks Rank #1 ratings are positioned for strong growth. Ross Stores plans 115 store openings with 13% Q2 sales growth, Roku's advertising revenue climbed 24.8%, APA Corp benefits from cost savings and long-term growth projects, Corcept Therapeutics sees strong drug demand with recent FDA approvals, and Halozyme generates royalties from pharma collaborations.

items.title: Sandisk Stock Could Be Worth $4,128 in the Next Year
items.summary: Sandisk stock has surged 497% year-to-date and could nearly triple to $4,128 over the next year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and data center storage growth. The company reported 51% quarter-over-quarter revenue growth to $9 billion, with CEO David Goeckeler stating the company is still in early innings of growth. Long-term customer agreements covering over half of fiscal 2027 bits shipped provide revenue visibility, though cyclical pricing risks remain.
